title: Desktop: write log records to standard error and a rotating log file
author: switch87
body:
## Why

The desktop app never installs a logger (only the web build does, via `WebLogger`), so every `log::warn!` / `log::error!` in the workspace is discarded, and the control server's messages only reach `eprintln!`. A launch from a desktop menu or the Dock has no terminal, so an ordinary user has nothing to attach to an issue, and `RUST_LOG` can't help them.

We ran into this in the sister project PhotoCraft (storytold/photocraft#1143): a window that stayed empty on Linux took an hour of `WAYLAND_DEBUG` and `gdb` to understand, while the app had already logged the relevant decision to nowhere.

## What

`apps/cadcraft/src/logging.rs`, no new dependency (just `log`):

- **Two sinks:** standard error and `<settings dir>/logs/cadcraft.log`. CADCraft had no per-user directory yet, so this adds `config_dir()` in the same style as the sister apps: `CADCRAFT_CONFIG_DIR` (empty = unset), else Linux/BSD `$XDG_CONFIG_HOME/cadcraft` or `~/.config/cadcraft` (a relative `XDG_CONFIG_HOME` is ignored, per the XDG spec), macOS `~/Library/Application Support/CADCraft`, Windows `%APPDATA%\CADCraft`.
- **Rotation:** each launch moves the previous log to `cadcraft.1.log` (and that one to `.2`), so the log of a run that crashed survives the next start.
- **Bounded:** the file stops at 16 MiB with one note; records logged before the file is attached are buffered (max 512, with a "N earlier lines dropped" note); without a usable directory the buffer is released (`stderr_only`).
- **Levels:** `info` for `cadcraft*` targets, `warn` for everything else. `RUST_LOG` replaces this with env_logger-style directives; a trailing `*` matches a prefix.
- **Never crash:** no `unwrap`/`expect`/indexing; an unusable directory or a failed write keeps standard error only; lock poisoning is handled.

`main.rs`: the logger is installed first; the file is attached after argument parsing so `--version` creates nothing. A `--control` / `CADCRAFT_CONTROL_PORT` value that is not a port number is now logged in…

title: macOS DMG: branded window background and icon layout
author: XusBadia
body:
## What

The macOS DMG opened as a plain white Finder window. It now opens like this:

![CADCraft DMG window in Finder](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/XusBadia/cadcraft/dmg-preview/finder.png)

The icon's figure as a cover on the CADCraft colour field, CADCraft.app and the `Applications` link side by side on Paper, and a small CADCraft-specific touch: the arrow and the mono line under the title come from the app's craft. Ink, Paper and the app colour only; Inter and JetBrains Mono.

## How

Same approach as PhotoCraft's and VectorCraft's, which have landed (storytold/photocraft#1201, storytold/vectorcraft#493):

- `packaging/macos/dmg/background.svg`: the source. Its text is outlined, so rendering it needs no fonts, and the figure is an `<image>` of the existing icon in `assets/app-icon/`.
- `background.tiff`: 1x 660×400 + 2x 1320×800 in one HiDPI TIFF (16-colour palette, Deflate, sRGB; 21 KB). No paper grain: noise doesn't compress, and this keeps the binary small.
- `dmg-layout.DS_Store`: Finder's view settings (window 660×400 content, icon size 128, CADCraft.app at (326, 205), Applications at (574, 205), the background). It's named so it isn't mistaken for, or ignored like, a Finder-generated `.DS_Store`.
- `generate.py`: writes both from the SVG on any OS (`pip install 'pillow>=12' ds_store==1.3.3 mac_alias==2.2.3`, resvg on PATH). The output is byte-for-byte reproducible and carries nothing from the machine that ran it: no paths, users, disk names or volume UUIDs.
- `package.sh` copies the TIFF and the layout into the staging folder. The image is still built with `hdiutil makehybrid`, and nothing extra runs in the signing job.

## One behaviour change: the volume name drops the version

`.DS_Store` points at the background through an alias that includes the volume name. With `CADCraft <version>` Finder kept the window and icon positions but lost the background (tested). So the mounted volume is now called `CADCraft`; the DMG file name still carries the versi…

title: DIMANGULAR: accept polyline segments (fixes #10)
author: SBaksa
body:
Fixes #10.

## Problem
DIMANGULAR only accepted LINE and ARC entities. Picking a side of a rectangle (RECTANG) or a PLINE segment was rejected with "Select a line or an arc." and the command stayed at the first prompt. Plain LINE objects worked, which is why this looked like "lines can't be selected".

## Fix
A small helper, `segment_at`, resolves the picked object to the segment under the cursor. Straight polyline segments are treated as lines, and polyline arc segments as arcs. The LINE and ARC paths are unchanged.

## Testing
- New regression test `interactive_angular_picks_polyline_segments`: rectangle corner → 90°, polyline arc segment → 180°. It fails before the fix and passes after.
- `cargo xtask ci` passes (fmt, clippy, test, assets, layers, wasm).
- Checked in the desktop app: RECTANG, then DIMANGULAR, clicking two sides places a 90° dimension.

## Not in this PR
- Picking a circle is still rejected, even though the prompt lists "circle". That needs a different prompt sequence, so I'd do it as a follow-up.
- A dimension on polyline segments isn't associative (it doesn't follow later edits to the polyline). Dimensions on LINE entities still are.

title: Redraw edits made while a command is still running (fixes #4)
author: SBaksa
body:
Fixes #4.

## Problem
LINE and PLINE add geometry on every point, but only the first segment appeared until the command ended. The canvas rebuilds its display list when `(revision, doc pointer)` changes. The revision was only bumped when a command finished, and the doc pointer only changes on the first copy-on-write edit, so later edits during the same command were never redrawn.

## Fix
`Session::feed` bumps the revision after each input once the running command has changed the drawing (`!Arc::ptr_eq(&run.before, &st.doc)`). This covers LINE, PLINE and any other interactive command that edits while running. Undo is unchanged: the whole command is still one undo step.

## Testing
- New test `edits_while_a_command_runs_redraw`: the canvas key changes after every LINE segment and PLINE vertex. It fails before the fix ("segment to 10,5 not redrawn") and passes after.
- `cargo xtask ci` passes (fmt, clippy, test, assets, layers, wasm).
- Checked in the desktop app: LINE and PLINE show every finished segment while still running.

## Cost, and an optional follow-up
Each input during a command that has edited the drawing now rebuilds the display list (clicks only, not mouse moves). That's the same rebuild that already happens when any command finishes. `cadcraft-cli perf 200000` (release) measures it at about 220 ms on a 200k-entity drawing. Normal drawings take a few milliseconds, but very large ones would hitch on each click inside LINE.

If that matters, a follow-up could avoid the rebuild entirely:
- Keep the display list built at command start.
- Draw entities *created* during the command as an overlay, the way the rubber band is drawn. They aren't in the cached list, and `DPrim` already carries its handle.
- Fall back to a full rebuild only when the command changes an entity that existed before it started. The chunked `EntityStore` makes that check cheap.

LINE and PLINE only create new entities, so they would never rebuild. The overlay would need checking to make su…

title: Print and Ctrl+P ask where to save the PDF (#5)
author: MarekSpodBiedry
body:
Fixes #5.

Ctrl+P and the Print toolbar button seemed to do nothing. Without a path, PLOT built the PDF in memory and then dropped it, and Ctrl+P was shown in the menu but not bound.

Now PLOT/PRINT/EXPORTPDF started from the menu, the toolbar, Ctrl+P or the command line open the save dialog with "<drawing>.pdf" as the suggested name and write the PDF to the chosen path. Cancelling does nothing. The Save dialog has a PDF filter and puts the filter matching the suggested name first. JSON calls from scripts, the control channel and MCP still never open a dialog.

Tests in crates/ui-egui/src/menus.rs:
- `print_asks_where_to_save_the_pdf` checks that start/cmdline ask for "Drawing1.pdf" and write the file, and that a JSON call does not ask.
- `cancelled_print_writes_nothing` checks the cancel path.

title: SCALE: Reference option (#17)
author: MarekSpodBiedry
body:
Fixes #17.

SCALE > Reference only printed "Reference: not available yet". You could not scale an object from a known length to a target length, for example 56 to 100.

Now Reference asks for the reference length and then the new length, and scales by new / reference. Each length can be typed. The reference can also be picked as two points, and the new length as one point measured from the base point. Lengths that are zero, negative or not finite are rejected and asked again. ROTATE Reference still shows "not available yet".

Tested by `scale_reference_typed_and_picked` in crates/engine/src/tests.rs. It covers typed lengths (56 to 100), a reference picked as two points with the new length picked as a point, and rejection of a zero new length and a zero reference length.

title: Blocks window: click a block to insert it (#8)
author: MarekSpodBiedry
body:
Fixes #8.

The Blocks window listed block names, but you could not do anything with them.

Each name is now a button. Clicking it starts INSERT with that block name already entered, so the command line goes on to ask for the insertion point. If a command is already running, it is cancelled first, the same as when you type a command. If the block cannot be found, INSERT stays at the block name prompt and shows the usual "not found" message.

Tests: two unit tests in `crates/ui-egui/src/dialogs.rs`. The first clicks a block named "Door 2" while LINE is running and inserts it at 5,6. The second clicks a block that does not exist and checks that INSERT still asks for a block name.

title: Default Windows startup to DirectX 12
author: DWAA1660
body:
No CADCraft issue reports this yet. This is a preventive fix for the same Windows startup crash.

Same fix as storytold/designcraft#168, applied to CADCraft. FilmCraft has the same change for storytold/filmcraft#179.
Fixes #33 
## Problem

CADCraft's desktop app uses eframe's default wgpu instance, which enables `PRIMARY | GL` on Windows. Creating the OpenGL backend can crash inside AMD's OpenGL driver (`atio6axx.dll`) before adapter selection or any Rust error handling runs. The app then flashes in Task Manager and exits with no window and no error (storytold/designcraft#167, storytold/filmcraft#179, storytold/filmcraft#268). `WGPU_BACKEND=dx12` was the verified workaround.

## Change

- New `apps/cadcraft/src/graphics.rs`: when no `WGPU_BACKEND` is set, the Windows wgpu instance enables only DirectX 12 before it is created, so OpenGL is never initialized as a fallback. Picking an adapter afterwards would be too late.
- `main.rs` applies it on Windows only. An explicit `WGPU_BACKEND` is still honoured, and the process environment is not changed.
- macOS, Linux and the web build are unchanged.
- README: a short Windows troubleshooting note on the default and the `WGPU_BACKEND` override.

## Validation

- `cargo test -p cadcraft graphics`: 2 passed. `windows_default_initializes_only_dx12` asserts that eframe's default includes GL and that the configured instance is DX12 only. `explicit_backend_override_is_preserved` covers overrides.
- `cargo clippy -p cadcraft --all-targets -- -D warnings` (Linux): clean. `rustfmt --check` on the changed files: clean.
- `cargo clippy -p cadcraft --target x86_64-pc-windows-gnu -- -D warnings`: clean, so the Windows-only call site compiles.
- Limitation: no Windows/AMD hardware here, so the driver crash itself was not reproduced. The DX12 workaround comes from the designcraft report.

title: Render tests: drop the always-true assert in degenerate_input
author: kaffeochknivar
body:
## Summary

`cargo xtask ci` fails at the clippy step on current stable Rust (1.96.1):

```
error: this boolean expression contains a logic bug
   --> crates/render/src/fill.rs:121:17
    |
121 |         assert!(triangulate_evenodd(&[vec![Vec2::new(f64::NAN, 0.0), Vec2::X, Vec2::Y]]).is_empty() || true);
    = note: `#[deny(clippy::overly_complex_bool_expr)]` on by default
```

`... || true` is always true, so the assert only proved that NaN input doesn't panic. This change calls the function and discards the result, with a comment that says so. The test keeps its purpose.

The release workflows use `dtolnay/rust-toolchain@stable`, so anyone running the gate on a fresh toolchain hits this before their own changes are checked.

## Test plan

- [x] `cargo xtask ci` on this branch: all 6 steps pass (fmt, clippy, test, assets, layers, wasm)

title: UNITS opens a Drawing Units dialog; SETVAR prompts at the command line (fixes #30)
author: kaffeochknivar
body:
Fixes #30.

> Builds on #37 (clippy fix needed for `cargo xtask ci` to pass), so this diff includes that one-line commit until #37 merges.

## The problem

Both parts of the issue come from the same gap: neither `UNITS` nor `SETVAR` had an interactive form.

- **UNITS:** when typed, it ran the JSON form with no parameters. That changes nothing and echoes nothing, so it looked like nothing happened.
- **SETVAR:** `SETVAR LUNITS 2` ran `setvar` right away with no `name`. That failed, nothing was left running, and `LUNITS 2` was dropped. Space acting as Enter is intended AutoCAD behavior and was not the cause.

## Changes

**UNITS → Drawing Units dialog** (`ui-egui/dialogs.rs`, `menus.rs`)
- Typed or menu-invoked `UNITS`/`UN` (no parameters) opens the dialog, the same way `QSELECT` and `PARAMETERS` do.
- The dialog has length type and precision, angle type and precision, insertion units (INSUNITS 0–24, names from the DXF Reference), and a sample output. The precision lists show each choice formatted with `units::format_distance`/`format_angle`.
- OK applies the values through the existing `units` command (`app.run`). Cancel or close discards them.
- JSON calls (control channel, MCP, `units {..}`) run the command as before and never open the dialog.

**SETVAR prompts** (`engine/cmd/settings.rs`)
- `Enter variable name or [?]:` is followed by `Enter new value for NAME <current>:`.
- `?` lists the variables.
- Unknown names end the command without creating a header variable.
- Read-only names show their value.
- A value of the wrong type echoes the error and re-prompts.
- Space submits at both prompts, so `SETVAR LUNITS 2` works on one line, in scripts too.

**`sysvars::set` hardening** (`engine/sysvars.rs`)
- Refuses variables that `get` derives from state and `set` can't change: `CMDNAMES`, `DWGNAME`, `DBMOD`, `CTAB`, `LASTPOINT`, `VIEWCTR`, `VIEWSIZE`, `EXTMIN`, `EXTMAX`. Before, these were silently written into the header and had no effect.
- Keeps integer header vari…

title: Smoke sweep over every command, with time/token/model metrics per run
author: Florin-Di
body:
cadcraft-cli smoke runs the whole registry headlessly. Each command gets a fresh
sample-drawing session: first execute() with null params, then, for the 133 that
have a prompt machine, a drive off Prompt::accept with canned points, picks,
numbers and text, finished the way a user does — Enter, then Escape. LINE and
PLINE prompt for ever on purpose, so a machine that doesn't stop by itself is
fine; one that ignores both Enter and Escape is not, and that is what gets
flagged. Results land in results.jsonl, summary.json and report.md.

First sweep: 291 of 295 commands, 428 results, 249 pass, 175 expected_error,
0 fail, 4 skip. No panics, every prompt machine exits. The 175 are commands
called with null params, so their bodies never ran — parameterised calls are
the next step. autoconstrain and boundary are the only two over 20 ms.

cargo xtask smoke wraps the sweep and logs what the run cost: wall-clock,
tokens per model, main agent vs subagents, tool calls, read out of the local
Claude Code transcripts (counters only). Runs go to target/smoke/<id>/, one
line per run into smoke/ledger.jsonl, LEDGER.md regenerated from it.

Menus, toolbar and mouse are not touched yet. results.jsonl carries a transport
field for when the sweep drives a running app over the control channel instead.

open, qsave, saveas and wblock are skipped: they write wherever the caller says.
ROADMAP and docs/parity.md now say 295 registered commands, not 290.

Metrics for this change, out of the ledger it adds:

The worker subagent that wrote the sweep module: claude-opus-5, effort high,
71 replies, 74 tool calls (Bash 51, Edit 12, PowerShell 6, Read 3, Write 2),
15:25:45Z to 15:47:37Z, 21m 52s. 173,484 fresh tokens is the cost figure;
7.64M of its 7.81M raw total is cache reads of the same prompt prefix re-sent
on each of those 71 turns, billed at a fraction of input rate. The task runner
reported 175,280.

Main agent 89 replies / 12.75M total against the worker's 71 / 7.81M, so the
worker was rough…

title: Scripts: split a line at keyword prompts so POLYGON 6 200,20 I 15 works (#43)
author: MarekSpodBiedry
body:
Fixes #43

In a script, a prompt that accepts text sent the whole rest of the line to the command as one string. At POLYGON's "Inscribed/Circumscribed" prompt, `I 15` was taken as one value, matched no keyword, and nothing was drawn.

Now a script line is sent as a whole string only when the text prompt has no keywords (TEXT content, attribute values, leader text and similar stay unchanged). At prompts with keywords the line is split on spaces, like typed input.

Test: `script_splits_line_at_keyword_prompt` runs `POLYGON 6 200,20 I 15` and expects one Polyline.

title: Layer Properties Manager: stop the window growing every frame (fixes #29)
author: LloydNicholson
body:
Fixes #29.

## Cause
In the Layer Properties Manager, the vertical `ui.separator()` between the filter tree and the table sits in a `horizontal_top` row with no height limit. A vertical separator takes all the height it is offered, and a resizable `egui::Window` offers its previous height, so the window grew 30px every frame until the screen clamped it. Just opening the dialog was enough to trigger it, and the footer ("All: N layer(s) displayed…") ended up off-screen.

## Fix
`ui.set_max_height(avail)` caps that row at the table's existing fixed height of 330px. The change is one line plus a comment.

## Evidence
- **New test** `layers::tests::dialog_keeps_its_height` runs the dialog headless for 30 frames on a 1600×1000 screen with the sample drawing and checks that the window height stays constant.
  - Without the fix it fails: `[436.0, 470.0, 500.0, 530.0, … 980.0, 1010.0, 1030.0, 1030.0, …]`
  - With the fix it passes.
- **Real app** (Linux, KDE Wayland, `--sample --control`, dialog opened via `ui.menu.invoke ui.dialog.layers`):
  - Before the fix, the window filled the full 1000px screen height within a second.
  - After the fix, it is still about 450px tall 10 seconds later and the footer is visible.
- **Checks run:** `cargo fmt --check`, `cargo clippy --workspace --all-targets -D warnings` and `cargo test -p cadcraft-ui-egui` (13 passed) all pass.
- **Not run locally:** the wasm step of `xtask ci`, because my distro's Rust lacks the wasm32 target. I'm relying on CI for it.

## Disclosure
I made this change with help from Claude Code (Anthropic). It helped diagnose the bug, write the test and make the fix. I reviewed the change and checked the evidence above myself.

title: Ask to save unsaved changes before closing the window (#34)
author: LloydNicholson
body:
Part of #34. This covers "when closing window doesnt ask for saving the changes". The issue's other points (DWG blocks, the selection cursor, hatch persistence, remembering the last selection option) are separate and not touched here.

## What changed
If any drawing has unsaved changes, closing the window, **File ▸ Exit** or **Cmd/Ctrl+Q** now cancels the close and asks:

> Save changes to "Bracket"? Your changes will be lost if you don't save them.  [Don't Save] [Cancel] [Save]

With several unsaved drawings, it says "N drawings".

- **Save** saves every changed drawing through `qsave`, which falls back to Save As for a drawing that has no file yet. The window only closes if every drawing saved. If the user cancels the file picker or a save fails, the window stays open and the error shows in the status bar.
- **Don't Save** closes the window.
- **Cancel** (or Esc) keeps the window open.
- With no unsaved changes, the window closes immediately, as before.
- The control channel's `app.quit` still quits without a dialog ("programmatic calls never open dialogs").

The pattern mirrors DeckCraft's quit dialog: a `quit_confirmed` flag, `CancelClose` on `close_requested`, and a `save_all` helper. `quit_requested` is now taken one-shot in `main.rs`, so a cancelled quit doesn't re-send `Close` every frame.

Closing a single drawing tab still doesn't ask. That would be a natural follow-up, but I kept this PR to the window close.

## Evidence
- **New tests** in `crates/ui-egui/src/dialogs.rs`:
  - `closing_with_unsaved_changes_asks_first` sends a close request for a clean drawing (it closes), then a dirty one (the close is cancelled and the dialog opens), then a dirty one after the user confirmed (it closes). Before the fix it failed with "unsaved changes must cancel the close".
  - `programmatic_quit_skips_the_prompt` checks that `app.quit` over the control channel bypasses the dialog.
- **Real app** on Linux, run in a headless `kwin_wayland --virtual` session and driven thro…

title: Ask to save unsaved changes before closing a drawing tab (#34, stacked on #47)
author: LloydNicholson
body:
Part of #34. This is a follow-up to #47.

> **Stacked on #47.** This branch contains #47's commit (`0a77920`) plus one new commit (`9d78d65`). Please review/merge #47 first; after that, this PR's diff is just the second commit. To see only the new change now, look at the commits tab, or compare `fix-34-ask-save-on-close...fix-34-ask-save-on-tab-close` on my fork.

## What changed
#47 made closing the **window** ask before discarding unsaved changes. Closing a single **drawing** still discarded them without asking. This PR adds the same prompt to:

- the **×** on a file tab
- **File ▸ Close**, **Cmd/Ctrl+W** and typing `CLOSE`
- **File ▸ Close All** (with several changed drawings it says "Save changes to N drawings?")

**Save** saves only the drawings being closed (Save As for one that has no file yet), then closes them. If a save is cancelled or fails, they all stay open. **Don't Save** closes them. **Cancel** keeps them open. A drawing with no unsaved changes closes immediately, as before.

JSON calls to `close` / `closeall` (control channel `engine.execute`, MCP, scripts with params) still close without a dialog, in line with "programmatic calls never open dialogs". The UI paths are routed in `run_ui_command` with the same `params.is_null()` convention that `layer` and `qselect` use.

I also refactored the code from #47:
- The window prompt and the drawing prompt now share one `save_prompt`.
- `save_all` became `save_where(pick)`, so closing one tab doesn't save other drawings.
- Drawings waiting on the dialog are tracked by `DocState::uid`, not by index, because indices shift as tabs close.

- **New tests** in `crates/ui-egui/src/dialogs.rs`:
  - `closing_a_drawing_with_unsaved_changes_asks_first`: a clean drawing closes immediately, a dirty one opens the dialog and stays open, and `app.start("close")` (File ▸ Close / Cmd+W) does the same. title: ui.render: fit the drawing and return pngBase64 like the headless render (#49, #50)
author: MarekSpodBiedry
body:
Fixes #49, fixes #50.

The desktop app's `ui.render` control handler (used by the MCP `render` tool when it is bridged to the running app) now behaves like the headless backend in `crates/mcp/src/backend.rs`:

- **#49:** the reply now includes `pngBase64`, `width` and `height`, so the MCP bridge returns an image instead of text. The old `bytes` key and `path` (when a path is given) are still there, so existing callers keep working.
- **#50:** `fit` (default `true`) frames the whole drawing with `View::fit(&list.bounds, w, h, 0.05)`. Before, the handler always rendered the current screen view, so a drawing outside it came out blank. `fit: false` keeps the current view.

The view choice and the reply are in two small helpers, `render_view` and `render_reply`, in `crates/ui-egui/src/control.rs`. Unit tests cover both: a drawing far from the current view is centred when `fit` is true and ignored when it is false, and the reply has decodable `pngBase64` plus `width`, `height`, `bytes` and an optional `path`.

`docs/control-protocol.md` and the module doc comment now describe the new `fit` parameter and the reply shape.

title: Show Ctrl/Shift shortcuts on Windows and Linux, symbols only on macOS (#53)
author: MarekSpodBiedry
body:
Fixes #53.

Menus and toolbar tooltips always showed macOS symbols (⌘, ⇧), also on Windows and Linux, in the desktop app and in the web build. The shortcuts themselves already worked.

The app now picks the shortcut text at runtime with egui's `ctx.os()`. A `cfg!(target_os)` check would not work for the web build, because it runs in a browser on any OS. egui reads the OS from the browser's user agent there.

- New `menus::shortcut_label(s, mac)` turns a registry shortcut such as `Cmd+Shift+Z` into `⇧⌘Z` on macOS (and iOS) and `Ctrl+Shift+Z` everywhere else. The menus use it.
- Toolbar entries now store a label and an optional registry shortcut. The tooltip ("Redo (Ctrl+Shift+Z)" / "Redo (⇧⌘Z)") is built when it is drawn, so it uses the same helper.
- The multiline text dialog shows "Ctrl+Enter to finish" instead of "⌘↩ to finish" on Windows and Linux. The key check was already `modifiers.command`, which is Ctrl on those systems.

On macOS, the toolbar tooltips do not change. In the menus, shortcuts that have Shift now show it before ⌘ (`⇧⌘Z`, not `⌘⇧Z`). This matches the toolbar and the usual macOS order.

Test: `shortcut_label_per_platform` covers Cmd, Cmd+Shift, Shift only and a shortcut with no modifier, on both platforms.

title: Fix successive line and polyline segment visibility mid-command (fixes #44)
author: mbonatte
body:
Fixes #44. Supersedes #22.

## Problem & Background
Issue #44 reported that when drawing a line or polyline, only the first segment appeared on the canvas while successive segments remained invisible until finishing the command with Enter or Esc.

In PR #22, an attempt was made to bump `st.revision` inside `Session::feed` when `!Arc::ptr_eq(&run.before, &st.doc)`. However:
1. **Unnecessary rebuilds on every event:** Once the first segment modified `st.doc`, `!Arc::ptr_eq(&run.before, &st.doc)` stayed `true` for all subsequent inputs, causing mouse moves, mode toggles, and keystrokes to invalidate the display list even without document changes.
2. **Wrong architectural layer:** `Session::feed()` only processes text input from the prompt machine, missing programmatic command executions, internal undo, and view restorations.

## Root Cause
In `cadcraft-ui-egui/src/canvas.rs`, `ensure_list` caches the display list keyed by `(st.uid, st.revision, band, lwdisplay, Arc::as_ptr(&st.doc) as usize)`.

When an interactive command starts, `run.before` stores a clone of `st.doc` (reference count 2).
- On the first segment, `Arc::make_mut` clones `st.doc` because ref count is 2. The pointer changes, so `ensure_list` rebuilds and renders the first line.
- On successive segments, `st.doc` has ref count 1. `Arc::make_mut` mutates `st.doc` in place, keeping the pointer unchanged.
- Because `st.revision` was previously only bumped when the command finished (`Session::finish`), the cache key remained unchanged mid-command and `ensure_list` returned early.

## Solution
1. **Mutation-level revision tracking (`cadcraft-engine`):**
   - Added `DocState::doc_mut(&mut self) -> &mut Drawing` that increments `self.revision += 1` whenever copy-on-write access to the drawing is taken, and routed `Session::doc_mut()` through it.
   - Increment `revision` on rollback / doc restoration so display lists refresh if an operation is cancelled.
2. **Font metrics fallback (`cadcraft-fonts`):**

title: Trackpad pan
author: Tru10
body:
## Problem

On a trackpad there was no realtime pan. A two-finger swipe arrives as a scroll event, and the canvas turned every scroll into a zoom. The only realtime pan is middle-drag, which needs a middle mouse button.

## Change

`crates/ui-egui/src/canvas.rs` now checks which device is scrolling, using the unit on egui's raw `MouseWheel` events:

- **Point units** (trackpad, Magic Mouse): scrolling pans the view on both axes, following the fingers like a middle-drag.
- **Line units** (notched mouse wheel): scrolling zooms about the cursor, exactly as before.
- Pinch and Cmd+scroll still zoom through `zoom_delta`, and middle-drag still pans.

The device choice is sticky across frames because egui spreads a wheel notch over several frames.

The second commit adds my entry to `contributors/people.toml`.

## Known limitation

A mouse whose driver adds smooth scrolling (Logi Options+, SteerMouse and similar) can report point units, so its wheel will pan instead of zoom. Cmd+scroll still zooms there. Telling those apart from a trackpad would need platform-specific input, which seemed out of scope.

## Testing

- Tried it on a MacBook Pro trackpad: two-finger swipe pans, pinch zooms.
- `cargo xtask ci`: fmt, clippy, test, assets and layers pass. I didn't run the wasm check locally (the target isn't installed on my machine); the change only uses cross-platform egui input APIs.

title: Dynamic Input: pointer input boxes with Tab, comma and relative entry
author: Tru10
body:
## Summary

Dynamic Input now has AutoCAD-style pointer input: a pair of value boxes beside the cursor whenever a command asks for a point. ROADMAP M1 lists "dynamic input fields"; this covers pointer input (not dimensional input).

**Behavior change to be aware of:** with Dynamic Input on (CADCraft's default), a typed `x,y` for a second or later point is now relative to the last point, as in AutoCAD. Turning Dynamic Input off (F12), or setting DYNPICOORDS to 1, restores absolute entry. The first point of a command is always absolute.

## How it works

- **First point:** X and Y boxes, absolute.
- **Second and later points:** distance and angle boxes by default (DYNPIFORMAT = 0), measured from the last point.
- **`,` after a value** locks it as X and moves to Y. **`<`** locks it as the distance and moves to the angle. A locked value shows a lock and holds the cursor.
- **Tab** types the separator for the format on show, so `40` Tab `90` is 40 units at 90°. With DYNPIFORMAT = 1, `40` Tab `40` is 40 over and 40 up.
- **Enter / Space** sends the entry with `@` in front, filling an empty box from the cursor. If a prompt's base point isn't the session's last point, it sends the finished point as `#x,y` instead, so the result always matches the preview.
- **Unchanged:** a plain number and Enter is still direct distance entry; `@`/`#` entries, keywords and command names go through as typed.

The command-line text is the single source of truth: the boxes are a view of it, so the command line always shows exactly what will be sent (`40,`, `40<90`) and Backspace just edits it.

## Notes for review

- **Tab and focus:** egui moves keyboard focus to the next widget on Tab, which left the command line deaf to typing. `cmdline::capture_tab` runs in the raw input hook (desktop and web) and, while no widget has focus, turns a pressed Tab into a `"\t"` text event so it keeps its order among keystrokes.
- **Scope:** scripts, the control channel's `cmdline.input` and MCP don't pass th…

title: Press-and-drag selection windows (PICKDRAG = 2)
author: Tru10
body:
Selection windows only worked click-then-click: the canvas reacts to clicks, and a press that moves before release is a drag, not a click, so a drag was ignored entirely.

Now, while objects are being selected (no command running, or a command asking for objects), a drag opens the window where the button went down and letting go closes it, as with AutoCAD's default PICKDRAG = 2. Dragging right is a window, dragging left a crossing window, Shift still removes, and click-click works as before. Drags that start on a grip or while a command asks for a point are left alone.

Session::begin_window opens the window at the drag's start, even over an object (a click there would pick the object instead), with an engine test.

author: dylanmtaylor
body:
## Summary

Adds cross-compiled RISC-V (`riscv64gc-unknown-linux-gnu`) Linux builds to the release workflow using Ubuntu 26.04, packaging native `.deb` and `.rpm` files alongside standalone `.tar.gz`, with `qemu-user-static` smoke testing. Also upgrades `flatpak` runners to `ubuntu-26.04`.

- **CI (`.github/workflows/release.yml`)**:
  - Upgraded `flatpak` runner matrix to `ubuntu-26.04` and `ubuntu-26.04-arm`.
  - Added `linux-riscv64` cross-compilation job running on `ubuntu-26.04`.
  - Added `nfpm` to generate `.deb`, `.rpm`, and `.tar.gz` packages for `riscv64`.
  - Smoke-tests `cadcraft-cli --version` under `qemu-riscv64-static`.
  - Uploads all assets via `dist/release/*`.
- **Packaging (`packaging/linux/package.sh`)**:
  - Added `CROSS_ARCH`, `CROSS_TARGET`, `CROSS_COMPILE`, and `EMULATOR` support.

- **Documentation (`README.md`)**:
  - Documented `riscv64` `.deb`, `.rpm`, and `.tar.gz` release assets.

### Note on AppImage and Flatpak for riscv64

AppImage and Flatpak remain unavailable for `riscv64`:
- **AppImage**: Upstream `appimagetool` continuous releases only produce runtimes for `x86_64`, `aarch64`, `i686`, and `armhf`. There is currently no official RISC-V runtime in AppImageKit.

title: PLINE: Halfwidth is centre-to-edge, and Width answers taper the next segment (fixes #83, #104)
author: SBaksa
body:
Fixes #83. Fixes #104.

Interactive PLINE kept a single width value. Halfwidth answers were stored as the total width (#83), and the ending-width answer overwrote the starting one, so the polyline got one constant width instead of a taper (#104).

**Change** (`PlineM` in `crates/engine/src/cmd/draw.rs`):
- The next segment's starting and ending widths are tracked separately (`start_w`, `end_w`). Halfwidth answers are doubled into total width, and its prompts read "Specify starting/ending half-width" with the defaults shown in half-width units.
- The ending width defaults to the starting width, so Enter gives a uniform segment.
- When a segment is drawn, including the closing segment, its first vertex gets the requested `start_width`/`end_width`. Later segments are uniform at the ending width, as in AutoCAD.
- Uniform polylines (every segment the same width) are still stored as `const_width` with zero vertex widths, so their DXF output is unchanged. Only real tapers use per-vertex widths, which the renderer, the DXF writer and the JSON `pline` form already support.
- Undo clears the widths of the removed segment.

| Input | Before | After |
|---|---|---|
| Halfwidth 0.5 / 0.5 | constant 0.5 | constant **1.0** |
| Halfwidth 0.5 / Enter | constant 0.5 | constant **1.0** |
| Width 0.5 / 0.5 | constant 0.5 | constant 0.5 |
| Width 1 / 0.2 | constant 0.2 | **taper 1 → 0.2** |
| Width 0.2 / 1 | constant 1.0 | **taper 0.2 → 1** |
| Width 1 / 1, or Width 1 / Enter | constant 1.0 | constant 1.0 |
| Width 1 / 0.2, then two more segments | constant 0.2 | taper 1 → 0.2, then uniform 0.2 |

**Tests** (`crates/engine/src/tests.rs`), driving the real prompts with `Session::cmdline`:
- `pline_halfwidth_is_centre_to_edge`: #83's table, the Enter default and a half-width taper.
- `pline_width_answers_taper_the_next_segment`: #104's taper in both directions, the uniform controls, later segments carrying the ending width, a width set mid-polyline including the closing segment, and Undo.…

title: Windows: prefer DirectX 12 over Vulkan for the GPU backend
author: JeremyYao
body:
## Summary

On Windows, `cadcraft` picks its GPU backend through wgpu's defaults, which prefer Vulkan. On an AMD Radeon laptop the app dies at startup with `STATUS_ACCESS_VIOLATION` inside AMD's Vulkan driver before a window ever appears. This PR makes the desktop app prefer DirectX 12 on Windows, with OpenGL as the fallback, while keeping the `WGPU_BACKEND` environment variable as an override.

Fixes a hard crash on launch; no behaviour change on macOS, Linux, FreeBSD or the web build.

## The problem

### Symptom

```
PS> cargo run --release -p cadcraft -- --sample
    Finished `release` profile [optimized] target(s) in 12.60s
     Running `target\release\cadcraft.exe --sample`
error: process didn't exit successfully: `target\release\cadcraft.exe --sample`
       (exit code: 0xc0000005, STATUS_ACCESS_VIOLATION)
```

No window, no log output, no panic message. The headless `cadcraft-cli` works fine on the same machine, which already pointed at the GPU path rather than the engine.

### Environment

| | |
|---|---|
| Machine | ASUS ROG Strix G513QY |
| CPU / iGPU | AMD Ryzen 9 5900HX with integrated Radeon graphics, driver 30.0.13002.13003 (2021-12) |
| dGPU | AMD Radeon RX 6800M, driver 32.0.21045.5002 (2026-08) |
| OS | Windows 11 IoT Enterprise LTSC 2024, build 26100 |
| Toolchain | rustc 1.99.0 stable, x86_64-pc-windows-msvc |
| eframe / egui-wgpu | 0.36 |

### Root cause

The Windows Application event log identifies the faulting module:

```
Faulting application name: cadcraft.exe, version: 0.4.0.0
Faulting module name:      amdvlk64.dll, version: 32.0.21045.5002
Exception code:            0xc0000005
Faulting module path:      C:\WINDOWS\System32\DriverStore\FileRepository\u0203303.inf_amd64_...\amdvlk64.dll
```

`amdvlk64.dll` is AMD's Vulkan ICD. The fault happens inside the driver during instance or device creation, which is why nothing in CADCraft runs first. A driver access violation is outside the reach of the never-crash guards (`catch_unwind` in `Session…

title: ARC: refuse zero-radius arcs instead of adding them (fixes #85)
author: SBaksa
body:
Fixes #85.

`run_arc` (`crates/engine/src/cmd/draw.rs`) checked its three-point form for collinear points, but added the arcs built by its start/center/end and center/radius forms unchecked. A radius of 0, or a start point on the center, added a degenerate Arc, marked the drawing dirty and recorded an undo step.

**Change:** every `arc` result now goes through the existing `finite_arc` check in `curves.rs` (finite center, radius and angles; radius above `EPS`), which is made `pub(crate)` for this. A degenerate arc fails with the same "these values do not define an arc" error that the `arc.*` variants and the interactive ARC already use, before anything is added.

| Request | Before | After |
|---|---|---|
| `arc {"center":[0,0],"radius":0,"start":0,"end":90}` | adds a radius-0 Arc, exit 0 | error, drawing unchanged, exit 1 |
| `arc {"start":[0,0],"center":[0,0],"end":[1,0]}` | adds a radius-0 Arc, exit 0 | error, drawing unchanged, exit 1 |
| `arc.sce` with the same points | error | error (unchanged) |
| `arc {"center":[0,0],"radius":5,"start":0,"end":90}` | quarter circle | quarter circle (unchanged) |

A negative radius is left as it was: `Arc::new` takes the radius's absolute value, and that isn't part of this issue.

**Tests:** `arc_refuses_zero_radius` in `crates/engine/src/tests.rs`. Both zero-radius requests return the error, and `drawing.inspect` reports 0 entities, `dirty: false` and an empty undo list. The radius-5 control still adds the arc. The test fails on `main`.

`cargo fmt --check`, `cargo clippy -p cadcraft-engine --all-targets -- -D warnings`, `cargo test --workspace` (325 passed) and `cargo xtask layers` pass. The issue's `cadcraft-cli run --metric --cmd 'arc …'` commands now exit 1 with the error for both zero-radius cases, matching `arc.sce`.

title: Menu commands open their dialogs; JSON calls never open file pickers (fixes #65, fixes #101)
author: kaffeochknivar
body:
Fixes #65. Fixes #101.

> Builds on #37 (clippy fix needed for `cargo xtask ci` to pass), so this diff includes that one-line commit until #37 merges. Merges cleanly with #38, #47, #48 and current `main`.

Both issues come from the same place, `menus::run_ui_command`, which decides when a command opens a dialog or a picker. The rule this PR applies everywhere is the one in AGENTS.md:

- Typed or menu-invoked commands (no parameters) open the dialog or picker.
- JSON calls never do.

## #65: Tools > Drafting Settings... does nothing

The menu item runs the engine command `dsettings`. With no parameters, its JSON form changes nothing. Only the status-bar gear (`ui.dialog.dsettings`) opened the dialog.

- Typed or menu-invoked `DSETTINGS`/`DS`/`SE` now opens the Drafting Settings dialog.
- `PROPERTIES`/`PR`/`CH` (Modify > Properties) had the same problem. It now shows the Properties palette.

## #101: programmatic file commands open desktop pickers

`open`, `saveas` and `qsave` opened a native picker whenever their parameters had no `path`/`data`, so `engine.execute` and the bridged MCP `execute` tool could block on a dialog.

- These engine commands now ask for a file only when typed or chosen from a menu. JSON calls get the command's own missing-path error.
- `ui.open` and `ui.saveas` are the pickers themselves (Cmd+O, Cmd+Shift+S), so they keep opening them.
- Side effect: the control method `app.save` on an unnamed drawing now returns qsave's "drawing has no file name yet; use saveas {path}" error instead of opening Save As.

## Also: the `cmd {json}` form at the command line

`CadApp::cmdline` intercepted the first word without looking at the rest. So `layer {}` typed at the command line opened the Layer Properties Manager, and `open {"path": …}` opened the picker. When the rest of the line is a JSON object, the engine now runs the command with those parameters.

## Test plan

- [x] New `crates/ui-egui/tests/dialog_dispatch…

title: Extents: a wide polyline's bounds follow its drawn band (fixes #90)
author: SBaksa
body:
Fixes #90.

Polyline extents were the centre line padded by `const_width / 2` (`crates/doc/src/extents.rs`), so per-segment `start_width`/`end_width` never counted. A band built from vertex widths, a taper, or segments of different widths reported the zero-height bounds of its centre line.

**Change:** a new `lwpolyline_bounds` encloses the filled band of every segment as it's drawn:
- **Straight segments**, tapers included: the band's four corners, which are exact.
- **Arc segments:** both band edges, sampled along the arc with the width interpolated, then widened by the sampling tolerance (0.01% of the outer radius) so the bounds are never smaller than the band. Sampling uses `Arc::tessellate`, capped at 4,096 points.
- **The same rules as drawing:** `const_width` wins over vertex widths, and the end vertex of an open polyline starts no segment. Non-finite or negative widths count as zero.
- **Thin polylines** only use the centre line, as before.

A constant-width polyline now gets its exact band too. The issue's constant example (0,0)→(10,0), width 2, went from `[[-1,-1],[11,1]]` to `[[0,-1],[10,1]]`, which is the band's actual extent.

| Case (from #90) | Before | After |
|---|---|---|
| constant width 2 | `[[-1,-1],[11,1]]` | `[[0,-1],[10,1]]` |
| per-vertex width 2 | `[[0,0],[10,0]]` | `[[0,-1],[10,1]]` |
| taper 0 → 4 | `[[0,0],[10,0]]` | `[[0,-2],[10,2]]` |
| widths 2 then 6 | `[[0,0],[20,0]]` | `[[0,-3],[20,3]]` |
| width only on the open end vertex | `[[0,0],[10,0]]` | `[[0,0],[10,0]]` |

These match the filled sizes measured from the SVG export in the issue.

**Tests** (`crates/doc/src/tests.rs`):
- `wide_polyline_extents_follow_the_band`: the five cases above, plus a diagonal band (exact corners, not padded), a closed polyline whose closing segment is the only wide one, the same polyline open, and NaN, infinite and negative widths.
- `wide_arc_segment_extents_reach_the_outer_edge`: a constant-width and a per-vertex-width half circle reach radius plus hal…
