title: SETVAR DIM* variables become style overrides for new dimensions (fixes #66)
author: kaffeochknivar
body:
Fixes #66.

> Builds on #37 (clippy fix needed for `cargo xtask ci` to pass), so this diff includes that one-line commit until #37 merges. Merges cleanly with `main`, #15, #20, #38, #60 and #125.

## The problem

`SETVAR DIMSCALE 24` was stored in the header but never reached new dimensions. They were created with empty `overrides`, and `dimension_geometry_with` only fell back to the header DIMSCALE when the style's scale was ≤ 0. Extents and leader arrows each used a third rule, as the issue points out.

Simply multiplying the header DIMSCALE into every dimension, as `extents.rs` did, would be wrong in two ways:

- It would rescale existing dimensions.
- It would double-scale AutoCAD drawings, whose header DIMSCALE already equals the style's (24 × 24).

## Changes

**Style overrides, as in AutoCAD**
- `Drawing::dim_overrides()` returns the header DIM* variables that differ from the current dimension style, as `DimStyle` fields. They are compared after the same `apply_fields` conversion, and arrow block and text style names compare without case.
- New dimensions take these on, through `annotate::dim`. Existing dimensions keep their size.
- `Drawing::sync_dim_vars()` sets the header variables back to the style's values. It runs when a style is made current (`dimstyle.current`) and when the current style is edited (`dimstyle`). That keeps the issue's workaround, `dimstyle {"name": "Standard", "DIMSCALE": 24}`, working instead of being cancelled by a stale header DIMSCALE of 1.
- `sysvars::get` reads DIM* variables that the header doesn't carry (e.g. `DIMASZ` in a new drawing) from the current style. So `GETVAR` works for them, and so does the interactive `SETVAR` from #38.

**One scale rule**
- `DimStyle::effective_scale(dimscale)` is used by the dimension geometry and by dimension extents. Extents now use the style with the dimension's overrides, so they agree with what is drawn.
- A DIMSCALE of zero (AutoCAD: scale to the layout viewport, not computed here) falls ba…

title: DXF: keep layer transparency and description through save and reopen (fixes #96, fixes #97)
author: kaffeochknivar
body:
Fixes #96. Fixes #97.

> Builds on #37 (clippy fix needed for `cargo xtask ci` to pass), so this diff includes that one-line commit until #37 merges. Merges cleanly with `main`, #38, #125 and #129.

## The problem

The LAYER writer (`dxf_write.rs`) omitted both properties, and the reader (`dxf_read.rs`) left them at their defaults. So a reopened drawing had every layer opaque and every description empty. The files written for 0 % and 40 % transparency were byte-identical, as #96 observed.

## Changes

AutoCAD stores both properties as xdata on the LAYER record. The writer now emits them after the record's own groups, and the reader picks them up:

| Property | Application | Groups |
|---|---|---|
| Transparency | `AcCmTransparency` | `1071` = `0x02000000 \| alpha`, with alpha = ⌊(100 − percent) × 255 / 100⌋. 40 % is alpha 153 = 33554585. |
| Description | `AcAecLayerStandard` | Two `1000` strings: the layer standard's name (unused, written empty), then the description. |

- Reading rounds alpha back to the nearest percent, clamped to 0..=90, so 1, 40, 50 (AutoCAD writes alpha 127) and 90 all come back exactly. A value without the "by alpha" flag (ByLayer, ByBlock, junk) leaves the layer opaque.
- A description is cut to the 255 bytes a `1000` group may hold, at a character boundary.
- Both applications are registered in the APPID table.

Helpers live in `dxf_ext.rs`: `transparency_to_dxf`, `transparency_from_dxf` and `xdata_str`.

## Limits

- `write_ascii` already turns line breaks in strings into spaces, so a multi-line description comes back as one line.
- DWG wasn't touched or tested.
- Entity transparency (group 440) isn't written to DXF either. That's a separate, unreported bug, and I'll file it separately.

## Test plan

- [x] `cargo xtask ci`: all 6 steps pass
- [x] New `layer_transparency_and_description_roundtrip` (io). It fails on `main` and covers:
  - transparency 0/1/40/90, with color and plot still intact
  - non-ASCII descriptions
  - the 255-byte cu…

title: TrueType text height: measure the H glyph when the font has no sCapHeight
author: STE1200
body:
Text height means cap height in CADCraft (`crates/fonts/src/ttf.rs`, "Text height = cap height"). Fonts whose OS/2 table predates version 2 carry no `sCapHeight`; DejaVu Sans, the default font on most Linux desktops, is one of them. For those the code fell back to 0.72 × ascent, which for DejaVu is about 9 % too small, so every TrueType text in such a font rendered about 9 % taller than its height says.

The fonts crate's own test caught it on a clean Ubuntu 24.04 clone:

```
---- ttf_tests::system_font_outlines_when_available stdout ----
cap height ~ text height, got 1.1105266234145772
```

This change measures the `H` outline when the table has no cap height and keeps the ascent share only for a font without an `H`. `cargo xtask ci` passes; the previously failing test now passes with DejaVu Sans, and fonts with `sCapHeight` are unaffected.



Also fixed by this change: `render::tests::truetype_text_is_filled_or_outlined`, which fails on the same clean Ubuntu clone for the same reason (DejaVu Sans without `sCapHeight`).

🤖 Generated with [Claude Code](https://claude.com/claude-code)

title: Keep ATTDEF prompt when saving DXF (#81)
author: MarekSpodBiedry
body:
Fixes #81.

The DXF writer always emitted an empty group 3 for ATTDEF, so an attribute definition's prompt was lost on save and reopen, and INSERT then fell back to "Enter attribute value". The reader already loads group 3 into `Attrib::prompt`.

`text_tags` now takes the ATTDEF prompt (`Option<&str>`) instead of a bare `attdef` flag and writes it to group 3. TEXT and the ATTRIBs written after an INSERT pass `None`, so their output is unchanged.

Test: `attdef_prompt_survives_dxf_roundtrip` in `crates/io/src/tests.rs` round-trips two ATTDEFs, one with prompt `Enter value` and one with an explicitly empty prompt, and checks that both prompts come back unchanged.

title: Keep elevations when EXPLODE splits a 3D polyline (#88)
author: MarekSpodBiedry
body:
Fixes #88.

EXPLODE on a 3D polyline built each segment with `line(a.xy(), b.xy())`, and that helper puts both endpoints at Z = 0. Each segment is now a `Line` built straight from the two consecutive `Vec3` points, so the exploded lines keep the polyline's XYZ endpoints. FLATTEN is still the command that drops elevations.

Test: `explode_polyline3d_keeps_elevations` explodes `3dpoly` (0,0,5) (1,0,6) (1,1,7) and checks that the two lines have Z (5,6) and (6,7). Without the fix it gets (0,0) and (0,0).

title: Reject out-of-domain values in PARAMETERS instead of dropping the constraint (#93)
author: MarekSpodBiedry
body:
Fixes #93.

`set_parameter` re-solved the trial drawing and committed it even when the new value put a dimensional constraint outside its domain (aligned distance -5, radius 0). The solver then listed that constraint as skipped, so the value was stored but no longer enforced, and later grip edits ignored the dimension.

Now `set_parameter` checks the solve report. If a constraint is skipped after the change but was not skipped before it, it returns `SolveError::Invalid` with the same message that creation gives (`Aligned value must be non-negative`, `Radius value must be positive`). The drawing stays unchanged, as the function's doc comment already promises. This matches `add`, which rejects the same values when the constraint is created. Constraints that were already skipped before the change do not block unrelated edits.

`set_parameter` is the only place that changes a parameter expression, so the `parameters` command and every other route to it (CLI, MCP, the Parameters Manager) get the check. A change to a user parameter that pushes a dependent dimension out of its domain is rejected the same way.

Test: `set_parameter_rejects_out_of_domain_dimension` sets d1 = -5 and rad1 = 0 and expects both to be rejected with the drawing unchanged. It then checks that the valid values 6 and 2 still apply and that all constraints are satisfied. Without the fix, the first assertion fails.

title: Keep arc-length dimensions as arc-length through DXF save and reopen (#100)
author: MarekSpodBiedry
body:
Fixes #100.

The DXF writer saved an arc-length dimension (`DimKind::ArcLength`) as dimension type 1, and the reader turns type 1 into `Aligned`. After a reopen the dimension was aligned. Any later update or save then rebuilt it as a straight dimension that measures the chord (14.14 for the issue's quarter circle) and not the arc (15.71).

Changes in `crates/io`:

- `dxf_write.rs`: `ArcLength` is now written as dimension type 8. The standard types 0 to 6 already have other meanings. It also writes the arc centre (group 15, `p15`), which the arc-length renderer and associativity need. Before, only `p13`/`p14` were written, the same as for aligned dimensions.
- `dxf_read.rs`: type 8 now reads back as `DimKind::ArcLength`. `p15` was already read for every dimension.

Aligned dimensions and the other kinds are written exactly as before.

Test: `arc_length_dimension_keeps_its_kind_and_centre_on_roundtrip` saves an arc-length dimension whose centre is not at the origin, reopens it, and checks that the kind is still `ArcLength` and the centre is unchanged. Without the fix it reopens as `Aligned`.

title: Apply DIMOVERRIDE text together with dimension variables (#108)
author: MarekSpodBiedry
body:
Fixes #108.

`run_override` handled `text` only when the call contained nothing but `text` and the target handles. A call that also gave a dimension variable (for example `{"text":"<> TYP","DIMDEC":1}`) went straight to `props::dim_override`, which does not know `text`, so it stored the precision, left the old annotation text in place and returned `"ignored":["text"]`.

Now, when `text` is present, the other keys (variables and `clear`) are passed to `props::dim_override` first for the same handles, and then the text is set. The response keeps the `changed` count and includes `ignored` from `dim_override` when variables were given. Calls with only `text` or only variables behave as before.

Unknown variables: a call with valid `text` and only unknown names (for example `"nope"`) still returns the existing "no valid dimension variables given" error, and nothing is changed, because the variables are validated before the text is written. A call that mixes valid and unknown names applies the valid ones and lists the unknown ones in `ignored`, as `dimoverride` already does without `text`.

Test: `dimension_override_text_with_variables` in `annotate_tests.rs` follows the issue's existing-state variant (`DIMTXT` 0.4 and text `<> OLD` set first, then the combined call). It checks that the text becomes `<> TYP`, `decimals` is 1 and `textHeight` is kept, and that the unknown-name call errors without changing the text. Without the fix the text stays `<> OLD`.

title: Write LWPOLYLINE elevation (group 38) to DXF (#77)
author: MarekSpodBiedry
body:
Fixes #77.

The DXF reader already takes a lightweight polyline's elevation from group 38 (`dxf_read.rs`, `t.fd(38, 0.0)`), but the writer never emitted it, so saving and reopening a rectangle drawn with `elevation: 5` or `-2.5` came back at 0.0. Resaving a file that did carry group 38 dropped it again.

The LWPOLYLINE writer now emits group 38 when the elevation is nonzero, right after the optional constant width (43), in the `AcDbPolyline` subclass where the DXF reference places it. Zero elevation is still omitted, the same way the writer already skips zero constant width, widths and bulges, so files without elevation are byte-for-byte unchanged.

Test: `lwpolyline_elevation_roundtrips` saves and reopens a closed polyline with elevation 5.0, -2.5 and 0.0, then saves and reopens the result a second time (the resave case from the issue). It checks the elevation and vertices each time. Without the writer change the 5.0 and -2.5 cases read back 0.0.

title: Convert typed ellipse arc angles to ellipse parameters (#82)
author: MarekSpodBiedry
body:
Fixes #82.

In the interactive elliptical-arc prompts (`ELLIPSE` > Arc, `ellipse.arc`, `ellipse.axis` > Arc, with or without Center), a typed start or end angle was stored as `angle + major.angle()` and used directly as the ellipse parameter. A picked point already goes through `Ellipse::param_of`, and the `ellipse.arc` JSON form does the same conversion (`to_param` in `draw2.rs`). So on a non-circular or rotated ellipse, a typed angle gave a different arc than the same direction picked as a point or sent as JSON.

The typed angle is now treated as a true angle from the major axis and converted the way the JSON path does it: `param_of(center + Vec2::from_angle(a + major.angle()))`. Both the start and end prompts share this branch, and every entry path listed in the issue ends in this one state machine, so they are all covered. Point input and the JSON command do not change.

Test: `ellipse_arc_typed_angles_are_true_angles` types `0` and `45` on a horizontal and on a vertical major axis with ratio 0.5. It checks for the parameters the issue expects, `[0, atan2(2,1)]`. On main the test fails: the horizontal end comes out as `pi/4`, and the vertical start/end come out shifted by `pi/2`.

title: Fix justified TEXT extents and picking (#89)
author: MarekSpodBiedry
body:
Fixes #89.

The approximate bounds of a single-line TEXT in `crates/doc/src/extents.rs` ignored justification: the box always started at the insertion (or alignment) point and extended right and up. Zoom extents, `drawing.inspect` and point picking all use these bounds, so right-justified text was framed and picked on the wrong side of its alignment point, and centered or vertically justified text was off as well.

The box is now placed the same way `cadcraft_fonts::place` places the strokes: origin is the insertion point for Left/Aligned/Fit and the alignment point otherwise, shifted by -w/2 (Center/Middle) or -w (Right) horizontally and by the Bottom/Middle/Top offsets vertically, then rotated.

ATTDEF entities and block ATTRIBs go through the same `Text` struct and the renderer justifies them the same way, so they used the same unjustified box. All three now share one helper.

The per-character width estimate goes from 0.8 to 0.9 of the height. The issue measured 4.4 units for "HELLO" at height 1 (about 0.88 per character), so the old 0.8 estimate did not cover the rendered strokes even for Left text.

Tests (in `extents.rs`, through `entity_bounds`):
- right-justified TEXT lies left of its alignment point (the issue's repro: strokes span x -4.4..0)
- Center and Top-Left TEXT follow their rendered placement
- right-justified ATTDEF lies left of its alignment point

All three fail on main.

title: Reject deleting a dimension that a remaining dimension refers to (#94)
author: MarekSpodBiedry
body:
Fixes #94.

`delconstraint` removed the selected constraints without checking the expressions that stay. With `d1 = 8` and `d2 = d1/2`, deleting `d1` (by id or by handle) reported success but left `d2` unevaluable: it stopped holding its width after an edit, and the next constraint add failed with ``unknown parameter `d1` ``.

Now `delconstraint` works on a copy of the drawing, removes the selected constraints there, and rebuilds the parameter table. If a surviving dimension or parameter that evaluated before now fails, the command returns "`d1` is used by `d2`" and the drawing is unchanged. This matches the guard `parameters {"delete": ...}` already uses for user parameters. Expressions that were already broken before the deletion do not block it.

- Covers deletion by `ids`, by `handles`, and the interactive Delete Constraints command (it goes through the same function).
- Selecting both dimensions still removes both, as the issue asks; a selection is never silently widened to the dependent dimension.
- The name in the message comes from the names the surviving expression actually uses (`expr::names`), not a substring match.

Test: `delconstraint_rejects_referenced_dimension` checks the error and that the drawing is unchanged for both the id and handle paths, and that deleting both dimensions together still works. It fails on main (the deletion succeeds).

title: MCP bridge: do not resend a mutation whose reply was lost (#102)
author: MarekSpodBiedry
body:
Fixes #102.

`Remote::call` (`crates/mcp/src/backend.rs`) resent the same request line on any failure of the first round trip. When the control connection closed after the app had applied a mutation but before it replied, the resend applied it a second time: one `execute` `circle` call added two circles and reported success with the second handle.

`roundtrip` now reports whether the request may already have reached the server:

- connect or write failed: the request was not delivered, so `call` still reconnects and sends it once more (unchanged behaviour);
- the request was sent but no reply came (EOF or read error): read-only methods (`drawing.inspect`, `document.inspect`, `engine.commands`, `cmdline.state`, `ui.inspect`, `ui.render`, `ui.screenshot`) are still resent, since repeating them cannot change the drawing; every other method returns an explicit error saying the reply was lost and the call may or may not have been applied, so the agent can inspect the drawing instead of getting a silent duplicate.

The healthy path is unchanged. This matches the restoration check in the issue: an explicit ambiguous failure is allowed, a second application is not.

Test: `lost_reply_to_a_mutation_is_not_resent` starts a loopback server that reads one `engine.execute` request and closes the connection without replying, then checks that the call returns the "may or may not have been applied" error and that no second connection arrives. Before the fix the bridge reconnected and resent the request, so the test fails on both assertions.

title: Write Wipeout entities to DXF so saving keeps them (#79)
author: MarekSpodBiedry
body:
Fixes #79.

The DXF writer had no arm for `EntityKind::Wipeout`, so it fell through to the empty fallback and every save route lost the entity: Save As, Quick Save, CLI `--save`, `wblock`, `document.bytes`, and native DWG (which is written through the same DXF serializer).

This PR adds a `WIPEOUT` arm to `crates/io/src/dxf_write.rs`:

- The image frame is a 1x1 image spanning the boundary's extents: insert = min corner, U/V = width/height. Each vertex is stored as `(p - insert) / size - 0.5`. The existing reader (`dxf_read.rs`, `insert + u * (x + 0.5) + v * (y + 0.5)`) maps this back to the same world coordinates, and the clip polygon stays inside the image rectangle.
- Clip boundary type 2 (polygonal). The boundary is closed by repeating the first vertex when needed, so a reopened Wipeout has the closing vertex the issue allows for.
- Display flags 7 (show image, show unaligned, use clipping boundary), clipping state on, and default brightness, contrast and fade, as the DXF reference specifies for WIPEOUT.
- When the drawing contains a Wipeout, the CLASSES section gets a `WIPEOUT` / `AcDbWipeout` entity class entry. This matches how `ACAD_TABLE` and `DIMASSOC` are declared there.

Drawings without Wipeouts produce the same output as before.

Test: `wipeout_survives_dxf_roundtrip` saves a drawing with the square from the issue (`(2,3)`, `(12,3)`, `(12,13)`, `(2,13)`), reopens it and checks that the Wipeout comes back with those world coordinates plus the closing vertex. Without the fix the reopened drawing has no Wipeout and the test fails.

title: Keep selected objects outside the joined chain when using JOIN (#86)
author: MarekSpodBiedry
body:
Fixes #86.

JOIN built the chain from the connected segments but then removed every selected handle, so a selected line or circle that never joined the chain was deleted without contributing any geometry.

`join` now records which entity each segment came from and removes only the entities whose segments ended up in the chain. Unconnected lines and unsupported entities (circles) stay with their handle and geometry, which matches what PEDIT join already does (`pedit_json_options` asserts the same preservation). The rejection paths ("Select at least two objects to join.", "Objects are not connected.") are unchanged, and they still return before anything is removed.

Both entry paths use the same `join` function: the JSON command (`join {"handles": ...}`, CLI/MCP) and the interactive JOIN prompt. The interactive prompt's message "N objects joined into 1 polyline" counted the whole selection; it now counts only the objects that were consumed.

Test: `join_keeps_selected_objects_outside_the_chain` in `modify2_tests.rs` joins two connected lines with a distant line and a circle in the selection. It checks that the result is a 3-vertex polyline, that the two connected lines are gone, and that the distant line and the circle are still there. On main the last two assertions fail.

title: Fence selection now includes crossed XLINE and RAY objects (#92)
author: MarekSpodBiedry
body:
Fixes #92.

`select_fence_with` asked the spatial index for candidates without infinite objects and then required each entity's bounds to intersect the fence. XLINE has empty bounds and RAY has base-only bounds, so a fence crossing either one selected nothing (except a fence through the ray's base point).

The fix matches what `select_window_with` (crossing) and `pick_with` already do for infinite objects: request them from the index (`candidates(..., true, ...)`) and skip the bounds pre-check when `is_infinite(e)`, so the existing `hit_polylines` geometry test decides. Fence is the only selection path with this gap (the `select` command's `fence` parameter is its only caller).

Test `fence_selects_crossed_xline_and_ray` in `crates/engine/src/select.rs` covers the cases in the issue:
- XLINE crossed at x = -5, 0 and 5: selected
- RAY crossed ahead of its base and at its base: selected
- RAY crossed behind its base: not selected
- fences that miss the XLINE and the RAY: not selected

Without the fix, the XLINE fences and the forward RAY fence select nothing and the test fails.

title: Keep viewport frozen-layer lists through DXF save and reopen (#98)
author: MarekSpodBiedry
body:
Fixes #98.

Saving a drawing as DXF and opening it again cleared each paper-space viewport's frozen-layer list (`vplayer freeze`). The writer did not save the list, and the reader always set it to empty.

**Fix**
- `dxf_write`: when a viewport has frozen layers, it now writes them as CADCraft xdata on the `VIEWPORT` entity (`1001 CADCRAFT`, `1000 VPFROZEN`, `1002 {`, one `1000` per layer name, `1002 }`). This uses the same `xdata_list` format as the dimension `ASSOC` links. Viewports with no frozen layers are written the same way as before.
- `dxf_read`: `VIEWPORT` now reads that list back through the new `dxf_ext::read_frozen`, capped at `MAX_XDATA_ITEMS` like the other xdata readers. Files from other writers have no `VPFROZEN` list, so their viewports still load with an empty list.

**Test**
`viewport_frozen_layers_roundtrip` writes one viewport with frozen `Walls` and `A B`, plus an unfrozen control viewport, and reads the file back. The frozen list must survive and the control must stay empty, as the issue's restoration check asks. Without the fix, the frozen viewport comes back with `[]`.

The change is limited to the frozen-layer list that the issue reports.

title: HATCHEDIT: clear the gradient when a named pattern is chosen (#107)
author: MarekSpodBiedry
body:
Fixes #107.

Changing a GRADIENT hatch to a named pattern (for example ANSI31) through HATCHEDIT or the Properties palette's Pattern selector updated `pattern` and `solid`, but left `gradient` set. The renderer draws the filled branch whenever `gradient` is present, so the hatch kept its solid fill and no pattern lines appeared until the drawing was saved and reopened.

The fix is in the Hatch branch of `properties.set` (`crates/engine/src/cmd/props.rs`), which both HATCHEDIT and the palette's Pattern selector go through: when the chosen pattern is not SOLID, `gradient` is cleared. This matches how HATCH/GRADIENT build a hatch, where a gradient always means a SOLID hatch. Scale-only and angle-only edits don't touch the gradient, as the issue asks.

Test: `hatchedit_pattern_replaces_gradient` in `crates/engine/src/cmd/hatch.rs` creates a gradient hatch, checks that a scale+angle edit keeps the gradient, then sets ANSI31 and checks that the pattern is applied, `solid` is false and `gradient` is gone. Without the fix, the last check fails.

title: Keep a free measured origin in place when its source moves (#109)
author: MarekSpodBiedry
body:
Fixes #109.

When every attached point of an associative dimension moves by the same delta, `assoc::recompute` carries the rest of the dimension along. For a linear or aligned dimension that also moved a measured origin (`p13`/`p14`) that has no attachment, such as the second origin of a DIMCONTINUE segment placed in empty space. The dimension kept its old length (15 instead of 12 in the issue's repro).

Change: in that rigid-carry step, a free `p13`/`p14` of a `Linear`/`Aligned` dimension is no longer moved. The dimension line (`defpt`) and text still follow as before. Ordinate and angular dimensions are unchanged. The issue is only about linear measured origins, and for those kinds the carried points do not measure the free distance in the same way.

Restoration check from the issue:
- Line-only move by [3,0]: origins [13,0] / [25,0], label 12. A second move: [16,0] / [25,0], label 9 (new test `moving_the_line_keeps_a_free_continued_origin`; it fails on main, where p14 ends at [28,0]).
- When both origins are attached, the result is unchanged, because both points are snapped directly.
- Rigid translation is unchanged. When both sources move together, both origins are attached and snapped. When the line and the dimensions are selected together, the dimension is already translated, so the delta is zero (`moving_the_object_carries_the_dimension` still covers this).

title: Keep dimension text rotation when saving DXF (#78)
author: MarekSpodBiedry
body:
Fixes #78.

A dimension text angle set with `dimtedit.angle` was lost when the drawing was saved as DXF and opened again. Two places in `crates/io/src/dxf_write.rs` dropped it:

1. **The DIMENSION record.** The writer never emitted group 53, so the reader (`dxf_read.rs`, `t.fd(53, 0.0).to_radians()`) fell back to zero. The writer now emits group 53 in degrees when the rotation is nonzero, the same way MTEXT writes its group 50.
2. **The anonymous `*D` block.** The block MTEXT was always written with rotation `0.0`, so a reopened drawing, which renders from that block, drew horizontal text even with the right `textRotation`. The MTEXT now uses `text_angle` from the rendered dimension geometry, which already includes the explicit rotation. This is the angle the renderer draws with, so the saved block matches the drawing on screen. Dimensions with no explicit rotation whose text is drawn at an angle (for example aligned dimensions) now also keep that angle in the block.

A zero rotation still writes no group 53, so drawings without a text angle save exactly as before.

**Test:** `dimension_text_rotation_roundtrips` (in `crates/io/src/tests.rs`) gives a linear dimension a 30-degree text angle, saves it and reads it back. It checks that the dimension's `text_rotation` and the rotation of the MTEXT in its `*D` block are both 30 degrees. Without the fix, both are zero.

title: Reject nonpositive MTEXT height on creation (#84)
author: MarekSpodBiedry
body:
Fixes #84.

`mtext` accepted `height` 0 or negative and stored it, so the text rendered at the fallback height, and after DXF save/reopen the reader clamped it to 1e-9 (a tiny dot).

`run_mtext` now returns `height must be positive` for `height <= 0`, the same check and message the `text` command already uses. This also matches the MTEXT branch of `properties.set` and the DXF MTEXT reader, which both reject nonpositive heights.

Test: `mtext_rejects_nonpositive_height` in `annotate_tests.rs` checks that heights 0 and -2 fail and add no entity, and that height 2 still works.

title: AREA of a normal hatch no longer counts unfilled islands (#91)
author: MarekSpodBiedry
body:
Fixes #91.

AREA on a hatch summed the absolute area of every boundary loop, so a 10x10 normal hatch with a 2x2 island reported 104 instead of 96.

The hatch branch of `area` now uses odd parity, the same rule the renderer uses for solid fills and pattern clipping (and the one documented for style 0): each loop's first tessellated point is tested against the other loops, and a loop nested inside an odd number of them is subtracted. Perimeter is unchanged (sum of all loop lengths).

Restoration checks from the issue:
- one island: 96 (perimeter 48), pick-point and boundary-handle hatches alike, any pattern (the pattern does not enter the computation);
- single boundary: still 100;
- outer/middle/inner squares: 68 (100 - 36 + 4).

Test: `area_of_hatch_excludes_island` covers the one-island case (96, perimeter 48) and the three-level nesting (68). It fails on main (104 and 140).

title: Store canonical autoTypes names so accepted spellings take effect (#95)
author: MarekSpodBiedry
body:
Fixes #95.

`constraintsettings` accepted any `autoTypes` entry that `kind_from_name` recognises (`gcParallel`, ` Parallel `, `parallel`), but stored the raw string. Inference in `crates/constraints/src/auto.rs` compares those strings case-insensitively against `ConstraintKind::name()`, so the `gc` prefix and padding never matched and AUTOCONSTRAIN silently added nothing.

Changes:
- `constraintsettings` now stores `kind_from_name(n)`'s canonical `name()` (e.g. `Parallel`). Unknown names are still dropped, as before.
- AUTOCONSTRAIN's per-command `types` override takes the same spellings: recognised names are canonicalised; unrecognised strings pass through unchanged, as before.

Test: `auto_types_spellings_are_stored_canonically` runs the issue's two near-parallel lines (1 degree tolerance) for `gcParallel`, ` Parallel ` and `parallel`. It checks the stored `autoTypes`, then checks that both the settings path and the `types` override add one Parallel constraint. It fails on main for `gcParallel` and ` Parallel `.

title: Keep an ordinate dimension's datum fixed when its feature moves (#105)
author: MarekSpodBiedry
body:
Fixes #105.

An ordinate dimension associates only its feature point (`p13`). When the attached geometry moved, `assoc::recompute` treated the single attached point's delta as a rigid move and carried every unattached definition point with it, including the ordinate's `defpt`, which is its datum (the drawing origin). The datum moved by the same amount as the feature, so the displayed coordinate stayed at its old value (5 instead of 8 in the issue's repro).

The fix excludes `defpt` from the rigid-move carry for `DimKind::Ordinate` only. The leader endpoint and the text still follow the feature, as before. Other dimension kinds are unchanged (the two-association linear control from the issue still translates as a whole). Both entry paths (`dimordinate` with parameters and the interactive DIMORDINATE) create the same origin datum and are updated by the same `recompute`, so one change covers both.

Test: `moving_the_object_keeps_the_ordinate_datum` in `annotate_tests.rs` reproduces the issue (line endpoint at X=5, ordinate, move the line by 3). It checks that the feature and leader follow to `[8,5]`/`[8,8]`, the datum stays at the origin, and the rendered value is `8.0000`. Without the fix the datum moves to `[3,0]` and the value stays `5.0000`.

title: Linux: default to XWayland for file drag-and-drop on Wayland desktops
author: dylanmtaylor
body:
### Rationale & History

Under Wayland sessions, dragging and dropping files from desktop file managers onto the window showed a "no" (prohibited) cursor and drops did not function.

This occurs because `eframe 0.36.2` depends on `winit 0.30.13`. In `winit 0.30`, Wayland drag-and-drop was not implemented ([winit#1881](https://github.com/rust-windowing/winit/issues/1881)). Native Wayland drag-and-drop was implemented for `winit 0.31` in [winit#4571](https://github.com/rust-windowing/winit/pull/4571) (merged July 2026, tagged in `0.31.0-beta.3`). However, bumping to `winit 0.31` is blocked by breaking event loop API changes until upstream `eframe` adds support.

On X11 / XWayland, drag-and-drop is fully supported in `winit 0.30`. This pull request adopts the established pattern from `designcraft` and `deckcraft` by Brandon Thomas:
1. Adds `winit = { version = "0.30", default-features = false, features = ["x11"] }` under `cfg(all(unix, not(target_os = "macos")))`.
2. Adds an event loop builder hook before running the native event loop: when an X server is reachable (`DISPLAY` is set) and `CADCRAFT_WAYLAND` is not set, configures `EventLoopBuilderExtX11::with_x11()` to route through XWayland so file drops work out of the box on standard Wayland desktop sessions.
3. Allows users desiring pure native Wayland to opt out and preserve the native Wayland backend by setting `CADCRAFT_WAYLAND=1`.

### Verification
Verified local compilation and dependency resolution with `cargo check -p cadcraft` on Linux (0 errors, 0 warnings).

title: DXF/DWG: keep hatch gradients through save and reopen (fixes #80)
author: vangel76
body:
Fixes #80.

## The problem

The HATCH writer (`dxf_write.rs`) never wrote `Hatch.gradient`, and the reader (`dxf_read.rs`) always set `gradient: None`. So a hatch made with GRADIENT reopened as a plain `SOLID` hatch after any DXF or DWG save. The boundary survived, so entity counts didn't show the loss — which is why `gradient.dxf` and `solid.dxf` were byte-identical in the report.

DWG has a second cause. DWG saves convert our DXF with the acadrust bridge. Our DXF says `AC1015` (R2000), and an R2000 DWG has no gradient fields. acadrust reads the native gradient groups correctly and keeps them when the DXF says AC1018 or newer, but drops them for AC1015.

## Changes

The writer emits the native HATCH groups from the DXF Reference after the seed points:

| Group | Value |
|---|---|
| 450 / 451 | 1 (gradient) / 0 |
| 460 | angle, radians |
| 461 | shift: 0.0 when centered, 1.0 when not |
| 452 / 462 | 0 (two-colour) / 0.0 tint |
| 453 | 2 colours |
| 463 + 63 + 421 | per colour: index 0.0/1.0, ACI, and true colour when there is one |
| 470 | gradient name |

It also writes a `CADCRAFT` xdata copy: `1000 GRADIENT`, the name (cut to 255 bytes at a character boundary), `1040` angle, `1070` centered, and both colour names. This copy is what survives the R2000 DWG conversion, the same way our dimension and table xdata already does (`dwg_roundtrip_keeps_extension_data`).

The reader prefers the native groups whenever a 450 group is present (another program may have edited them) and falls back to the xdata otherwise. A true colour wins over its ACI fallback. Hostile values (NaN angles, out-of-range colours, extra colour records, missing groups) fall back to the GRADIENT command's defaults.

## Limits

- The file stays R2000 (`AC1015`). Native gradient groups are formally R2004+, but readers that know them (acadrust, for one) pick them up. In the DWG output, the gradient travels only in CADCraft's xdata.
- Hatch `origin` and `background` still aren't written; separate, not re…

title: HATCH/GRADIENT/BOUNDARY: keep islands drawn as separate lines (fixes #106)
author: vangel76
body:
Fixes #106.

## The problem

Picking an internal point traced the outer boundary from all curves (`geom::region`), but islands came only from single closed objects (circle, closed polyline, full ellipse, closed spline). A square drawn as four LINEs inside a rectangle was therefore ignored: HATCH drew pattern lines through it, GRADIENT filled all 400 units, and BOUNDARY created only the outer polyline. The same square as a closed polyline worked.

## Changes

- `geom::region::boundary_at` returns the outer loop plus its islands: every connected group of curves inside the picked face that doesn't touch the face's boundary and doesn't surround the pick point. Each island is the outline of the group's outside, traced with the same sharpest-turn walk as the outer boundary (from the group's leftmost vertex, after pruning dangling ends), and it reports which input curves it came from. `enclosing_loop` is now a thin wrapper.
- `loops_at`, shared by HATCH, GRADIENT and BOUNDARY, adds those islands when every curve in the group is an open LINE, ARC, elliptical arc, open polyline or open spline. Groups that contain a closed object keep the existing per-object islands, so closed-polyline, circle and ellipse islands are unchanged (bulges kept).
- Hostile input: island traces are bounded by the group's edge count, islands per boundary by `MAX_ISLANDS` (4096), and input segments by the existing `MAX_SEGMENTS`, now also checked while collecting.

## Limits

- HATCH with `handles` (select objects) still only accepts closed objects, so selecting the four separate LINEs still gives no island. That path is separate from point picking and is left for a follow-up.
- Blocks, text, solids and other non-curve objects don't form traced islands; their behaviour is unchanged.

## Test plan

- [x] New engine tests, failing on `main`:
  - `hatch_pick_point_keeps_island_of_separate_lines` — rendered pattern never enters the hole, JSON and interactive.
  - `gradient_pick_point_keeps_island_of_sepa…

title: cadcraft-cli mcp: --connect without HOST:PORT is an error, not a headless session (fixes #103)
author: vangel76
body:
Fixes #103.

## The problem

`cadcraft-cli mcp` chose its backend with `position("--connect")` followed by `get(i + 1)`. A `--connect` with no value got `None` — the same as leaving the flag out — so it fell back to a headless session. A client meant to drive the app then got successful edits in a separate drawing, and the process exited 0. The same parser took whatever came next as the address (`--connect --foo`) and silently ignored unknown arguments, so a typo like `--conect 127.0.0.1:7979` also ended up headless.

## Changes

The `mcp` arguments now go through `parse_mcp_args`, which returns `Headless` or `Connect(addr)`:

| Invocation | Before | After |
|---|---|---|
| `mcp` | headless | headless |
| `mcp --connect 127.0.0.1:7979` | connects | connects |
| `mcp --connect` | **headless, exit 0** | `--connect needs HOST:PORT (…)`, exit 1 |
| `mcp --connect ""` / `"  "` | `cannot connect to : invalid socket address` | `--connect needs HOST:PORT (…)`, exit 1 |
| `mcp --connect --foo` | tried to connect to `--foo` | `--connect needs HOST:PORT (…)`, exit 1 |
| `mcp --conect ADDR`, `mcp ADDR` | **headless, exit 0** | `mcp: unknown argument …` plus the usage text, exit 1 |
| `--connect A --connect B` | used A | `--connect given more than once`, exit 1 |
| unreachable address | `cannot connect to …`, exit 1 | unchanged |

Every error happens before the server reads stdin, so nothing on stdout is answered. Nothing documents a default control port (`cadcraft --control` has none), so the CLI reports an error instead of guessing one. `docs/mcp.md` now says what happens without an address. The `mcp` startup moved into its own `fn mcp`, returning `Result` instead of an early `return`.

## Test plan

- [x] Parser unit tests in `cadcraft-cli`: `mcp_without_connect_is_headless`, `mcp_connect_with_address_selects_remote`, `mcp_connect_without_address_is_an_error_not_headless`, `mcp_rejects_unknown_and_repeated_arguments`.
- [x] New `apps/cadcraft-cli/tests/mcp_connect.rs` runs th…

title: LINE: deferred tangent/perpendicular for the first point, so belt lines tangent to two circles work (fixes #69)
author: vangel76
body:
Fixes #69.

## The problem

Tangent and perpendicular snaps are computed from the prompt's base point (`snap.rs`). The first point of a LINE has no base yet, so it could never snap tangent, and there was no way to draw a line tangent to two circles (a belt). Even with a candidate, the click reached the command as a plain point, so the command could not tell which curve was meant.

## Changes

As in AutoCAD, the first point can now be a *deferred* tangent (or perpendicular), resolved once the line's other end is known.

- **Snap:** with no base, and only where the prompt says it can resolve them, osnap offers "Deferred Tangent" (circles, arcs) and "Deferred Perpendicular" (circles, arcs, lines, xlines, rays). These only win where no other snap does, so quadrant, endpoint and the rest still take precedence. The hit carries the curve (`SnapHit::deferred`).
- **Solver:** `snap::resolve_deferred` finds the line:

  | First point | Other end | Line |
  |---|---|---|
  | TAN circle/arc | point | tangent from the point |
  | PER circle/line | point | perpendicular from the point |
  | TAN | TAN | common tangent of the two circles (new `Circle::common_tangents` in geom: 2 outer, 2 crossed) |
  | TAN | PER | tangent along the normal of the line, or through the center of the circle |
  | PER | PER | through both centers, through a center along the normal of the line, or between parallel lines |

  When several lines fit, the one closest to where the curves were picked wins. No solution (point inside the circle, concentric or nested circles, non-parallel lines, non-finite input) returns `None`, never a panic.
- **Prompt-level, opt-in:** `Prompt::deferred()` marks prompts that resolve deferred snaps, and `Input::Deferred` carries the pick. At any other prompt the session turns it into the point it was picked at, so other commands are unchanged. LINE is the only user so far.
- **LINE:** the first point (and the next one while the first is still deferred) accepts deferred snaps. N…

title: DXF: write non-ASCII text as \U+ escapes so R2000 files read correctly elsewhere (fixes #164)
author: vangel76
body:
Fixes #164.

## The problem

The DXF writer declares `$ACADVER AC1015` (R2000) and `$DWGCODEPAGE ANSI_1252`. Before R2007, DXF text is in the code page, not UTF-8 — but `cadcraft_dxf::write_ascii` wrote strings as raw UTF-8, so other readers (ezdxf, and any code-page-aware reader) decoded `图号` as `å›¾å·`. CADCraft read its own files back fine because its reader tries UTF-8 first, which hid the bug.

## Changes

The header and the R2000 structure don't change; only the bytes of string values do.

- `write_ascii` now writes pure ASCII. Every non-ASCII character in a string group becomes the pre-R2007 `\U+XXXX` escape; characters above U+FFFF become a surrogate pair of escapes (`😀` → `\U+D83D\U+DE00`). The file is valid under any code page, and since it's done in `write_ascii` it covers TEXT, MTEXT, ATTRIB/ATTDEF, layer, style and block names, dimension text, xdata and XRECORD strings.
- The reader requires exactly four hex digits, combines surrogate pairs, and keeps malformed escapes and unpaired surrogates as literal text. It now also unescapes strings in binary DXF.
- DWG save is unchanged: the DXF still goes to acadrust as R2000, and acadrust decodes the escapes. A new test checks that CJK, Latin-1 and astral text survive DXF → DWG → DXF.

I kept R2000 instead of declaring AC1021+, so DWG output and the other writers' assumptions stay the same. `dxf_write.rs` / `dxf_read.rs` are untouched.

## Limits

- The reader still ignores `$DWGCODEPAGE`: non-UTF-8 bytes are read as Latin-1, as before. Real CP1252 (0x80–0x9F) and other code pages (936, 932, …) are a separate issue.
- The ATTDEF prompt (group 3) isn't written to DXF — a separate, pre-existing bug (#81).
- Escaped strings are longer on disk. MTEXT chunks are split before escaping, so an escape is never split.

## Test plan

- [x] New `non_ascii_text_is_escaped_for_r2000_and_roundtrips` (io, fails on `main`): TEXT, MTEXT, layer name, block name and ATTRIB/ATTDEF with CJK, Latin-1 and an astral character; output i…

title: CLI: image exports honour the current view; add --window / --view framing (fixes #165)
author: vangel76
body:
Fixes #165.

## The problem

`convert` and `run --export` always fitted the model-space extents. The CLI's `export()` called `cadcraft_io::write(drawing, out)`, which never sees the session's view, so `zoom`, `pan` or `view.set` in a run produced a byte-identical image, and there was no way to export a region short of erasing entities.

## Changes

| Command | Default framing | Explicit |
|---|---|---|
| `convert IN OUT.(png\|svg\|pdf)` | fit the extents (unchanged) | `--window x0,y0,x1,y1`, `--view extents\|current` |
| `run … --export OUT.(png\|svg\|pdf)` | the current view **if the script/commands changed it** (zoom, pan, view.set…), otherwise fit the extents (unchanged) | same |

- **io:** `write_framed(drawing, name, window)` frames PNG, SVG and PDF on a model-space rectangle: centred, fitted without margin and without distortion. `write()` delegates with no window, and its output is unchanged. DXF/DWG ignore the window. `PdfOptions` gains `window` (model space only).
- **Validation:** `check_window` rejects non-finite, inverted, zero-size and out-of-range (±1e12) windows, and sides smaller than 1e-9 of the coordinate magnitude. The CLI parser adds clear messages for malformed `--window` text. Hostile input is an error, never a panic. `--window` together with `--view`, or framing options with DXF/DWG output, are errors too.
- **Why "changed by the commands" rather than "always the session view":** a freshly opened drawing's view is its extents plus 10%. Using it unconditionally would silently change every default export. Comparing the model-space view before and after the run's steps keeps plain runs as they were, and makes `zoom` do what you'd expect.
- **Selection:** `select …` then `zoom {"mode":"object"}` frames the selection set, since ZOOM Object falls back to the selection. Documented and tested.
- `--help` and the README describe how images are framed.

## Limits

- Exporting *only* the selected entities (hiding the rest) is out of scope; the issue's co…

title: MCP plate test: finish TEXT before undo and check the centre line survives
author: vangel76
body:
Fixes #51.

## The problem

`agent_draws_a_plate_with_holes` scripts `TEXT 0,-10 5 0 PLATE 100x60\n`. TEXT works the way it does in AutoCAD: after each line it asks for another one and only finishes on an empty Enter. A single trailing newline doesn't produce that Enter, so TEXT was still running (`running: "text"`, `TEXT Enter text:`) when the test ran `undo`.

An interactive command only pushes its undo snapshot when it finishes. So `undo` popped the previous snapshot, the centre line's, and took the uncommitted text with it. The only post-undo check was "no Text", so the test passed even though the centre line was gone.

## Changes

Test-only (`crates/mcp/src/tests.rs`):

- The script ends TEXT with a blank line (`...PLATE 100x60\n\n`). The `script` tool documents a blank line as Enter, and an AutoCAD `.scr` file finishes TEXT the same way. The test now asserts that no command is running after the script.
- After undo, the test checks:
  - that exactly `["Single Line Text"]` was undone
  - that there is no Text
  - that there are still 4 Circles, 1 Polyline and 1 Line
  - that `query_entities {type: Line, layer: Center}` still finds the centre line

I checked that the new assertions catch the bug: with the old single-newline script, the test fails at the post-undo `Line` count (`left: Null, right: 1`).

## Limits

- The script path isn't buggy here. `Session::script` already turns a blank line into Enter, and TEXT asking for more lines matches the reference behaviour. I left it unchanged.
- I didn't change undo semantics, as the issue scopes it. Possible follow-up: a programmatic `undo` (`execute {"command":"undo"}`) while an interactive command is running pops the *previous* command's snapshot. It discards the running command's uncommitted entities, and the command keeps running with a stale `before` snapshot. Cancelling or finishing the running command first, or refusing, might be the better contract. That's a separate decision, not part of this test fix.

title: Ask Save / Don't Save / Cancel before closing a dirty drawing
author: vangel76
body:
Fixes #124.

## The problem

File ▸ Close, a file tab's × and File ▸ Close All call the engine's `close` / `closeall` straight away, and those just remove the drawing. Nothing checks for unsaved changes on any platform. The report is about the web build, but the desktop build has the same problem; it isn't a native dialog that's compiled out on wasm. There was never a prompt.

## Changes

One in-app egui modal, the same on desktop and web. There's no native message box on the web, and a single code path keeps both builds consistent and testable without a window.

- New `crates/ui-egui/src/closing.rs`. A close request from the UI becomes a queue of drawings, tracked by `DocState::uid` so the indices stay valid as tabs close. Clean drawings close right away. When the queue reaches a dirty drawing, that drawing becomes active and the app asks **"Save changes to X?"** with **Save / Don't Save / Cancel**. Escape counts as Cancel. Colours come from `theme::Tokens`.
  - **Cancel** keeps the drawing and its edits and stops the request.
  - **Don't Save** closes the drawing.
  - **Save** goes through the existing `qsave` path (untitled drawings get the host's save picker). The drawing closes only if it is clean afterwards. If the picker was cancelled, the save failed, or there's no picker (the web today, see #133), the drawing stays open and a status/command-line message says it wasn't saved.
  - **Close All** goes through the tabs in order and asks about each dirty drawing. Cancel stops it there; drawings that were already closed stay closed.
- `menus::run_ui_command` sends `close` / `closeall` to the prompt when they're called with null params (menu, native macOS menu, typed CLOSE/CLOSEALL, `ui.menu.invoke`). This follows the existing `layer` / `qselect` pattern. The tab × calls `CadApp::request_close(Some(i))`.

title: Fonts: per-character fallback, FONTALT and .ttc support for CJK text in SHX styles
author: vangel76
body:
Fixes #130. Covers requests 1 (SHX → TTF fallback) and 2 (`.ttc` in the font scan). Native SHX and big-font rendering (request 3) stays on the roadmap (M4) and is out of scope here.

## The problem

A style such as `romans.shx` + big font `chineset.shx` resolves to our stroke font (`ttf::find` returns `None` for `.shx`), and the stroke font has no CJK glyphs, so every ideograph was drawn as the missing-glyph box. The font scan also skipped `.ttc`/`.otc`, which is where most CJK system fonts live (macOS, Noto CJK, WenQuanYi, Windows `msjh.ttc`/`msyh.ttc`).

## Changes

**Per-character fallback** (`crates/fonts`). When a text's font lacks a character, the glyph now comes from an installed font that has it, checked by cmap and not by name. This works for both the stroke font and TrueType fonts.
- Fonts with wide coverage are tried first: Noto Sans CJK, Source Han, WenQuanYi, Droid Sans Fallback, PingFang, Hiragino, STHeiti, Microsoft JhengHei/YaHei, Yu Gothic, MS Gothic, Malgun, SimSun, MingLiU, then others. Regular weights come before bold, light and so on.
- Fallback glyphs are sized like TrueType text in CADCraft (cap height = text height), and their advances go into `line_width`/`text_width`, so alignment and MTEXT wrapping stay consistent.
- Results are cached per character. Each search is bounded: at most 24 files and 160 MiB loaded, 256 faces checked per character, and no file over 96 MiB is read. Spaces, control characters and private-use code points never trigger a search.
- If no installed font has the character, it is drawn as a box, as before.

**Font substitution settings.** These are process-wide, like AutoCAD's profile variables, and are never saved in the drawing:

| Sysvar | Seeded from | Meaning |
|---|---|---|
| `FONTALT` | `CADCRAFT_FONTALT` | Font used for a style font that can't be found (an SHX file, a missing TTF). Empty (the default) = our stroke font. |
| `FONTFALLBACK` | `CADCRAFT_FONTFALLBACK` | Comma-separated list of fonts tried first for …

title: Entity transparency: set it in properties.set, report it, round-trip DXF group 440
author: vangel76
body:
Fixes #132.

> Related to #131 (layer transparency). Both use the same alpha ↔ percentage mapping. This PR doesn't add #131's `transparency_to_dxf` / `transparency_from_dxf`. It keeps two small entity-level functions next to the entity common groups in `dxf_write.rs` / `dxf_read.rs`, so the two PRs don't touch the same lines and merge cleanly in either order. Once #131 lands, the alpha math in those two functions can call its helpers.

## The problem

Per-object transparency was missing from start to finish:

- `properties.set` listed `transparency?` in its params but `run_set` never read it. It answered `{"changed":1}` and left the entity at ByLayer.
- Neither `properties` nor `drawing.inspect` reported it. The palette's Transparency row was a fixed "ByLayer" box.
- No entity wrote DXF group 440, and the reader ignored it.

- **`properties.set`** takes `transparency`: `"ByLayer"`, `"ByBlock"` or a percentage 0–90, given as a number or a string (`"50"`, `"50%"`). Fractions round to the nearest percent. title: DWG open: stop runaway conversions early and name the limit (#57)
author: vangel76
body:
Refs #57 — makes the failure fast and accurate; it does not make the reporter's file open (that looks like acadrust inflating the file, which can't be confirmed without it), so I left the issue open.

## The problem

`file too large` is `DxfError::TooLarge`, the DXF reader's cap of 50,000,000 group codes (`MAX_TAGS`). It isn't a file-size limit. A DWG is opened by converting it to DXF text with acadrust and parsing that text, and the cap was only checked at the very end of that chain:

1. acadrust reads the whole DWG,
2. writes all of its DXF text into one `Vec` (`write_to_vec`),
3. `decode_text` copies the text into a `String`,
4. the parser allocates 50 million tags and only then gives up.

That's where the ~2 minutes and the memory went before the misleading message.

A real 10 MB DWG doesn't come close to the cap. A synthetic AutoCAD 2010 (AC1024) file of 10.0 MB (125,000 entities, generated with our own writer through the bridge) converts to 58 MB of DXF, which is 3.7 million group codes. It opens in about 2 s on `main` already. Mixes with blocks, attributes, MTEXT and 800 layers give the same ratio, about 0.4 group codes per DWG byte. The reporter's file needed more than 5 per byte, so it isn't a size problem. The DWG reader is producing far more drawing than the file contains.

That happens when acadrust misreads data. It caps every count it reads at 100,000 and returns zeros when it reads past the end of the data, so one desynchronised object turns into a polyline with up to 100,000 vertices. Bit flips in a 0.25 MB AC1024 file are enough: acadrust took 8 s and 5.3 GB to read it and then wrote **11 GB** of DXF, nearly all of it LWPOLYLINE vertices. The 2.1 MB AC1015 file in the report works and the 9.9 MB AC1024 one doesn't, which fits a reader problem specific to the R2007+ format. Without the file I can't tell which object it is.

## Changes

- **cadcraft-dwg**: new `Limits { max_dwg_bytes: 512 MB, max_dxf_bytes: 1 GB }` and `dwg_to_dxf_with(bytes, limits)`…

title: fix(engine): programmatic undo/redo ends a running command first
author: vangel76
body:
Fixes #177.

## The problem

Interactive commands push their undo step only when they end (`Session::finish`). A programmatic `undo` (`engine.execute`, MCP `execute`, the control channel, or `undo {}` in a script) run while a command was still active, such as TEXT waiting for another line, popped the *previous* command's step instead. That removed the earlier geometry and dropped the running command's entities, and the command kept running from a stale `before` snapshot. `redo` swapped the drawing under the running command in the same way.

## Changes

- `crates/engine/src/cmd/edit.rs`: `run_undo` and `run_redo` now end a running command the way Esc does (`Session::cancel`) before they undo or redo.

  This is the behaviour Cmd+Z, the Edit menu, the toolbar and a typed `u` already have: they go through `Session::start`, which cancels the active non-transparent command first. Cancelling keeps what the command already drew as one undo step (as Esc does for LINE/TEXT), so `undo` removes that step and the earlier geometry stays. I chose this over refusing with an error: it doesn't add a second rule only for programmatic calls, and agents don't need to send an extra `cancel` first.
- `crates/engine/src/tests.rs`: regression test `programmatic_undo_during_a_command_ends_it_first`. It draws a line, leaves TEXT active with one line of text, and runs `undo`: TEXT has ended and only the line is left. Then `redo` restores the text, and `redo` while TEXT is active ends it without touching the entities.

This also makes the original sequence in `agent_draws_a_plate_with_holes` (#51) undo just the text. #171 is still a valid test fix either way.

## Test plan

- [x] `cargo test -p cadcraft-engine`: 135 passed. Without the `edit.rs` change, the new test fails (line removed, TEXT still running).
- [x] `cargo test -p cadcraft-mcp`: 3 passed
- [x] `cargo clippy -p cadcraft-engine --all-targets -- -D warnings`: clean
- [x] `cargo fmt --all -- --check`: clean
- [ ] I didn't run `cargo …

title: Light and System interface themes (System follows the OS appearance live)
author: vangel76
body:
Fixes #59.

## The problem

CADCraft had a single, hard-coded dark interface. `Tokens::get()` always returned `Tokens::DARK`, the app installed `Visuals::dark()` once at startup, and there was no theme choice. So it stayed dark when macOS (or another OS) was in Light mode.

## Changes

**Palettes** (`theme.rs`)
- New `Tokens::LIGHT`: light grey chrome with dark text. `Tokens::DARK` is unchanged.
- `Tokens::get()` returns the palette of the theme in use. That theme is a UI-thread thread-local, set once per frame in `CadApp::logic`. No `unsafe`.
- `theme::apply(ctx, theme)` builds both of egui's styles from the tokens and switches egui to the theme shown. Standard widgets, menus, popups and dialogs follow it, along with everything we paint ourselves: title/tool bar, menu bar, file tabs, Tool Sets, Layers/Properties palettes, command line and status bar.
- Hard-coded colours that bypassed the tokens now go through them:
  - the command line's history panel, border, keywords and keyword hover, and the AutoComplete list
  - the status-bar message colour
  - the layer status icon

In `DARK` they hold the exact values that were hard-coded, so Dark looks as before. The one exception is the layer status icon, which now uses `icon`/`text_faint`. That shifts its colour by a few RGB units.
- **The drawing area keeps its model-space colours in both themes:** canvas background, grid, axes, selection, grips, snap markers, selection windows, ViewCube and UCS icon. AutoCAD-style apps treat the model-space background as a drawing setting, separate from the interface theme, and the issue lists it as a non-goal. `LIGHT` takes these colours from `DARK` (`..Tokens::DARK`). title: Command line, ViewCube and UCS icon take the pointer; command history window (F2)
author: vangel76
body:
Fixes #136. Part of #7.

## The problem

The command line, the UCS icon and most of the ViewCube didn't react to the mouse. Reproduced on Linux 0.4.0 with real pointer events over the control channel:

- **Command line:** the history lines and the chevron were only painted, with no widget behind them. Clicking the history went through to the drawing and started a selection window. While a command was running it would have entered a point instead. The chevron did nothing, and there was no way to see more history.
- **UCS icon:** also only painted. A click on it started a selection window in the drawing.
- **ViewCube:** only the Top face was a widget, and it only sensed clicks. In egui, a click-only widget on top of the canvas (which senses clicks and drags) leaves the canvas hovered underneath. So the crosshair was drawn over the cube, the wheel zoomed the drawing, and the compass ring and the "WCS ⌄" pill were dead (clicks went to the drawing). The face itself did zoom to extents.

The root cause is the same for all three. An overlay only keeps the pointer away from the canvas if it registers a widget that senses clicks **and** drags (egui's hit test then makes it the top click and drag target). Most overlays registered nothing.

## Changes

- **Pointer routing.** Each overlay registers a click-and-drag widget over its area: the whole command line (bar, history, AutoComplete list), the ViewCube, the WCS pill and the UCS icon's arms. Keyword and AutoComplete buttons sit on top of the command-line widget, so they keep working. The canvas no longer picks, starts windows, enters points or zooms under an overlay, and the normal arrow cursor shows there instead of the crosshair.
- **Command history** (`cmdline.rs`):
  - A click on the history lines or on the chevron opens a history window. It's scrollable, shows the whole log with the newest line at the bottom, and is at most half the drawing area tall. The chevron now points up when the window is closed and down when it'…

title: Linux: present without a vsync queue so the crosshair follows the mouse (#25)
author: vangel76
body:
Refs #25.

> This touches `apps/cadcraft/src/main.rs` in different places from #159 (XWayland default) and #122 (DX12 on Windows). `git merge-tree` is clean against both branches. The two changes work together: with #159, Wayland desktops also run through XWayland, which has the same three-image swapchain minimum as X11.

## The problem

Over the canvas, CADCraft hides the OS pointer and draws its own crosshair. So every frame the swapchain holds back shows up as lag between the mouse and the crosshair. Two things made that queue longer on Linux X11 (Linux Mint's Cinnamon session) than on Windows:

1. **The vsync queue is two frames deep on X11.** eframe already asks wgpu for FIFO with `desired_maximum_frame_latency = 1`. On Vulkan, wgpu-hal turns that into the swapchain image count (`latency + 1`), clamped to the driver's minimum. The X11 surface on this machine reports `minImageCount = 3` (NVIDIA under XWayland, from `vulkaninfo`), so the request for 1 queued frame becomes 2. On Windows, DX12 honours 1 (`SetMaximumFrameLatency`). As far as I know Mesa's X11 WSI also reports 3, but I haven't checked that here.
2. **The canvas called `request_repaint()` on every frame while the pointer was over it**, even with the mouse still. That kept the FIFO queue full all the time, so new input always waited behind queued frames. It also kept the app at 60 fps while idle.

I measured a third, smaller cost: the hover and selection highlight scanned the whole display list on every frame. On a 270k-entity drawing that took about 2.5 ms per frame whenever the pointer rested on an entity.

## Changes

- `gpu::surface_config` (ui-egui) picks the present mode. On Linux/BSD it uses `AutoNoVsync`: wgpu tries Immediate, then Mailbox, then FIFO, so it works on every surface. Frame latency stays at 1. Under a compositor (Cinnamon, KDE, GNOME), the compositor still syncs to the display, so frames don't tear. `CADCRAFT_VSYNC=1` switches back to vsync. `CADCRAFT_VSYNC=0` turns on the low-late…

title: IMPORT, EXPORT, Plot Preview and Batch Publish; ATTACH, SHARE, 3DORBIT say not available yet (part of #9)
author: vangel76
body:
Part of #9.

Four of the seven commands work now: IMPORT, EXPORT, PREVIEW (Plot Preview) and PUBLISH (Batch Publish). ATTACH, SHARE and 3DORBIT still need features CADCraft doesn't have, so they now say "not available yet" instead of "unknown command". See Limits.

## The problem

The tool bar has Import, Export, Attach, Share, Batch Publish, Plot Preview and Orbit buttons (Orbit is also in the View tool set). None of these commands was registered, so each click printed `unknown command`. The File menu had no Import, Export or Batch Publish either.

## Changes

New engine module `crates/engine/src/cmd/exchange.rs`. The UI side is in the new `crates/ui-egui/src/exchange.rs`. Typed at the command line, chosen from a menu or clicked on the tool bar, EXPORT, IMPORT and PUBLISH ask for a file and PREVIEW opens a window. JSON calls (`app.run`, control channel, MCP, scripts) run the command directly and never open a dialog.

| Command | What it does now |
|---|---|
| `export` (File > Export..., alias `EXP`) | `{path?, format?: dxf\|dwg\|svg\|png\|pdf}`: writes the drawing in that format through the existing io hooks (`cadcraft_io::write`). The format comes from `format` or from the path's extension. Without `path` it returns base64 `data`. Unlike SAVEAS, it leaves the drawing's file name and title alone. The file is written to a temp file first and then renamed. Typed or from the menu/tool bar, it opens the save dialog with `<drawing>.svg` filled in. |
| `import` (File > Import..., alias `IMP`) | `{path \| data+name, at?, scale?}`: reads another DXF or DWG and copies its model space into the current space. Objects are scaled about the origin, then moved to `at`. It brings along the layers, linetypes, text/dimension/multileader/table styles and blocks those objects use. Where a name already exists, this drawing's definition is kept. Generated `*U`/`*D` blocks whose names collide are given new names. Every imported object gets a fresh handle, and associative dimension links …

title: Option to keep the system cursor over the drawing area for screen magnifiers (#39)
author: vangel76
body:
Refs #39.

Windows Magnifier (and other tools that follow the mouse pointer) can now track the pointer over the drawing area, once you turn on **View > Accessibility > Show System Cursor** or start CADCraft with `CADCRAFT_SYSTEM_CURSOR=1`. It is off by default, so this PR doesn't close the issue on its own. See Limits.

**To use it with Windows Magnifier:** choose **View > Accessibility > Show System Cursor**. To have it on at every start, run `setx CADCRAFT_SYSTEM_CURSOR 1` once in a command prompt, then start CADCraft again.

## The problem

Over the drawing area the canvas asks egui for `CursorIcon::None` and draws its own crosshair (`crates/ui-egui/src/canvas.rs`). egui-winit 0.36.2 turns `CursorIcon::None` into `window.set_cursor_visible(false)`. On Windows, winit 0.30.13 then calls `ShowCursor(FALSE)` (`platform_impl/windows/util.rs`, `set_cursor_hidden`). With the system cursor hidden, Magnifier set to "follow the mouse pointer" or "keep the mouse pointer centered" loses it, so the magnified view stops following (as shown in the issue's video). Screen recorders and remote desktop clients can lose it the same way.

The app doesn't warp, confine or grab the cursor anywhere (no `CursorGrab`, `CursorPosition` or `set_cursor_position`). Hiding it is the only cause I found.

## Changes

- New UI setting `UiState::system_cursor` (`systemCursor` in `ui.set`). When it is on, the canvas asks for `CursorIcon::Crosshair` instead of `None`. The small system crosshair sits at the centre of CADCraft's drawn crosshair, and the drawn crosshair, pickbox and dynamic input are unchanged.
- **View > Accessibility > Show System Cursor** toggles it (UI command `ui.toggle.systemcursor`, `{"on": bool}` like the other `ui.toggle.*` commands).
- `CADCRAFT_SYSTEM_CURSOR=1` (anything except empty, `0`, `false` or `off`) turns it on at startup. It is read as the setting's default, so **Window > Reset Palettes** keeps it. On the web the variable doesn't exist and the setting stays off.
- R…

title: Reject layer.set atomically: a refused call no longer applies other changes (#71)
author: MarekSpodBiedry
body:
Fixes #71.

`run_set` called `apply()` on the live layer before the current-layer freeze check, so a combined `{"frozen": true, "color": 1}` request on the current layer returned an error but still changed the colour (only `frozen` was reset). The same was true of a rejected rename (layer 0 / Defpoints, invalid name). Because the command took `doc_mut()` before validating, `Session::execute` also saw a changed drawing and recorded a "Set Layer Properties" undo step for the failed call.

Now `layer.set` validates everything on a copy of the layer, read through `s.doc()`, and takes `doc_mut()` only after the freeze-current and rename checks pass. A refused call:
- leaves the layer exactly as it was (colour, frozen state, everything else),
- adds no undo step, so the circle render and undo history stay unchanged, and nothing reaches a later DXF save.

Valid edits behave as before: colour-only edits on the current layer, and combined colour/freeze edits on a non-current layer, still apply. Renames still re-point entities and `CLAYER`.

Test: `rejected_layer_set_changes_nothing` covers the rejected freeze-current and the rejected rename of layer 0, each sent with a colour change. For each one it checks that the layer is unchanged and the undo history length is the same. It then checks that a colour-only edit of the current layer still applies. On `main` it fails because the colour is changed.

title: Layer delete and purge keep layers used by block definitions (#72)
author: MarekSpodBiedry
body:
Fixes #72.

`layer.delete` and `purge` decided whether a layer was in use by looking only at model space and layout entities. A layer whose only objects live inside a block definition was treated as empty: `layer.delete` removed it and `purge` dropped it, leaving the block's entities on a layer that no longer exists.

Changes:

- `layer.delete` (`crates/engine/src/cmd/layer.rs`): the "layer has objects on it" check now also looks at the entities of every block definition.
- `purge` (`crates/engine/src/cmd/blocks.rs`): the layer pass now uses the existing `layer::used_layers()`, which already covers model, layouts and block definitions (it is what `layer` uses for its `used` flag). It runs after unused blocks are removed, so a layer used only by a purged block is still purged in the same run.

Test: `delete_and_purge_keep_layers_used_by_block_definitions` puts a line on layer A, turns it into block B (originals deleted), inserts B on layer 0, then checks that `layer.delete A` fails and that `purge` keeps A. It fails on main at both steps.

title: Reject two-line angular constraints over 180 degrees that can never be satisfied (#73)
author: MarekSpodBiedry
body:
Fixes #73.

A two-line angular constraint measures a signed angle in [-180, 180] (`atan2` of the two directions) and takes its sign from the starting geometry. The residual is wrapped, so a target such as 200 degrees "converges" to -160 degrees: `add` reported success, but `constraints.inspect` then showed the constraint and the drawing as unsatisfied. The range check in `Built::new` allowed up to 360 degrees for every angular form.

The check now uses 180 degrees for two lines and keeps 360 degrees for an arc sweep, which can really reach a full turn. Out-of-range two-line values get the existing `angle out of range` error (the one 361 already got), so `add` fails and leaves the drawing unchanged, as its doc comment promises. This follows the pattern of the other dimensional kinds in `Built::new`, which reject unreachable targets (negative distance, non-positive radius) instead of reinterpreting them.

I chose rejecting over normalising (for example 200 -> -160 or 160) because changing the value silently would store an expression the user did not type, and the issue's restoration check accepts an error that leaves the drawing unchanged.

How the issue's cases are handled:
- `dcangular` and `dimconstraint {"type":"angular"}` at 200 or 181: both go through `cs::add`, so both now return `angle out of range` and change nothing.
- 90 and 180: still accepted and satisfied.
- 361: unchanged, same error.
- Arc sweep constraints: unchanged, up to 360.

Test: `two_line_angle_over_180_is_rejected` adds a 200-degree angle between two lines and checks that it fails, adds no constraint and moves no line, then checks that 180 is still accepted and satisfied. Without the fix the 200-degree `add` returns `Ok` and the test fails.

title: Layer rename re-points paper-space and block-definition entities (#75)
author: MarekSpodBiedry
body:
Fixes #75.

`layer.set` with `newName` (`crates/engine/src/cmd/layer.rs`) renamed the layer and then re-pointed only the entities in `d.model`. Entities in paper-space layouts (`d.layouts[..].entities`) and inside block definitions (`d.blocks[..].entities`) kept the old name. That name was no longer in the layer table, so those entities fell off the renamed layer, the old name was written to DXF, and ByLayer entities in blocks lost the layer colour (red became black in the issue's SVG export).

The re-point loop is now a small `repoint` helper. It runs on model space, on every layout, and on every block definition. Matching is case-insensitive, the same as before. A block is copied (`Arc::make_mut`) only if it has an entity on the renamed layer, so the cheap shared-clone undo snapshots stay shared for blocks the rename does not touch.

The `rename` command (`{table: "layer"}`) calls `layer.set`, so it gets the fix too.

Test `rename_repoints_paper_space_and_block_entities` (in `layer.rs`): it puts a Line on layer `A` into a block definition (`block ... keep: delete`) and a second Line on `A` into `Layout1`, then renames `A` to `B`. It checks that no paper-space or block entity is left on `A` and that both are on `B`. Without the fix, both stay on `A` and the test fails.

title: Keep the active drawing when closing an earlier inactive one (#76)
author: MarekSpodBiedry
body:
Fixes #76.

`run_close` (`crates/engine/src/cmd/file.rs`) removed the drawing from `s.docs` but only clamped `s.active` to the new length. Closing a drawing that sits before the active one shifts every later drawing down by one, so `s.active` ended up pointing at the drawing after the one the user was working in.

The fix decrements `s.active` when the closed index is lower than it. Closing the active drawing itself, or one after it, works as before. `close` is the only place that removes a drawing from `s.docs`, so no other path needs the change.

Tests (in `file.rs`, same style as the `layer.rs` test module):
- `closing_earlier_inactive_drawing_keeps_active_drawing`: the issue's case. Three drawings, switch to `Drawing2`, close index 0; `Drawing2` must still be active. Without the fix `Drawing3` is active and the test fails.
- `closing_later_inactive_drawing_keeps_active_drawing`: control case. Closing a drawing after the active one leaves the active drawing as it was.

title: Deliver browser saves as downloads; keep unsaved state when they fail (#133)
author: vangel76
body:
Fixes #133.

## The problem

On the web, `save`/`qsave`/`saveas` serialized the drawing, skipped the file write (there is no file system in wasm), and then did everything a real save does: marked the drawing saved, set its path and tab title, and returned `{path, bytes}`. The user got a success message and a clean tab, but no file. The web app also has no save picker, so Save and Save As from the menu (and Save in the close prompt) did nothing.

## Changes

- **Engine: a file-delivery hook** (`crates/engine/src/cmd/file.rs`). `file::set_deliver(fn(name, mime, bytes) -> Result<(), String>)` sits next to `set_io`, so the engine stays I/O-agnostic and has no web-sys dependency (layering unchanged). Saving now goes through `store`:
  - native: the atomic temp-file write and rename, as before;
  - wasm: hands the bytes to the delivery hook under the path's file name. If no hook is installed, or the hook reports an error, the save returns an error.
- **Dirty semantics** (`commit_save`). The drawing is marked saved, renamed and retitled only after the bytes were stored. A failed store keeps the unsaved changes, the old path and the old title. On the web a *started* download counts as saved: from there the browser owns the file, and a page can't tell whether the user kept it. The name is kept so later QSAVEs download the drawing again under it. The web result also says what was downloaded: `{path, bytes, download}`.
- **Web: a reusable download helper** (`apps/cadcraft-web/src/download.rs`). `download(name, mime, bytes) -> Result<(), String>` uses web-sys only: a `Blob`, an object URL, and a temporary hidden `<a download>` that is clicked and then removed. The URL is revoked after 60 s, or right away if anything fails. It needs no JS, and it errors instead of panicking when there is no window, document or body. The web app installs it as the engine's delivery hook. New web-sys features: `HtmlAnchorElement`, `Blob`, `BlobPropertyBag`, `Url`. `js_sys` comes through `web_sys::…
