title: Linetype rename keeps layer, object and current-linetype references (#74)
author: MarekSpodBiedry
body:
Fixes #74.

`rename {"table":"linetype"}` only changed the name in the linetype table. Layers, objects and `CELTYPE` still pointed at the old name, which no longer resolved, so dashed lines were drawn solid (also after DXF save and reopen).

The linetype branch of `rename` now works like `style.rename` and `dimstyle.rename`:

- Layer linetypes, `CELTYPE`, and objects with an explicit linetype in model space, every layout and every block definition now use the new name. Objects set to ByLayer stay ByLayer and pick up the renamed pattern from their layer.
- Renaming to a linetype name that already exists is refused ("a linetype `X` already exists"), the same check the style renames use. Before, this produced two table entries with the same name.
- ByBlock, ByLayer and Continuous cannot be renamed, like the Standard style. Without this check, renaming ByLayer would now also rewrite every ByLayer object.

Test: `linetype_rename_updates_references` follows the issue's steps (layer A with DASHED, a ByLayer line, a line with DASHED set explicitly, `CELTYPE` = DASHED) and adds a line inside a block. After the rename to MYDASH it checks every reference, checks that layer 0 keeps Continuous, and checks that both refusals return an error.

title: Respect locked layers in Clear, Cut, Stretch, Trim, Extend, Fillet, Explode and SplineEdit (#87)
author: MarekSpodBiedry
body:
Fixes #87.

Clear, Cut, STRETCH, TRIM, FILLET, EXPLODE and SPLINEDIT changed or removed objects on a locked layer. ERASE, MOVE and grip editing already protected them. This PR adds the same `curves::is_locked` check to each command and follows how the existing commands handle a lock:

- **Skip the locked objects** for commands that work on a set of objects. This is what `erase` and `transform_entities` (Move/Rotate/Scale) do, and `reverse` in `modify2.rs` does the same.
  - Clear (`erase.selection`) and Cut (`cutclip`): locked objects are not erased and are not copied to the clipboard by Cut.
  - STRETCH: both the JSON form and the interactive crossing-window prompt leave locked objects out.
  - EXPLODE: locked objects stay as they are.
- **Return an error ("The object is on a locked layer.")** for commands that edit one picked object. This is the message `pedit` and the grip commands already return.
  - TRIM, EXTEND, FILLET/CHAMFER (lines, curves and the polyline option) and SPLINEDIT.

EXTEND and CHAMFER were not listed in the issue. They share the trim and fillet code paths, so they get the same check.

The new test `editing_commands_leave_locked_layer_objects_alone` (`modify2_tests.rs`) runs each command on locked objects, including the interactive STRETCH, and checks that the drawing does not change. Then it unlocks the layer and checks that the edits work again.

title: Keep viewport layer colour overrides through DXF save and reopen (#99)
author: MarekSpodBiedry
body:
Fixes #99.

The DXF writer emitted a paper-space VIEWPORT without its per-viewport layer colour overrides (`Viewport::layer_colors`), and the reader always set them to an empty list. After a save and reopen the override was gone, so a ByLayer line plotted in the layer colour (red) instead of the viewport override (blue).

The writer now adds the overrides to the VIEWPORT as CADCraft xdata, the same way the dimension associativity links are stored (`1001 CADCRAFT`, a named `1002 { ... }` list read back with `xdata` / `xdata_list`):

```
1001 CADCRAFT
1000 VPCOLORS
1002 {
1000 <layer>   1000 <colour>   (one pair per override)
1002 }
```

The colour is the `Color::name` text, which `Color::parse` reads back exactly (index colours as "Blue" / "Color 34", true colours as "255,128,0"), so true-colour overrides are not reduced to the nearest ACI. Viewports without overrides are written as before. Files from other writers have no such xdata and load with an empty list, as now; malformed pairs are skipped. The list is capped at `MAX_XDATA_ITEMS` pairs, like the other xdata lists.

Both paths in the issue (CLI `--save` and engine `saveas`) go through `write_dxf`, so both are covered. DWG does not read or write viewports at all, so it is not touched.

#150 (issue #98, now on main) stores viewport frozen-layer lists the same way (`VPFROZEN`). Because `xdata` reads only the first group for an application, the writer now puts both lists under one `1001 CADCRAFT` group on the VIEWPORT, each list only when it is non-empty.

Test: `viewport_layer_colors_roundtrip` writes three viewports: one with an index-colour and a true-colour override (one on a layer name with a space), one with none, and one with both a frozen layer and the overrides in the shared group; it reads the DXF back and checks every list. Without the fix the reopened overrides are empty and the test fails.

title: Save As: offer DWG and keep the drawing's format (complements #21)
author: Tru10
body:
Related to #14. #21 fixed the Open dialog; this fixes the same problem in Save As.

## Problem

The Save As dialog listed DXF, SVG, PNG and PDF, though CADCraft writes DWG. On macOS the dialog accepts only listed extensions, so a name typed as `part.dwg` was changed to .dxf and the drawing was saved as DXF.

## Change

- Adds "Drawing (DWG)" to Save As. The existing suggested-type-first ordering makes a drawing opened from DWG default to DWG; new drawings and DXF files keep DXF first.
- The list moves into `filters_for_save` (`apps/cadcraft/src/main.rs`) with a unit test.
- The new label gets its Ukrainian translation, following "Drawing (DXF)".

## Testing

- `cargo xtask ci` passes.
- Manually on macOS: Save As with a `.dwg` name keeps .dwg, and the saved file reopens with File > Open.

title: Web: File > Open… shows the browser's file picker (fixes #55)
author: vangel76
body:
Fixes #55.

## The problem

The web app built `CadApp` with `Services::default()`, so it had no open picker. File > Open…, the toolbar's Open button, the Start tab's "Open..." and typing `OPEN` all reached `ui.open`, found no picker and returned `Ok(null)`. No picker appeared and no message was shown. Native OPEN takes a path, and a browser page has none. The engine's `open` already accepts `{data: base64, name}`, but nothing on the web called it.

Files dropped on the page went nowhere either. eframe hands them over unread on the web (`DroppedFile::web_file`), and the UI handles drops only natively (`#[cfg(not(target_arch = "wasm32"))]`).

## Changes

- **`apps/cadcraft-web/src/upload.rs`** (new, web-sys only, no new crates): `Inbox::pick` adds a hidden `<input type="file" accept=".dxf,.dwg">` and clicks it. When a file is chosen, it is read in the background (`Blob.arrayBuffer()` through `wasm-bindgen-futures`, already a dependency). The result goes into an `Rc<Cell<Vec<…>>>` inbox and a repaint is requested. `Shell::logic` drains the inbox before each frame. Cancelling does nothing; a leftover input from a cancelled pick is replaced by the next one. Files dropped on the page are read the same way (`Inbox::take_dropped`).
- **`apps/cadcraft-web/src/main.rs`**: installs the picker as `app.services.pick_open` (it starts the async pick and returns `None`). `Shell` now holds the inbox.
- **`crates/ui-egui`**: `CadApp::open_bytes(name, bytes)` runs OPEN with `{data, name}`, just as `open_path` runs it with `{path}`, and shows/zooms the drawing the same way. `CadApp::open_failed` reports a file that never reached OPEN (unreadable, too large) on the command line and in the status bar, as a failed OPEN is reported. `MAX_OPEN_BYTES` is 256 MB: the browser holds the drawing several times over while decoding it (bytes, base64, decoded copy), so files are capped below the DWG reader's own 512 MB. The browser checks `File.size` against the cap before reading anything. Nothing …

title: Print opens a Plot dialog (#160)
author: vangel76
body:
Fixes #160.

## The problem

File > Print..., Cmd/Ctrl+P and typing PLOT or PRINT ran the `plot` command with no parameters. It built the PDF and returned it as base64 to nobody, so printing seemed to do nothing. There was no window for choosing what to plot or how.

## Changes

- **Plot dialog** (`crates/ui-egui/src/managers.rs`). File > Print..., Cmd/Ctrl+P and typed PLOT / PRINT now open a Plot dialog, laid out by function like the reference app's Plot dialog:
  - Printer/plotter: PDF (vector). CADCraft only plots to PDF, so there is no copies field.
  - Layout: Model or any layout. It starts on the current one.
  - Paper size, orientation, plot area, Fit to paper or a scale (a number or a ratio such as `1:50`), and Plot object lineweights.
  - Model space offers the plot areas Extents, Display, Limits and Window. Window adds first and opposite corner fields.
  - A small sheet sketch shows the orientation, the printable area and the size in mm.
  - Settings start from the layout's page setup. Model space starts from fitted extents on A4 in metric drawings and ANSI A otherwise.
- **OK** asks where to save the PDF when the host has a file dialog, then runs `plot` with the chosen settings through `app.run`. It reports the result on the command line. If you cancel the file dialog, the Plot dialog stays open with its settings. If plotting fails, the error is echoed and the dialog stays open. **Apply to Layout** saves the settings into the layout's page setup with `pagesetup`. **Cancel** closes the dialog.
- **Shared page-setup rows.** The Page Setup Manager and the Plot dialog now draw the same rows from one function (`page_rows`), instead of each having its own copy. The plot-area dropdown now shows capitalised labels.
- **`plot` command** (`crates/engine/src/cmd/layout.rs`). It now takes `plotArea` for Model: `extents` (default), `display` (the current model view), `limits` (LIMMIN/LIMMAX), or `window` with `window: [[x1,y1],[x2,y2]]`. A layout accepts only `layout`…

title: macOS: the window title lines up with the traffic lights (fixes #161)
author: vangel76
body:
## The problem

On macOS the window has no system title bar (`with_fullsize_content_view`, `with_titlebar_shown(false)`). AppKit draws the traffic lights itself, centred in its standard 28 pt title-bar band at the top of the window. CADCraft's integrated title row is already that band, but the title text was drawn 1 pt below the row's centre (`title_h / 2.0 + 1.0`). With the system font (SF Pro) the middle of the capitals is the middle of the text box, so the text sat 1 pt below the lights' centre line (#161).

Neither winit 0.30.13 nor egui/eframe 0.36 can move the traffic lights. Doing it directly takes AppKit calls (`unsafe`), which the workspace forbids. So the title row fits the lights instead of the other way round, as in WordCraft (storytold/wordcraft#255).

- **Title text:** centred on the traffic lights' centre line (the middle of the 28 pt row). The 1 pt nudge is gone.
- **Nothing under the lights:** a long drawing name in a narrow window used to spread under the lights. The title now starts no further left than `MAC_CONTENT_LEFT` = the end of the three lights (12 pt buttons, 20 pt pitch, first one at about 10 pt) plus the 8 pt gap the lights keep from the top of the window, so the gap after them matches the gap above them. Short titles stay centred.

title: DXF: keep saved layer states through save and reopen (fixes #201)
author: vangel76
body:
Fixes #201.

## The problem

`layerstate.save` (Format ▸ Layer States Manager…) stores states in `Drawing::layer_states`. The DXF writer never wrote them and the reader never read any, so after a DXF save and reopen the list was empty and `layerstate.restore` failed with "no such layer state". DWG lost them too, because it's written from the same DXF.

## Changes

- **Writer** (`dxf_write.rs`): saved layer states are written as JSON (`{version: 1, states: [...]}`) in a `CADCRAFT_LAYERSTATES` XRECORD in the named object dictionary. This is the same mechanism as the `CADCRAFT_CONSTRAINTS` record, and other readers keep or ignore it. A drawing with no layer states gets no record. The constraint record and this one are now written by one loop over `(key, handle, chunks)`.
- **Reader** (`dxf_read.rs`): `Objects::xrecord_text(key)` collects a CADCraft XRECORD's text, capped at `MAX_PAYLOAD`. Constraints and layer states both use it.
- **`dxf_ext.rs`**: the 250-character chunking with backslash escaping is now in a shared `json_chunks` helper. New `layer_state_chunks` / `parse_layer_states`: version check, at most 100 000 states, malformed payloads ignored.

AutoCAD's own layer-state storage (`ACAD_LAYERSTATES` under the LAYER table) isn't described in enough detail in the DXF Reference to write it clean-room, so this uses CADCraft's own record, like the constraints do.

## Test plan

- [x] New test `layer_states_roundtrip_next_to_constraints`: two states (one with every layer off/frozen/locked/no-plot, and a layer with a non-ASCII name, true colour, transparency and a description containing a backslash) survive DXF save → reopen → save → reopen, and a DWG round trip. The constraints in the same drawing still round-trip. A drawing without states writes no record. The test fails without the reader change.
- [x] `cargo test -p cadcraft-io`
- [x] `cargo clippy -p cadcraft-io --all-targets -- -D warnings`
- [x] `rustfmt --check` on the touched files
- [x] `cargo xtask wasm`

title: Pick box at object-selection prompts; prompts remember the last option (#34)
author: vangel76
body:
Part of #34: the pick box cursor at object-selection prompts, and prompts remembering the last option. The other parts of #34 are handled elsewhere (DWG filter #21, save prompt on close #47/#48) or out of scope (dynamic blocks).

## The problem

- **Pick box.** The crosshair drew the pick box only at prompts that accept a selection set ("Select objects"). Many commands pick a single object themselves with a plain point prompt: FILLET/CHAMFER "Select first object/line", OFFSET "Select object to offset", TRIM, EXTEND, BREAK, LENGTHEN, PEDIT, the dimension and constraint picks. There the cursor stayed a bare crosshair with no rollover highlight, so you couldn't tell what a click would hit. The idle crosshair also showed the box when PICKFIRST was off.
- **Remembered options.** HATCH's "Select objects" option wasn't kept. The next HATCH went back to "Pick internal point", and pressing Enter in select mode returned to the pick prompt instead of creating the hatch. Several prompts didn't show the value used last time as `<default>`: HATCH pattern/scale/angle, FILLET radius, CHAMFER distance, POLYGON Inscribed/Circumscribed, ROTATE angle, SCALE factor.

## Changes

- **Engine:** `Prompt::picks_objects()` is true for a selection prompt, or a point prompt whose message starts with "Select" (AutoCAD's wording for object picks). `Session::picking_objects()` adds the idle case: no command running and PICKFIRST on. The canvas uses it for the pick box and the rollover highlight.
- **Pick box:** the box is the pick aperture the click actually uses (half side PICKBOX × 1.5 px, the same as `select::pick`), so the square shows what gets hit. It is hidden at PICKBOX 0 and drawn with a new `crosshair` theme token (the crosshair's colour was hard-coded before). The `draw_crosshair` call site is unchanged, so this doesn't overlap with #39's cursor change.
- **HATCH/GRADIENT:** "Select objects" is now a real mode: "Select objects or [picK internal point/Undo/seTtings/sCale/Angle]:", and E…

title: DXF: keep block descriptions and constant attribute definitions (fixes #204)
author: vangel76
body:
Fixes #204.

## The problem

Saving to DXF lost parts of block definitions:

- **Constant attribute definitions.** The ATTDEF writer put only the invisible bit into group 70, so a constant ATTDEF (70 = 2) came back as a variable one. After reopening, INSERT creates an attribute for it. Other programs stop drawing the constant text on existing references, because a variable ATTDEF isn't drawn as part of the block.
- **Block descriptions.** BLOCK's `description` (also shown by `blocks.list`) was never written as BLOCK group 4, and the reader ignored group 4.
- **Insertion units and explodability.** The BLOCK_RECORD groups 70 and 280 were neither read nor written, so blocks from opened files came back unitless and explodable.

## Changes

- `dxf_write.rs`: a new `attrib_flags` helper writes group 70 as invisible (1) | constant (2) for ATTDEF and ATTRIB. User blocks get BLOCK group 4 when they have a description, and BLOCK_RECORD 70 (insertion units) and 280 (explodability). Generated blocks (`*D`, arrowheads, `*T`) and the space blocks are written as before.
- `dxf_read.rs`: BLOCK group 4 is read into `Block::description`. BLOCK_RECORD 70/280 go into `Block::units` / `Block::explodable`, with defaults 0 and explodable when the groups are missing. The constant bit was already read.

## Test plan

- [x] New test `block_definition_properties_and_constant_attdefs_roundtrip`: a block with a description, units 4 and explodable off, holding constant, constant + invisible and normal ATTDEFs, keeps all of them through a DXF round trip. A plain block keeps the defaults. The test fails without the change.
- [x] `cargo test -p cadcraft-io`
- [x] `cargo clippy -p cadcraft-io --all-targets -- -D warnings`
- [x] `rustfmt --check` on the touched files
- [x] `cargo xtask wasm`

DWG (written by converting this DXF) now keeps the description and the constant flag. The DWG bridge still drops the units and explodability.

title: fix(geom): preserve three-point circle precision at large coordinates
author: Ni-zav
body:
## Summary
Fix inaccurate circumcenter calculations when creating circles
from three points at large drawing coordinates.

## Changes
- Calculate circumcenters using point-relative vectors instead
  of absolute coordinate squares.
- Apply a scale-aware collinearity threshold.
- Reject non-finite intermediate results.
- Preserve accuracy for small circles far from the origin.

## Regression Tests
- Circles near coordinates of 1e12.
- Small valid triangles.
- Collinear points.
- Non-finite inputs.

## Validation
- Changes committed and pushed against upstream main.
- Regression tests added but not executed.
- Cargo compilation and CI remain unverified.

title: fix(geom): calculate tight ellipse and arc bounds analytically
author: Ni-zav
body:
## Summary
Improve bounding-box accuracy for rotated ellipses and partial
elliptical arcs by calculating their extrema analytically.

## Changes
- Replace tessellation-based bounds with analytical extrema.
- Calculate exact extrema for both coordinate axes.
- Include extrema only when they lie within the arc sweep.
- Preserve both arc endpoints.
- Remove dependence on tessellation resolution.

## Regression Tests
- Rotated complete ellipse bounds.
- Partial elliptical arc bounds.
- Extrema inside and outside angular sweeps.

## Validation
- Changes committed and pushed against upstream main.
- Regression tests added but not executed.
- Cargo compilation and CI remain unverified.

title: fix(geom): measure bulged polylines and distant polygons accurately
author: Ni-zav
body:
## Summary
Improve area calculations for curved polylines and polygons
positioned far from the drawing origin.

## Changes
- Calculate circular-segment areas analytically instead of
  relying on tessellation.
- Preserve signed area contributions from polyline bulges.
- Accumulate polygon areas relative to a local vertex.
- Reduce floating-point cancellation at large coordinates.
- Preserve existing implicit closing-edge behavior.

## Regression Tests
- Positive semicircular bulges.
- Negative semicircular bulges.
- Polygons at large coordinate offsets.
- Reversed polygon winding.
- Open-polyline area calculations.

## Validation
- Two commits pushed against upstream main.
- Regression tests added but not executed.
- Cargo compilation and CI remain unverified.

title: fix(geom): avoid false line-circle tangencies on long construction lines
author: Ni-zav
body:
## Summary
Fix numerical precision issues that can incorrectly classify
long construction lines as tangent to nearby circles.

## Changes
- Replace the quadratic-discriminant approach with a
  closest-point distance calculation.
- Avoid subtracting large, nearly equal floating-point values.
- Calculate intersection coordinates relative to the
  projection foot.
- Preserve accurate secant intersections for long lines.
- Prevent false tangencies for lines slightly outside circles.

## Regression Tests
- Long line passing slightly outside a circle.
- Exact tangent intersection.
- Long secant producing two intersections.

## Validation
- Two commits pushed against upstream main.
- Regression tests added but not executed.
- Cargo compilation and CI remain unverified.

title: DXF: keep thickness, point angle, hatch origin/background/elevation, xref paths and the built-in font name (fixes #213)
author: vangel76
body:
Fixes #213.

## The problem

Saving to DXF and reopening lost several properties of entities, blocks and text styles:

- Entity thickness (group 39) was never written, so RECTANG's Thickness, and the thickness of anything read from another program, came back as 0.
- POINT's X-axis angle (group 50) was never written.
- HATCH lost its origin and background colour. The elevation was written but read back as 0.
- Xref blocks were written as ordinary blocks: BLOCK 70 had no xref bit and group 1 had no path.
- The `Standard` style's built-in font `CADCraft Stroke` is written as `txt` for other programs and reopened as `txt`.
- Polyface (POLYLINE 70 bit 64) and polygon mesh (bit 16) polylines from other programs were read as 3D polylines through their vertices. Polyface face records became extra vertices at the origin.

## Changes

`dxf_write.rs`
- A small `thickness` helper writes group 39 when it's non-zero, in the position the DXF Reference gives for each record: LINE, POINT, CIRCLE, ARC, TEXT, SOLID, TRACE, LWPOLYLINE, POLYLINE.
- POINT writes group 50 (degrees) when the angle isn't 0.
- HATCH: the origin is added to each pattern line's base point (43/44). That is how the DXF Reference places a pattern, so other programs show the shift too. The DXF Reference has no HATCH groups for the origin or the background colour, so both also go out as `CADCRAFT` xdata: `1000 HATCH`, `1011` origin (a world position, which other programs move along with the hatch), and `1000` colour name (empty for none). When the hatch has a gradient, this is appended to the gradient's `CADCRAFT` xdata, so there is only one `1001 CADCRAFT` group.
- STYLE: the built-in font still goes out as `txt` in group 3, because every reader has that file. The CADCraft font name follows as `CADCRAFT` xdata (`1000 FONT`, name).

title: DXF: keep linetype text, multileader styles, page setups, named views, UCSs and groups (fixes #209)
author: vangel76
body:
Fixes #209.

## The problem

Saving a drawing to DXF and reopening it lost several table and object-section items:

- Complex linetype elements. Every dash was written as `74 0`, and the reader only read group 49, so embedded text and shapes were dropped. The built-in `FENCELINE1` was affected.
- Multileader styles. No MLEADERSTYLE objects were written, and `$CMLEADERSTYLE` wasn't either, so the current style fell back to Standard.
- Layout page setup. The plot scale, plot style table, plot area, "center" and "scale to fit" flags and the device were written as fixed values and never read. The layout's saved paper-space view wasn't stored anywhere.
- Named views, UCSs and groups. The VIEW and UCS tables were always empty, `ACAD_GROUP` had no entries, and the reader ignored all three. Files from other programs lost them when CADCraft saved them.

## Changes

- **LTYPE** (`dxf_write.rs` / `dxf_read.rs`): each element now gets its 74 type flags (2 text, 4 shape, +1 for absolute rotation), 75 shape number, 340 STYLE, 46 scale, 50 rotation, 44/45 offset and 9 text, as the DXF Reference describes. The reader parses them per element. The 340 handles are filled in once the STYLE table has handles. A shape whose style isn't a text style (for example `ltypeshp.shx`) gets an unnamed shape STYLE record (`70 1`, file in group 3). The reader maps such records back to the file name, and they don't become text styles.
- `DashElement` gets an `absolute` flag (serde default `false`) for absolute rotations. `FENCELINE1` now names its text style (`Standard`), so it round-trips exactly.
- **MLEADERSTYLE** objects go in a new `ACAD_MLEADERSTYLE` dictionary, with a CLASS entry. They carry arrow size (44), text height (45), landing gap (42), dogleg length (43) and text style (342). The other groups are written as defaults: MText content, straight ByBlock leaders. The reader reads these back by dictionary name. `$CMLEADERSTYLE` is written to the header.

  - device…

title: DXF: keep raster images through save; report entities a save can't keep (fixes #208)
author: vangel76
body:
Fixes #208.

## The problem

When you open a drawing from another program and save it, CADCraft drops two kinds of objects:

- **Raster images.** The DXF writer had no case for IMAGE entities, so they were left out of the saved file. The reader also ignored the IMAGEDEF object, so an image's file path was empty even before saving.
- **Entity types CADCraft doesn't model** (MLINE, MULTILEADER, 3DSOLID, REGION, BODY, MESH, SURFACE, OLE2FRAME, TOLERANCE, ACAD_PROXY_ENTITY…). They are read as "Proxy" entities with their raw groups, but the writer dropped them, and `qsave`/`saveas` still reported success.

## Changes

**Images round-trip** (new `crates/io/src/dxf_image.rs`, following the DXF Reference):
- Read: the IMAGE entity's placement, pixel U/V vectors, size, clip boundary (pixel coordinates, rectangle or polygon), clipping state, display flags, and brightness/contrast/fade. A pass after the OBJECTS section follows each IMAGE's group 340 to its IMAGEDEF and fills in the file path, the definition's name (its `ACAD_IMAGE_DICT` key), the default pixel size and the resolution unit. This works for images in model space, in layouts and in block definitions.
- Write: the IMAGE entity (groups 90, 10–13, 340, 70, 280–283, 360, 71, 91, 14/24), one IMAGEDEF per path and name (shared by images that use the same file, with every reactor listed), an IMAGEDEF_REACTOR per image, RASTERVARIABLES, the `ACAD_IMAGE_DICT` and `ACAD_IMAGE_VARS` entries in the named object dictionary, and the four CLASS records. An image without a clip boundary gets the full-image rectangle. A definition without a name is named after its file.
- `Image` (crates/doc) gains `name`, `clip`, `clipping`, `display`, `brightness`, `contrast`, `fade`, `pixelSize` and `resolutionUnits`. They all have serde defaults. The clip is in pixel space, so MOVE, ROTATE, SCALE and MIRROR stay correct without changes.

**Entities the file can't keep are reported.** I didn't write them back verbatim, because that isn't safe y…

title: Transparent 'ZOOM/'PAN run nested and resume the interrupted command (fixes #220)
author: vangel76
body:
Fixes #220.

## The problem

`Session::start` only let transparent commands *without* a prompt machine (`'zoom.in`, `'pan.left`…) run inside another command. A transparent command with its own prompts (`'ZOOM`, `'PAN`, Zoom Window/Object) fell through to `self.cancel()`: `LINE 0,0` then `'ZOOM` printed `*Cancel*`, the line in progress was lost, and the transparent command became the "last command", so Enter at `Command:` repeated ZOOM.

## Changes

- `Session` gains `suspended: Option<Running>`: a transparent interactive command typed with `'` while a command runs moves that command there (one level, as in AutoCAD) and prompts on its own. Its start is echoed as `>>ZOOM`, and `prompt_text()` prefixes its prompts with `>>`.
- When the transparent command ends (done, Enter, an internal error, or `*Cancel*` from its own machine), the outer command resumes where it was ("Resuming LINE command.").
- `last_command` is left on the outer command, so Enter afterwards repeats it.
- `Session::cancel()` (Esc) and starting a non-transparent command end both levels. A second interactive transparent command inside the first is refused with a message rather than cancelling anything.
- Changes made by the transparent command go into the outer command's undo step; it does not push one of its own.

## Test plan

- New `crates/engine/tests/transparent.rs`: `LINE 0,0` / `'ZOOM` / `W` / two corners / `10,0` / Enter draws the line with no `*Cancel*`; the nested prompt starts with `>>`; Enter afterwards restarts LINE; the same in a script (`LINE 0,0 'PAN 0,0 1,1 5,0`); Enter at a nested `'PAN` resumes CIRCLE; Esc, or starting LINE, inside a nested `'ZOOM` leaves nothing running or suspended.
- `cargo test -j 4 -p cadcraft-engine` (all pass)
- `cargo clippy -j 4 -p cadcraft-engine --all-targets -- -D warnings`
- `cargo check -j 4 --target wasm32-unknown-unknown -p cadcraft-engine`
- `rustfmt --edition 2024` on the touched files

Three keywords were listed in their prompts but did nothing, so the value typed after them was read the wrong way:

title: DWG: keep true colours, transparency, table styles, layouts and viewport ids (fixes #223)
author: vangel76
body:
Fixes #223.

## The problem

DWG saves convert our DXF with acadrust (`cadcraft_dwg::dxf_to_dwg`). Our DXF says `AC1015`, so acadrust wrote an R2000 DWG. R2000 DWG has no true colours, entity transparency or table styles, and acadrust's R2000 reader puts the paper-space entities of every layout into the first one (hakanaktt/acadrust#121). Reopening such a DWG gave index colours, ByLayer transparency, only a default table style, and an empty Layout2.

DWG also doesn't store viewport ids. Readers number a layout's viewports in order, and id 1 is the layout's paper-space viewport (the sheet). CADCraft keeps that viewport implicit, and MVIEW numbers its viewports from 2. Through DWG, the first real viewport became id 1, and the renderer and layout commands then took it for the sheet and didn't draw its model-space view. AutoCAD also treats a layout's first viewport as its paper-space viewport.

## Changes

- `cadcraft-dwg`: `dxf_to_dwg` writes at least AutoCAD 2004 (`AC1018`) DWG. The DXF handed to it, and every plain DXF save, stays R2000 (`AC1015`, `ANSI_1252`, `\U+` escapes), so #169's text encoding and the gradient/xdata payloads are untouched. AC1018 rather than newer because it is the oldest version that has all of the above, and AC1032 handles our TABLESTYLE records differently (title suppression is lost).
- acadrust 0.6.1 → 0.6.3 (semver-compatible). 0.6.3 encodes explicit transparency the way CAD applications read it (hakanaktt/acadrust#119) and fixes the ACI fallback of RGB layers.
- DXF writer: a layout that has viewports but no id-1 viewport gets a paper-space viewport written ahead of them: the whole sheet at 1:1, id 1, with `CADCRAFT` xdata `PAPERVIEW`. The reader drops viewports with that marker, so a DXF round trip doesn't change the document. Layouts that already have an id-1 viewport (files from other programs) are written as before.
- DXF writer: VIEWPORT records now carry status group 68 (positive = on) and the always-set bit 32768 in group 90 (DXF R…

title: Select objects: W, C, F, WP and CP selection modes (fixes #224)
author: vangel76
body:
Fixes #224.

## The problem

At "Select objects:" the typed selection modes `W`, `C`, `F`, `WP` and `CP` were rejected with *Invalid selection*. The points that followed were then taken as an ordinary window, where the corner order decides window or crossing. `ERASE C 5,-1 25,1` therefore did a left-to-right *window* selection, and a fence or polygon could not be given at all. Scripts and agents driving the command line have no other way to get these selections.

## Changes

- `preprocess_selection` (crates/engine/src/lib.rs) recognises `W`/`Window`, `C`/`Crossing`, `F`/`Fence`, `WP`/`WPolygon` and `CP`/`CPolygon` at any prompt that selects objects. It then starts a `select::SelectMode` held in the new `Session::select_mode`. The mode collects points through `select_mode_input`:
  - W / C: "Specify first corner" and "Specify opposite corner". The selection is a window or a crossing whatever order the corners come in.
  - F: "Specify first fence point" and "Specify next fence point or [Undo]". Enter ends it and selects what the fence crosses (the existing `select_fence`).
  - WP / CP: "Specify first polygon point" and "Specify endpoint of line or [Undo]". Enter closes the polygon.
  - The result reaches the command as an ordinary pick, so "N found, M total", Remove mode and single-object prompts work unchanged. Enter with too few points drops the mode. Esc cancels the command as before.
- `current_prompt()` shows the mode's prompt while it collects points, but only while the command is at its "Select objects" prompt. A command nested inside it (a transparent command) keeps its own prompt and input. The mode ends with the command (`finish`). Points are capped at 10,000 (typed input is hostile).
- New `select::select_polygon` for WP/CP. WP keeps objects whose hit geometry lies entirely inside the polygon without crossing its edges. CP adds objects that cross an edge or have a vertex inside.

title: Scripts and the command line read a trailing or double space as Enter (fixes #227)
author: vangel76
body:
Fixes #227.

## The problem

In an AutoCAD script a space ends an input, so a space at the end of a line or two spaces in a row are an Enter. CADCraft dropped these in both places that read text input:

- `Session::script` trimmed every line (`trim_end()`), so `ERASE L ` / `JOIN ALL ` stayed at "Select objects:".
- `Session::cmdline` (`cmdline.input`, MCP) split on any run of whitespace, so `MOVE L  0,0 5,5` fed `0,0` and `5,5` to the selection instead of ending it, while the script path already read the double space as Enter. The two paths each had their own tokenizer.

## Changes

- One tokenizer, `Session::input_line`, used by both: each space (or tab) ends an input, and an empty input (two spaces in a row, a trailing space, an empty line) is Enter. At `Command:` that Enter repeats the last command, as before for an empty line.
- `script` only strips non-space trailing whitespace (`\r`), so a trailing space is an Enter.
- Free text works as before:
  - In a script, a free-text prompt (TEXT/MTEXT contents) takes the rest of the line. A prompt with keywords still splits (`POLYGON … I 15`, #43).
  - At the command line, a line typed at a free-text prompt is one input, since the UI types spaces literally there. A one-line `cmdline` input still splits at name prompts reached mid-line (`divide 6,0 b DOT n 2`).
- The command line still ignores what follows once its command ends (`SETVAR NOSUCHVAR 1`); scripts carry on to the next command, as before.

## Test plan

- New `crates/engine/tests/space_is_enter.rs`:
  - script `ERASE L ` erases the line and ends.
  - `cmdline("ERASE L ")` does the same.
  - `cmdline("MOVE L  0,0 5,5")` moves the line, and the script form agrees.
  - TEXT contents with spaces stay one string, both in a script line and typed at the TEXT prompt.
  - The test fails on main (stays at `ERASE Select objects:`).
- `cargo test -j 4 -p cadcraft-engine -p cadcraft-mcp -p cadcraft-ui-egui -p cadcraft-cli` (all pass, including the existing command-line, S…

title: STRETCH: repeat Select objects until Enter, C/W windows, Displacement (fixes #228)
author: vangel76
body:
Fixes #228.

## The problem

STRETCH finished selecting after one window, ignored `C` (so `STRETCH C 12,1 8,-1  0,0 5,0` misread its points and the script stopped with `Unknown command "0,0"`), and ended without stretching on Enter at "Specify base point or [Displacement]", on the `Displacement` keyword, and on Enter at the second point.

## Changes

- STRETCH has its own prompt machine (`StretchM` in `crates/engine/src/cmd/modify.rs`). It is no longer a special case inside the shared MOVE/ROTATE/SCALE machine, and those commands behave as before.
- "Select objects" repeats until Enter:
  - Implied windows: right to left is a crossing window, left to right a window.
  - `C`/`Crossing` and `W`/`Window` choose the kind of the next window.
  - A single pick and All/Last/Previous select objects that move whole.
  - Remove/Add work as at other selection prompts.
  - Vertices inside any of the windows move.
  - CP/WP/Fence say they are not available yet in STRETCH and the prompt stays. The text is never misread as a command.
- "Specify base point or [Displacement] <Displacement>": Enter or `D` asks "Specify displacement <0,0>". Enter at "Specify second point or <use first point as displacement>" uses the base point as the displacement.
- Objects on locked layers are left alone, like MOVE does.
- `stretch_entity` takes a list of windows. The JSON `stretch {window, delta}` is unchanged.

## Test plan

- New `crates/engine/tests/stretch.rs`:
  - The script form with `C`.
  - Two implied crossing windows before Enter.
  - Enter and `D` for Displacement, and Enter at the second point.
  - All three tests fail on main.
- `cargo test -j 4 -p cadcraft-engine` passes.
- `cargo clippy -j 4 -p cadcraft-engine --all-targets -- -D warnings` passes.
- `rustfmt --edition 2024 --check` on the touched files passes.

title: Array commands: ARRAY, and edit-array option loops for ARRAYRECT/ARRAYPOLAR (#230)
author: vangel76
body:
Fixes #230.

## The problem

- `ARRAY` (alias `AR`) was not a command.
- `ARRAYRECT` created a fixed 4 × 3 grid as soon as the selection ended. There was no way to set counts or spacing at the command line.
- `ARRAYPOLAR` asked for the center, then "Enter number of items". Input written for the usual edit loop (`ARRAYPOLAR L <Enter> 0,0 I 4 X`) failed: `I` gave "Requires a positive integer.", `4` ended the command, and `X` started EXPLODE.

## Changes

The array commands now live in `crates/engine/src/cmd/array.rs`. Their specs, JSON runs and interactive machines moved out of `modify.rs`, so `SelectThen` loses only its two array arms.

- **ARRAY / AR**: select objects, then "Enter array type [Rectangular/PAth/POlar] <Rectangular>:". It continues as the chosen command with the selected objects. For PAth this uses the new `PathArrayM::with_objects` in `modify2.rs`. The JSON form `array {type?, …}` dispatches to `arrayrect`/`arraypolar`/`arraypath`.
- **ARRAYRECT**: after the selection it echoes "Type = Rectangular  Associative = No", previews the array and loops on `Select grip to edit array or [ASsociative/Base point/COUnt/Spacing/COLumns/Rows/Levels/eXit] <eXit>`:
  - COUnt: columns, then rows.
  - Spacing: column distance (or Unit cell, two corners), then row distance.
  - COLumns: count, then spacing (or Total).
  - Rows: count, then spacing (or Total), then the elevation increment. A non-zero increment is reported as not available (2D).
  - Base point: distances picked with a point are measured from it. Enter resets it to the centroid.
  - eXit / Enter creates the copies.
- **ARRAYPOLAR**: "Specify center point of array or [Base point/Axis of rotation]:" (the preview follows the cursor), then the loop `[ASsociative/Base point/Items/Angle between/Fill angle/ROWs/Levels/ROTate items/eXit] <eXit>`:
  - Items, Angle between and Fill angle are linked: angle between is derived from the item count and the fill angle. Setting it changes the fill angle, and the items may …

title: ROTATE: Reference option (fixes #235)
author: vangel76
body:
Fixes #235.

## The problem

At "Specify rotation angle or [Copy/Reference]", `Reference` only echoed "not available yet". The values typed after it were then taken as the rotation angle or run as commands. For example, `ROTATE ALL  0,0 R 30 120` failed with `Unknown command "120"`.

- "Specify the new angle or [Points] <0>" takes:

  - Enter (0),
  - a point (its angle from the base point),
  - or `P`, then "Specify first point" and "Specify second point".
- The objects turn by the new angle minus the reference angle. `Copy` still applies.
- Coincident points re-prompt ("The two points must differ."). The command does not fail.
- The rubber band shows the objects turning to the cursor once the reference angle is known.

The hunks stay clear of #206 (remembered rotation angle default) and #231 (STRETCH), so all three merge cleanly in any order.

title: AREA Object/Add area/Subtract area and DIST Multiple points take effect (fixes #233)
author: vangel76
body:
Fixes #233.

## The problem

AREA and DIST offered options that did nothing when chosen. AREA's `Object`, `Add area` and `Subtract area` were dropped without a message, so there was no way to measure a picked object from the command line or keep a running total. `Arc` and `Length` were ignored at first, and with three or more points they ended AREA as if `Total` had been chosen. DIST's `Multiple points` was ignored, so in a script the points after `M` ended DIST and the rest of the line ran as commands.

`crates/engine/src/cmd/inquiry.rs`:

title: TEXTEDIT prompt, Undo and Mode; MTEXT in scripts takes lines until an empty one (fixes #234)
author: vangel76
body:
Fixes #234.

## The problem

- TEXTEDIT prompted `Select an annotation object or or [Undo/Mode]:`. The message already ended in "or" and the prompt formatter adds " or [", so the word appeared twice. Its `Undo` and `Mode` options were dropped without a message.
- MTEXT took a single input as its whole contents. In a script (or typed at the command line), the second line of text ran as a command, and an empty line repeated MTEXT. On AutoCAD's command line and in scripts, MTEXT takes one paragraph per line and ends on an empty line.

## Changes

- `crates/engine/src/cmd/modify2.rs`, TEXTEDIT:
  - The prompt is `Select an annotation object or [Undo/Mode]:`.
  - `Undo` reverts the last edit made in this TEXTEDIT, one per `Undo`. The object is restored as it was. With no edits left, TEXTEDIT says so.
  - `Mode` asks `Enter a text edit mode option [Single/Multiple] <Multiple>:`. In Single mode TEXTEDIT ends after one edit. The mode lasts for that run of the command. AutoCAD keeps it in TEXTEDITMODE, a system variable we don't have yet.

title: SPLINE Close is smooth and options report; POLYGON typed radius has a flat bottom; CIRCLE rejects bad input (fixes #238)
author: vangel76
body:
Fixes #238.

## The problem

- `SPLINE … C` appended the first fit point and fitted an open, clamped spline through it. The result had a corner at the seam, a duplicate first point in its fit data, and DXF flag 70 = 9 (closed but not periodic).
- SPLINE's `Method`, `Knots`, `Object`, `start Tangency`, `end Tangency` and `toLerance` were ignored without any message. Garbage text was also ignored without a message.
- POLYGON with a typed radius put a vertex at the top when inscribed but a flat edge at the bottom when circumscribed. AutoCAD draws the bottom edge horizontal in both modes when the radius is typed.
- An invalid token at CIRCLE's centre prompt (e.g. `D`) was ignored without a message.

## Changes

- **geom:** new `Spline::from_fit_points_closed`, a periodic cubic interpolation. It uses chord-length parameters that include the closing chord, a periodic (unclamped) knot vector, and the first 3 control points repeated at the end, which is how DXF stores periodic splines. A repeated closing fit point is dropped. Also adds `Spline::from_fit(fit, closed)` and `Spline::is_periodic()`.
- **SPLINE:**
  - `Close` builds the periodic curve.
  - `Method` asks for Fit or CV; CV hands over to the existing SPLINE-by-control-vertices machine.
  - `Knots`, `Object`, `start/end Tangency` and `toLerance` echo "… not available yet" and stay at the same prompt, so the next token is still read there. The geometry has no end-derivative or approximation fit yet.
  - Text that isn't a point or keyword reports `Point or option keyword required.`
  - On start it echoes the current settings line, as the CV variant already does.
- **Closed-spline editing:** SPLINEDIT Close, refit and move, and fit-point grips, now refit a closed spline as periodic instead of open plus a flag.
- **DXF:** writing sets group 70 bit 2 (periodic) for a closed spline with an unclamped knot vector. Reading refits a closed spline as closed when its stored knots are invalid.

title: UNDO asks for the number of operations; U undoes one (fixes #241)
author: vangel76
body:
Fixes #241.

## The problem

UNDO undid one operation at once and never asked how many. In a script, `UNDO 3` undid once and then stopped with `Unknown command "3"`. Typed on one line, the 3 was ignored.

## Changes

- **UNDO prompts** (`crates/engine/src/cmd/edit.rs`): "Enter the number of operations to undo or [Auto/Control/BEgin/End/Mark/Back] <1>".
  - A positive integer undoes that many operations. Enter undoes one. Anything else re-prompts with "Requires a positive integer.".
  - BEgin/End/Mark/Back say "not available yet" and end the command.
  - Auto and Control first take their value (ON/OFF, All/None/…) and then say "not available yet", so no following token runs as a command.
  - The JSON form `undo {count?}` (execute, MCP, control channel) is unchanged.
- **U is its own command**, as in AutoCAD. It undoes one operation without asking. Edit > Undo, Cmd+Z (`crates/ui-egui/src/menus.rs`) and the toolbar button (`crates/ui-egui/src/chrome.rs`) now run U, so they still undo immediately. Before, `u` was an alias of `undo`.
- **No undo step for UNDO** (`Session::finish`): an interactive command outside undo (`noundo`) that changed the drawing records no undo step and leaves redo alone, as `execute` already does. UNDO is the only such command; without this, UNDO would have recorded itself and cleared redo. Commands outside undo that don't touch the drawing (SELECT, ZOOM, DIST…) take the unchanged path.

## Test plan

- New `crates/engine/tests/undo_count.rs`:
  - `UNDO 3` in a script and on one line, then REDO 3 restores everything (UNDO added no step and redo survived).
  - Enter at the UNDO prompt undoes one.

title: OFFSET Erase/Layer/Multiple/Undo and MOVE/COPY Displacement take effect (fixes #244)
author: vangel76
body:
Fixes #244.

## The problem

OFFSET listed Erase and Layer at its distance prompt, and Multiple and Undo at its object/side prompts, but all four keywords were swallowed: `OFFSET E Y 2 …` kept the source and then complained "Requires a positive distance" about the `Y`. MOVE and COPY listed Displacement at "Specify base point", but `D` (and Enter) did nothing, so the displacement typed next became the base point.

## Changes

- **OFFSET Erase / Layer**: `Erase` asks "Erase source object after offsetting? [Yes/No]" and `Layer` asks "Enter layer option for offset objects [Current/Source]". The choices are remembered in the drawing header (OFFSETERASE, OFFSETLAYER) and shown in the "Current settings" line. With Erase=Yes the source is removed after offsetting (not when its layer is locked); with Layer=Current the copy goes on the current layer.
- **OFFSET Multiple / Undo**: Multiple keeps offsetting, each side point offsetting the newest copy again, until Enter (`<next object>`) goes back to "Select object to offset". Undo takes back the last offset (the drawing before it is restored, keeping any settings changed meanwhile).
- **OFFSET JSON**: the JSON form takes `erase?: bool` and `layer?: "source"|"current"`. Defaults stay as before; it does not read the remembered options.
- **MOVE / COPY Displacement**: a small wrapper around the shared select-then-points machine. At "Specify base point" (`<Displacement>` is now the default), `D` or Enter asks "Specify displacement" and moves or copies the selection by that vector. Base point then second point works as before.
- Not included: OFFSET of a closed spline still gives an open spline. A proper fix needs the smooth closed fit from #240 (`Spline::from_fit(fit, closed)`). Once that is merged, it is a one-line change in `offset_kind`.

Every change is in `crates/engine/src/cmd/modify.rs`, in hunks that don't overlap our other open PRs that touch this file (#206, #231, #232, #236) or #196. A trial merge with #231, #232 and #23…

title: Dimension and multileader options take effect (fixes #243)
author: vangel76
body:
Fixes #243.

Several dimension and multileader prompts listed options that did nothing:
- DIMORDINATE `Mtext/Text/Angle` were ignored, and any keyword other than `Xdatum` forced a Y datum.

title: -INSERT asks for X and Y scale; Basepoint/Scale/Rotate take effect (fixes #245)
author: vangel76
body:
Fixes #245.

## The problem

The command-line INSERT had one "Enter scale factor" prompt after the insertion point, so the usual `-INSERT name point xscale yscale rotation` sequence went wrong: the Y scale became the rotation and the rotation was typed at `Command:` (`-INSERT B1 20,20 1 1 0` rotated the block by 1° and then reported ``unknown command `0` ``). The `[Basepoint/Scale/Rotate]` options at the insertion-point prompt were listed but ignored, so their values landed at later prompts. There was no way to give different X and Y scale factors, from the command line or the JSON form.

- `crates/engine/src/cmd/blocks.rs`: the INSERT prompt machine now follows the sequence insertion point → "Enter X scale factor, specify opposite corner, or [Corner] <1>" → "Enter Y scale factor <use X scale factor>" → rotation → attributes.

author: vangel76
body:
Fixes #248.

**Stacked on #206. Merge #206 first.** This branch builds on #206's FILLET radius and CHAMFER second-distance defaults, so until #206 is merged the diff below also shows #206's commit. Only the last commit (`FILLET/CHAMFER Trim, Multiple, Undo; …`) belongs to this PR.

## The problem

FILLET listed Trim, Multiple and Undo, and CHAMFER listed Angle, mEthod, Polyline, Trim, Multiple and Undo (plus Angle/Method at the second-line prompt). All of them were swallowed. `CHAMFER A 2 45 …` used the old distances, `FILLET T N …` trimmed anyway, and every run ended after one corner.

## Changes

- **Trim**: "Enter Trim mode option [Trim/No trim]", remembered in TRIMMODE and shown in the current-settings line. With No trim the arc or chamfer line is added and both objects are put back unchanged (`fillet_corner`, a wrapper around the existing `fillet_lines`).

The second distance comes from the law of sines in the corner triangle; an angle that can't close the corner is rejected. `Distance` sets CHAMMODE=0.

title: BLOCK refuses a definition that references itself; names are case-insensitive (fixes #250)
author: vangel76
body:
Fixes #250.

## The problem

BLOCK accepted a redefinition whose selection contained a reference to the block being defined, either directly (the usual case after BLOCK converted the originals to a reference) or through another block. The block then contained itself. Its original geometry was gone from the definition, every reference drew a self-nesting copy down to the depth limit, and the cycle was saved. Redefining with a name that differed only in case (`Door`, then `DOOR`) added a second block instead of replacing the first, although block names are case-insensitive.

## Changes

- `crates/engine/src/cmd/blocks.rs`, `make_block`: before changing anything, it follows the block references in the selection through nested definitions. If any of them reaches the block being defined, it returns "Block "B" references itself." The drawing is untouched.
- A redefinition reuses the existing block's name when the new name matches it ignoring case.
- Interactive BLOCK and -BLOCK: a definition that can't be made now reports why and ends the command. Before, it stayed at a finished selection prompt.

## Test plan

- New `crates/engine/tests/block_redefine.rs`:
  - The command-line script `-BLOCK B 0,0 ALL` over B's own reference reports "references itself". B keeps its line, and the reference and the new line stay in the drawing.
  - The nested A→B→A case is refused through JSON.
  - `Door`/`DOOR` leaves one block, `Door`, holding the new definition.
  - Both tests fail without the change.
- `cargo test -j 4 -p cadcraft-engine -p cadcraft-mcp -p cadcraft-cli` pass. `cargo test -j 4 -p cadcraft-ui-egui` passes except `i18n::tests::ukrainian_covers_commands_menus_tools_and_snap_labels`, which already fails on `main`.
- `cargo clippy -j 4 -p cadcraft-engine --all-targets -- -D warnings`, `rustfmt --edition 2024 --check` on the touched files, and `cargo check --target wasm32-unknown-unknown -p cadcraft-engine` are clean.

author: vangel76

title: macOS: open drawings sent from Finder, Open With and the Dock (fixes #158)
author: kaffeochknivar
body:
Fixes #158.

> Builds on #256 (CI on stable 1.96), so this diff includes its three commits until #256 merges. Merges cleanly with `main`.

## The problem

A Finder double-click, Open With, a drop on the Dock icon or `open -a CADCraft file.dxf` don't pass the path in argv. LaunchServices sends a `kAEOpenDocuments` ('odoc') Apple event instead. winit 0.30 doesn't handle it, so AppKit answered *"CADCraft cannot open files in the 'Drawing Exchange Format' format"* and the app started with an empty drawing, as the issue describes.

## The fix

Handling the event needs Objective-C class declarations (`unsafe`), which this workspace forbids. So this uses **`fmv-macos-events` `=0.1.0`** (MIT OR Apache-2.0), the crate photocraft, pdfcraft, effectcraft and wordcraft use for the same thing.

- It registers an `NSAppleEventManager` handler. It registers once at install and again at `NSApplicationWillFinishLaunching`, so it is in place before Finder's launch event arrives.
- It leaves winit's application delegate alone and hands over safe events.
- I read all 168 lines before adding it.

Changes:
- **`apps/cadcraft/src/apple_events.rs`** installs the handlers on the main thread before `eframe::run_native` and adapts the crate's events. Events that arrive between frames request a repaint.
- **`cadcraft_ui_egui::{OsEvent, Services::os_events}`** is platform-neutral (just a closure). `CadApp::logic` drains it every frame:
  - `OsEvent::Open` opens each drawing exactly like a file dropped on the window. This works at launch and for a running instance (new tabs, same process).
  - `OsEvent::Quit`: the crate also takes over 'quit' (Dock ▸ Quit, logging out). It sets `quit_requested`, which is the Cmd+Q path, so unsaved changes are asked about.
- **Workspace `rust-version` goes from 1.90 to 1.95**, because the crate declares 1.95. photocraft already declares 1.95. Happy to drop this if you'd rather handle MSRV differently.

title: Layout viewports scale model-space linetypes by PSLTSCALE (fixes #257)
author: vangel76
body:
Fixes #257.

## The problem

The renderer never read `PSLTSCALE`. Model-space objects seen through a layout viewport got their dash pattern at model-space length (`LTSCALE` × the object's linetype scale), and then the viewport scaled it down. With the default `PSLTSCALE` = 1, the dashes should keep their paper-space length at any viewport scale. In a 1:100 viewport a DASHED line came out with dashes 0.005 paper units long instead of 0.5, so it looked solid in the layout, in Plot Preview and in PDF plots.

## Changes

- `crates/render/src/lib.rs`: the drawing context gets an `lt_factor`, which is 1 everywhere except model space drawn inside a viewport. There it is 1 / viewport scale when `PSLTSCALE` ≠ 0. It goes into the linetype scale in `resolve` and is passed down through block references. Model space, paper-space entities, hatch patterns and `PSLTSCALE` = 0 keep the old behaviour.
- New test file `crates/render/tests/psltscale.rs`: a DASHED line in a 1:100 viewport. With `PSLTSCALE` = 1 the dashes measure 0.5 paper units. With `PSLTSCALE` = 0 they measure 0.005, which is the old behaviour. In model space the dashes are unchanged.

## Test plan

title: -LAYER: command-line option loop for layers (fixes #254)
author: vangel76
body:
Fixes #254.

## The problem

`-LAYER` had no command-line form. `Session::start` strips the dash, so `-layer` ran the `layer` listing command and ended at once. Every following token was then read as a new command: `-LAYER M Walls C 1 Walls` started MOVE. Scripts could not create a layer, make it current or change its properties.

Two gaps in the layer commands showed up along the way:
- `layer.new` and `layer.set` accepted any linetype name, including ones that are not loaded.
- `layer.set {newName}` could rename a layer onto another existing layer's name, which left two layers with the same name.

## Changes

- `layer` gets an interactive prompt machine (`crates/engine/src/cmd/layer/prompts.rs`), so typed `-LAYER` (and `LAYER` in scripts and headless sessions) runs the AutoCAD-style option loop until Enter: `[?/Make/Set/New/Rename/ON/OFF/Color/Ltype/LWeight/TRansparency/MATerial/Plot/Freeze/Thaw/LOck/Unlock/stAte/Description/rEconcile]`.
  - Make creates the layer if needed and makes it current. Set makes an existing layer current. New takes a comma list. Rename asks for the old name, then the new one.
  - ON/OFF/Freeze/Thaw/LOck/Unlock, and the value options Color (index, name, r,g,b or Truecolor), Ltype (only loaded linetypes, `?` lists them), LWeight (snapped to a standard lineweight), TRansparency (0–90), Plot (Plot/No) and Description, take a comma-separated layer list with wildcards. Where AutoCAD defaults to the current layer, Enter applies the change to it.
  - Turning the current layer off asks first. Freezing the current layer is refused with a message.

  - Every option calls the `layer.new` / `layer.set` / `layer.current` command bodies directly, so validation matches the JSON form and the whole -LAYER session is one undo step.

title: Points draw with the point style (PDMODE/PDSIZE) (fixes #261)
author: vangel76
body:
Fixes #261.

## The problem

The renderer drew every POINT as a one-pixel dot. Format ▸ Point Style… (`ddptype`) stored `PDMODE` and `PDSIZE`, but nothing read them, so the setting changed nothing on the canvas, in Plot Preview or in PNG/SVG/PDF output. Points placed by POINT, DIVIDE and MEASURE stayed nearly invisible.

## Changes

- New `crates/render/src/point.rs` turns `PDMODE` into a figure: the low bits pick dot (0), nothing (1), plus (2), cross (3) or a tick upwards (4), +32 adds a circle and +64 a square. The figure turns with the point's angle. `PDSIZE` sets the size: positive values are drawing units, negative values a percentage of the view height, and 0 means 5 %. Hostile values fall back to a dot.
- `crates/render/src/lib.rs`: POINT entities draw that figure, with the entity's colour and lineweight. A relative size is divided by the block/viewport scale, so it stays a share of the view. `Options` gets `view_height`. When it is 0 and the style needs it, the height of the space's extents is used. Previews only compute extents when they contain a point.
- Callers: the canvas passes its view height (`crates/ui-egui/src/canvas.rs`, 1 line). PDF plots pass the plot window's height when there is one (`crates/io/src/pdf.rs`). The pdf.rs edit is placed so it doesn't overlap #200.
- New test file `crates/render/tests/point_style.rs`: X-in-circle at an absolute size, dot / nothing / square+circle, relative sizes from a given view height and from the extents, and hostile `PDMODE`/`PDSIZE` values.

I checked rendered PNGs by eye for `PDMODE` 35 and 99.

title: Bound block expansion in drawing and extents: nested, self-referencing or arrayed blocks no longer hang (fixes #255)
author: vangel76
body:
Fixes #255.

## The problem

`MAX_BLOCK_DEPTH` (16) bounds only how *deep* block references nest, not how many copies they expand to. A small DXF with a block that references itself a few times, blocks that each insert the next several times, or one MINSERT with large row and column counts expanded to billions of copies (4 self-references give 4^16). Drawing (`cadcraft_render::build`: the canvas and PNG/SVG/PDF export) and extents (`cadcraft_doc::entity_bounds`: ZOOM Extents, `cadcraft-cli info`, `$EXTMIN/$EXTMAX` on save, the spatial index) then hung, with memory growing without bound. Mutation fuzzing of our own DXF output found it: a fuzzed 2.8 KB file produced 28.7 million display primitives.

## Changes

- **render**: a per-display-list budget, `MAX_BLOCK_EXPANSION` (2 million). Each MINSERT copy and each entity drawn inside a block uses one unit (also for dimension blocks and model space seen through viewports). Once the budget is spent, the remaining block contents aren't drawn. The count is kept in a new public `DisplayList::expanded` field. Ordinary drawings stay far below the limit.
- **doc**: `entity_bounds` computes each block's content bounds (in block coordinates) once per call and reuses them for every further reference. Nested and self-referencing blocks now cost one pass per definition instead of one per reference. The results don't change: the bounds of a block's contents don't depend on the reference.

The changes stay inside the expanding functions. The display-list builder's construction sites are untouched, to stay clear of the open PSLTSCALE and point-style PRs.

## Test plan

- New `crates/io/tests/block_expansion.rs`:
  - `block_expansion_bombs_are_bounded`: a self-referencing block (4 and 12 references), a 15-level chain of blocks that each insert the next 4 times, and a 10,000 × 10,000 MINSERT. Each one reads, gets finite extents, draws at most `MAX_BLOCK_EXPANSION` primitives and saves. The test takes about 1 s in a debug build; without t…

title: Programmatic SPLINE limits the degree to 1..10 (fixes #268)
author: vangel76
body:
Fixes #268.

## The problem

`spline {"control": [...], "degree": N}` (control channel, MCP, scripts' JSON form) accepted any degree up to the number of control points minus one. Tessellation and extents grow roughly with the square of the degree. With 3000 control points, degree 1000 took 5 s and degree 2147483647 (clamped to 2999) took 65 s for the extents alone, in a debug build, and every redraw took as long again. SPLINE's `Degree` prompt, `spline.cv` and the DXF reader already limit the degree to 1–10, as AutoCAD does. Fuzzing `Session::execute` with hostile parameters found it.

## Changes

- `run_spline` (`crates/engine/src/cmd/draw.rs`) clamps the degree to 1..=10, the same as `spline.cv`.

## Test plan

- New `crates/engine/tests/spline_degree.rs`, `programmatic_spline_degree_is_limited`: 3000 control points with degree 2147483647, 2999 and 11 give degree 10, 0 gives 1, and 4 is kept. The extents span the control polygon. The test runs in 0.2 s.

title: Raster points no longer panic debug builds (fixes #270)
author: vangel76
body:
Fixes #270.

## The problem

The CPU rasteriser (PNG export, plot preview, agent screenshots) draws each point as a 1.5 px anti-aliased square with `Pixmap::fill_rect`. tiny-skia's anti-aliased rectangle filler has a `debug_assert!(false)` (`scan/hairline_aa.rs:124`) that fires when a rect narrower than two pixels has both its left and right sides mid-pixel in adjacent pixels: the inner run is then zero pixels wide. Release builds skip the assertion and draw correctly, but debug builds (dev runs, `cargo test`, debug CLI builds) panic for roughly every other point position.

## Changes

- `crates/render/src/raster.rs`: the point square is filled as a path (`PathBuilder::from_rect` + `fill_path`), which goes through tiny-skia's general anti-aliased path filler instead. The square has the same size, position and anti-aliasing as before. All `Kind::Point` primitives go through this code, including the dot that the point-style figures in #265 emit.

## Test plan

- New `crates/render/tests/raster_points.rs`:
  - `points_at_subpixel_positions_do_not_panic`: 256 points at every 1/16-pixel offset, plus points on and just outside the image border, rendered with and without anti-aliasing. The test also checks that a point is still drawn in the foreground colour.
  - `point_in_large_png_export_does_not_panic`: the reported case (a line plus a POINT at 3,0, fitted like PNG export) at 2400 × 1600 and two odd sizes.
  - Both tests panicked at `hairline_aa.rs:124` on `main` before this change and pass now.
- `cargo clippy -j 4 -p cadcraft-render --all-targets -- -D warnings`
- `cargo test -j 4 -p cadcraft-render`

title: DXF read: map mirrored OCS (extrusion 0,0,−1) of 2D entities to WCS
author: STE1200
body:
AutoCAD and BricsCAD store a mirrored block reference, and most 2D entities drawn in a mirrored UCS, with extrusion (0,0,−1). Their points and angles are then in an OCS whose x axis runs the other way. `dxf_read.rs` honoured that only for CIRCLE, ARC, LWPOLYLINE and SOLID/TRACE. Every other mirrored entity landed on the wrong side of the y axis: in our office drawings that is mirrored door and profile blocks (one door schedule had them at x = −57 618 instead of +57 618), mirrored hatches, mirrored texts and attributes, and mirrored dimensions' text.

## Changes (crates/io/src/dxf_read.rs)

- INSERT: insertion point through the OCS, negative x scale, opposite rotation and negative column spacing. Only for extrusions parallel to −Z (x/y noise up to 1e-3). A tilted block plane needs a 3D transform that `Insert` cannot hold and is left as read.
- HATCH and R12 2D POLYLINE: boundary x and bulges mirrored like LWPOLYLINE; the hatch pattern angle mirrors too.
- TEXT/ATTDEF/ATTRIB and MTEXT: points through the OCS; drawn readable (MIRRTEXT = 0) with the mirrored footprint, so the direction turns and left/right justification or attachment swap.
- ELLIPSE: centre and major axis are WCS, but the minor axis is extrusion × major, so the parameter range is negated.
- DIMENSION: the text midpoint (group 11) is the one OCS point.

Six tests in `crates/io/src/tests.rs`: a mirrored INSERT (incl. DXF round trip and extents), ELLIPSE, 2D POLYLINE, HATCH, TEXT, MTEXT.

## Checked

Against an independent DXF library (ezdxf `matrix44()`) on five private office drawings (AC1024/AC1027, BricsCAD-written): every one of 4166 INSERT transforms in a door schedule plan matches (3946 +Z, 202 −Z, 18 with noisy extrusion), as do the mirrored arcs, ellipses, polylines and hatches. Visually: a cafe plan's 12 mirrored chairs, a ground floor's hatch block and cadastral text, and 56 mirrored references in a block library now sit where BricsCAD draws them.

title: fix(annotate): DIMCONTINUE/DIMBASELINE in linear time, cap the points (#279)
author: vangel76
body:
Fixes #279.

## The problem

With DIMASSOC on (the default), `dimcontinue` / `dimbaseline` looked up the objects under each new dimension's definition points with `assoc::find_snap`. That function scans the whole space. Each point adds a dimension, so the space grows as the chain runs, and a call with *n* points cost about *n* × (entities + *n*). Measured on main: 4,000 points take 0.26 s (continue) and 0.73 s (baseline); 16,000 points take 2.7 s and 10 s. With `DIMASSOC 0` the 16,000-point chain takes 40 ms, so the time is all in the snap scan. The number of points per call had no limit either.

## Changes

- `assoc.rs`: a new `SnapIndex` holds the snap candidates of one space, sorted by x. `find` binary-searches the tolerance window (the same tolerance as `close`, which depends only on the query point). It returns the same snap as `find_snap`: lowest rank first, then the first object in space order. `find_snap` and the index share the rank in a new `snap_rank` helper.
- `annotate.rs` `chain_run`: builds one index per call (only when DIMASSOC is on) and attaches each chained dimension's `p13`/`p14` through it. Dimensions add no snap candidates, so the index stays valid while the chain adds them.
- A call with more than 100,000 points is refused with "at most 100000 `points` per call" before anything is created (input-sized loop cap, AGENTS.md).

The interactive DIMCONTINUE/DIMBASELINE (one point per input) and the other dimension commands are unchanged.

## Test plan

- New `crates/engine/tests/dim_chain.rs`, `chains_attach_like_dimreassociate_and_long_chains_are_capped`. Its checks don't depend on timing:
  - The fixture puts lines end to end, a point on every joint (a tie with the line start, decided by space order) and a circle on every midpoint (a centre outranks a line midpoint). It runs a continue chain and a baseline chain over joints and midpoints. Every dimension gets two associations, and `dimreassociate` (which still scans per point) gives exactly the sa…

title: fix(engine): guard begin/prompt/preview of interactive commands against panics (#283)
author: vangel76
body:
Fixes #283.

## The problem

`Session::execute` and interactive input (`run.machine.input` in `feed`) run under `catch_unwind`, as AGENTS.md requires. The other steps of an interactive command did not:

- the machine factory and `machine.begin`, the first step of `Session::start`;
- `machine.prompt()`, through `current_prompt()` and `prompt_text()`, which the UI calls every frame;
- `machine.preview()`, through `Session::preview`, on every cursor move.

A panic in any of them unwound out of the engine and took the app (and the drawing) down.

## Changes

- New `crates/engine/src/guard.rs`. `Guarded::create(id, factory, session)` runs the factory under `catch_unwind` and wraps the machine in `Guarded`, which implements `Interactive` by running every step of the inner machine under `catch_unwind`:
  - factory, `begin`, `input`: a panic becomes `EngineError::Internal`. `feed` already handles that by restoring the drawing to its state before the command, echoing "Internal error in <command>: <message>" and ending the command (as for input today).
  - `prompt`, `preview`: these take `&self` and can't end the command. The wrapper records the panic, returns an "Internal error; press Enter to end the command" prompt or an empty preview, and stops calling the broken step. The next input then ends the command through the same internal-error path. Esc cancels it as usual.
- `lib.rs`: `Session::start` creates the machine through `Guarded::create`, one changed line plus `mod guard;`. `current_prompt`, `prompt_text`, `preview` and `feed` are untouched, so this stays clear of the open PRs that edit them (#221, #226, #229, #206); `pairs.sh` reports no conflicts.
- AGENTS.md / CLAUDE.md: the "Last-resort guard" line names the wider guard.

## Test plan

- New unit test `guard::tests::panics_in_a_command_machine_end_the_command_not_the_app`. It uses a test-only machine that adds a point in `begin` and `input` and panics in the step under test. It is started the way `Session::start` s…

title: Only colour 7 flips with the background (fixes #272)
author: vangel76
body:
Fixes #272.

## The problem

`cadcraft_color::display_rgb` chose the on-screen and on-paper colour from luminance alone: any colour above 0.94 became black on a light background, and any colour below 0.06 became white on a dark one. Only colour 7 should do that. It means "white or black, whichever contrasts with the background". As a result:

- ACI 51 (light yellow), ACI 255 and true-colour white printed black in PDF and SVG, so white masking fills became black blocks.
- Dark index colours (18, 28, 168 … 248) and true-colour black showed as white on the dark canvas and in PNG export.

## Changes

- `crates/render`: `DPrim` has a new `aci7` flag. While the display list is built, colours resolve through a small `Ink` (RGB + "is colour 7"). The flag is set when an entity's colour comes out as 7: directly, by layer, by block (including the colour-7 fallbacks for layer 0 and unresolved ByLayer/ByBlock), through a dimension style colour, or through an MTEXT inline `\C7`. Inline true colours and every other index or true colour never set it. Clipping into viewports keeps the flag. `DPrim::display_rgb(background)` gives the colour to draw with.
- `crates/color`: `display_rgb(c, aci7, background)` flips only when `aci7` is set (white on dark, black on light). Otherwise it returns the colour's own RGB.
- Callers use `prim.display_rgb(bg)`: the raster renderer, PDF and SVG export (`crates/io`), and the egui canvas and GPU mesh (`crates/ui-egui`). In those two crates only the call sites change, plus the `aci7: true` field in two test literals.

## Test plan

- New `crates/render/tests/aci7_display.rs`, nine cases on paper (white) and on the dark canvas:
  - flips: ByLayer on layer 0, index 7, and ByBlock inside a colour-7 insert;
  - keep their RGB: index 51, index 255, true-colour white, index 250, true-colour black, and ByBlock inside an index-255 insert.

title: Extents: ignore what draws nothing (rays, missing or empty blocks, hidden block geometry), as ZOOM Extents does
author: STE1200
body:
Opening real office drawings in CADCraft often shows a tiny plan in a huge empty canvas. The extents included things that draw nothing:

- the base point of a RAY. Autodesk's reference states that infinite construction lines and rays do not affect ZOOM Extents. An apartment floor plan in our corpus (AC1024, BricsCAD) carries two rays 1.98 million units from the building, so the plan opened as a dot.
- the insertion point of an INSERT whose block is missing (purged definition, bound xref that never came along) or empty (unloaded xref). A floor plan had such references 125 000 and 3.4 million units away.

XLINEs were already ignored; rays now are too, and an insert contributes only what its block draws (attributes still count).

A second commit applies the same idea inside block definitions: an entity in a block counts for the insert's (or a dimension block's) extents only if it is not an ATTDEF, is not flagged invisible (group 60) and sits on layer 0 or on a layer that is on and thawed. Dynamic blocks from BricsCAD keep their constraint dimensions on `*ADSK_CONSTRAINTS` with defpoints far from the visible geometry; a block library in our corpus opened with its extents inflated by those. Text and MText that is empty, blanks only, or only `\~` has empty bounds. Each rule has its own test (ten new tests in `crates/doc/src/tests.rs`).

Checked against BricsCAD V26: after ZOOM Extents its EXTMIN/EXTMAX on a site plan is (−507, −282)…(616, 730); a reference to an empty block at x = −1875 in that drawing is ignored there, as it is here now. On the door schedule plan below, CADCraft's extents with this change match BricsCAD's (29 011, −24 079)…(236 029, 41 617).

title: Default lineweight follows LWDEFAULT (fixes #292)
author: vangel76
body:
Fixes #292.

## The problem
Objects whose lineweight resolves to "Default" (directly, or ByLayer on a layer with lineweight Default, or ByBlock from a Default block reference) were always drawn and plotted at 0.25 mm: `resolve` in `crates/render/src/lib.rs` hard-coded the width. title: LAYMRG and LAYDEL: merge layers, delete a layer with its objects (fixes #286)
author: vangel76
body:
Fixes #286.

## The problem

LAYMRG and LAYDEL were not registered. Typing them gave ``unknown command `LAYMRG` `` and stopped a script. The only way to get rid of a layer that still had objects was to find and erase every object by hand, in model space, every layout and every block definition, and then call `layer.delete`.

## Changes

- New `crates/engine/src/cmd/layer/merge.rs` with both commands. They are registered at the end of `layer::specs()`, with Format ▸ Layer Tools ▸ Layer Merge / Layer Delete as the menu entries.
- **LAYMRG**: "Select object on layer to merge or [Name/Undo]:" repeats until Enter. Name takes a layer name or a comma list, and Undo drops the last layer. Then it asks "Select object on target layer or [Name]:", echoes a warning naming the layers, and asks "Do you wish to continue?" `[Yes/No] <No>:`. On Yes, every object on the source layers moves to the target. That covers model space, layouts and block definitions (an attached xref's own blocks are left alone). The sources are dropped from viewport freeze lists and VP colour overrides, and the source layers are deleted.
- **LAYDEL**: same pick loop ("Select object on layer to delete or [Name]:"), warning and confirmation. On Yes, the layers are deleted along with every object on them in the same places. A block definition that loses all its objects stays defined.
- JSON forms that never prompt: `laymrg {from: [names], to}` and `laydel {names: [...]}`.
- Refusals: layer 0, Defpoints and xref-dependent (`xref|layer`) layers can't be merged away or deleted, and a layer can't be merged into itself or into an xref layer. LAYDEL refuses the current layer. LAYMRG accepts the current layer as a source and makes the target current (thawing it if needed), so there's no extra step before merging the layer you're working on. Typed, a refused pick is reported and the prompt repeats.

title: Default save format for new drawings (DXF or DWG)
author: Tru10
body:
Save As suggested `.dxf` for every untitled drawing, so saving new work as DWG meant typing the extension each time. AutoCAD keeps this choice in Options > Open and Save > "Save as".

## Change

- **File > Default Save Format > DXF / DWG** sets the format Save As suggests for drawings that have no file yet. Drawings opened from a file keep that file's format, as before. **DXF stays the default**, so nothing changes unless someone opts in.
- The choice is saved across restarts with the other preferences (`saveFormat`), survives Reset Palettes, and is scriptable as `ui.saveformat {format}` or the `saveFormat` UiState field (documented in `docs/control-protocol.md`).
- Ukrainian labels for the new menu entries.

CADCraft has no Options / Preferences window yet (see #23), so this follows the Interface Theme and Interface Language pattern as a menu item, placed in File next to Save As. If a preferences window lands, this would belong there (AutoCAD keeps it in Options > Open and Save), and I'm happy to move it.

If you'd rather not add a menu entry, an alternative is to remember the last format used in Save As and suggest it for new drawings. Happy to switch to that.

## Testing

- `cargo xtask ci` passes, including the new `default_save_format_persists_and_names_new_drawings` test.
- Manually on macOS: with DWG chosen, Save As on a new drawing suggests and keeps `.dwg`; the choice survives a restart; an opened `.dxf` still suggests `.dxf`; switching back to DXF restores `.dxf`.
