title: Metric drawings load library linetypes in millimetres (fixes #294)
author: vangel76
body:
Fixes #294.

## The problem
CADCraft's linetype library (`crates/doc/src/library.rs`, our own definitions) is defined in inches, and `LINETYPE` loaded it unchanged into every drawing. In a metric drawing (MEASUREMENT 1, millimetres) at LTSCALE 1, DASHED was 0.5 mm on / 0.25 mm off, so dashed, hidden and center lines looked continuous unless the user found the right LTSCALE (≈ 25).

## How other CAD programs handle it, and the choice here
AutoCAD keeps two linetype files: with MEASUREMENT = 1 it loads the ISO-scaled one, in which the same linetypes have their lengths multiplied by 25.4 (so LTSCALE 1 fits both unit systems). CADCraft does the equivalent with its own definitions, without a second table: the library stays defined once (in inches), and **`library::standard_linetypes_for(d)` scales every length by 25.4 when the drawing is metric** — dashes, gaps, embedded text/shape size and offsets. One source of truth means a metric and an inch variant can never drift apart, and it is exactly the inch→mm relation the metric definitions have. As in AutoCAD, the scaling happens when a linetype is loaded; definitions already in a drawing (e.g. from a DXF) are left alone.

## Changes
- `crates/doc/src/library.rs`: `standard_linetypes_for(&Drawing)` (scaled for MEASUREMENT 1), docs on `standard_linetypes`.
- `crates/engine/src/cmd/props.rs`: `LINETYPE` (`load`, also used by the Layer and Linetype managers) loads through it.
- `crates/engine/src/cmd/draw2.rs`: the CENTER linetype CENTERMARK / CENTERLINE load on demand is scaled too.

## Test plan
- New `crates/engine/tests/metric_linetypes.rs`: DASHED loads as 0.5/−0.25 in an imperial drawing and 12.7/−6.35 in a metric one; CENTER 31.75/…; FENCELINE1's embedded text scales to 2.54; CENTERLINE in a metric drawing loads the millimetre CENTER. All three fail on main.

- `cargo test -j 4 -p cadcraft-doc -p cadcraft-engine`
- `cargo check -j 4 --t…

title: WBLOCK honours base when writing a block (fixes #297)
author: vangel76
body:
Fixes #297.

## The problem

`wblock {path, name, base}` ignored `base`. A block was always written measured from its own base point, so you couldn't choose a different insertion point for the written drawing. The objects form (`handles` + `base`) already used `base`.

## Changes

- `run_wblock` (`crates/engine/src/cmd/blocks.rs`): with `name`, `base` (in the block's coordinates) now replaces the block's base point, which is still the default. In both modes the base point becomes the written drawing's origin, and the written drawing's `$INSBASE` is set to 0,0,0 explicitly, so inserting the file puts the base point at the insertion point.
- The params doc is unchanged: it already listed `base?`.

## Test plan

title: Draw hatch island styles, backgrounds, two-colour gradients and DXF pattern definitions (fixes #289, #290)
author: vangel76
body:
Fixes #289. Fixes #290.

## The problem

Hatch properties CADCraft already reads and stores were ignored when drawing (canvas, PNG/SVG/PDF export, plot):

- **Island detection style** (group 75: normal / outer / ignore): every hatch was filled with odd parity.
- **Background colour** of a pattern hatch: never drawn.
- **Gradients**: a flat fill in colour 1; colour 2, the gradient name, angle and shift were ignored, and a ByLayer colour 1 came out white (resolved against colour 7, not the hatch's layer).
- **Pattern definitions from DXF** (groups 78, 53, 43/44, 45/46, 79, 49) were skipped on read, so any pattern not in our library drew as ANSI31 and was saved with `78 0`.

## Changes

- `render/src/hatch.rs` now draws the whole hatch (`lib.rs` just calls `hatch::draw`):
  - `fill_loops`: style 1 keeps the outermost loops and their first islands, style 2 only the outermost loops. The nesting depth is how many other loops enclose a loop (point-in-polygon on an edge midpoint). Other values stay odd parity. The loop × vertex work is capped.
  - A pattern hatch's background is filled under its lines, in the background colour (ByLayer/ByBlock resolved).
  - Gradients: colour 1 → colour 2 along the gradient angle. LINEAR, CYLINDER, CURVED, SPHERICAL and HEMISPHERICAL ramps, with the `INV` forms swapping the colours; unknown names fall back to linear. Not centred moves the centre up and back. All backends draw it as plain triangle primitives: a base fill in the middle colour (it hides antialiasing seams), then the fill triangles split into pieces of at most 1/64 of the extent, each in one of 64 colour steps. Colours resolve through `ink()` against the hatch's layer and block colour, and a blended step only counts as colour 7 when both ends are.

title: OFFSET keeps a closed spline closed (fixes #303)
author: vangel76
body:
Fixes #303.

## The problem
OFFSET rebuilt the offset copy of every spline with the open fit-point interpolation (`Spline::from_fit_points`), so a closed spline came out open. Its start and end points matched, but it had a clamped knot vector, a corner at the seam and `closed: false`. Because of that, commands that need a closed boundary didn't treat it as closed.

## Changes
- `offset_kind` (crates/engine/src/cmd/modify.rs) builds the copy with `Spline::from_fit(points, sp.closed)` from #240. A closed source now gives a closed, periodic offset that stays smooth across its start point. Open splines are unchanged.
- New regression test `crates/engine/tests/offset_closed_spline.rs`: draws `SPLINE 0,0 10,0 10,10 0,10 C` at the command line, then offsets it inwards and outwards. It checks that each copy is closed and periodic, has no gap at the seam, and lies 1 unit inside or outside the original.

This is one line in `offset_kind` and stays clear of #246's OFFSET option hunks.

## Test plan

title: Wipeouts mask what is drawn before them; WIPEOUTFRAME controls the frame (fixes #291)
author: vangel76
body:
Fixes #291.

## The problem
A WIPEOUT was rendered only as its outline polygon, so everything behind it stayed visible — on the canvas and in PNG, SVG and PDF output — and the outline stayed even with `WIPEOUT Frames OFF` (`WIPEOUTFRAME 0`). (Saving wipeouts to DXF was #79/#147; this is the drawing side.)

## Changes
- **Display list** (`crates/render/src/lib.rs`): new primitive kind `Kind::Mask` — the wipeout polygon as triangles (stored like `Kind::Tris`) that a backend fills with *its background colour*. It is emitted in draw order, so it hides what was drawn before it and is covered by what comes after (`DRAWORDER` decides). Masks survive viewport clipping in layouts.
- **Frame** follows `WIPEOUTFRAME`: 0 = no frame, 1 = shown and plotted (default), 2 = shown on screen/exports but not in plots (`build_plot`).
- **Backends**: raster/PNG fills masks with `RasterOptions::background`; SVG and PDF with paper white; the egui CPU canvas with the canvas colour (the white sheet in layouts).
- **GPU canvas** (`crates/ui-egui/src/gpu.rs`): it drew all fills, then all lines, so a mask couldn't respect draw order. The mesh now records draw-order breaks before each mask (`MeshData::breaks`) and paint draws each group's fills, lines and quads in turn (`batch_ranges` maps a group's range onto the chunked GPU buffers). Without wipeouts there is one group, as before. Infinite lines (XLINE/RAY) are still drawn on top of everything, as before.
- Stays compatible with #285 (colour-7 flag): the mask is created through `Builder::tris` and its kind changed afterwards, so no new `DPrim` literal; I checked that this branch merged with #285 builds (`cargo check -p cadcraft-render -p cadcraft-io -p cadcraft-ui-egui --tests`).

Checked in the running app (GPU canvas): a line and a wide polyline under a wipeout are hidden inside it, a line drawn afterwards shows on top, and `WIPEOUT F OFF` removes the frame.

title: Wide polylines are drawn with their linetype (fixes #293)
author: vangel76
body:
Fixes #293.

## The problem
A polyline with width (constant or tapered) was always filled as one continuous band: with FILLMODE on, `crates/render/src/lib.rs` triangulated the whole band and never looked at the linetype (it only showed with FILLMODE 0, on the centre line). CAD programs dash wide polylines too: each dash is a filled piece of the band and the gaps are empty.

## Changes
- `crates/render/src/linetype.rs`: `ranges(len, lt, scale, min_pattern)` lays the pattern out along a length as (start, end) distances (dots: start == end), with the same continuous fallbacks as `apply` (sub-pixel pattern, too many repeats).
- New `crates/render/src/wide.rs`: `dashed` samples the centre line per segment with the same width interpolation as `fill::wide_polyline` (tapers, arc segments), then fills the band between each dash's start and end; a dot becomes a line across the band.
- PLINEGEN as for thin polylines: on, the pattern runs along the whole polyline; off, it restarts at every vertex.
- `lib.rs`: the wide-polyline arm uses it when the polyline has a linetype; without one, nothing changes.

I also rendered a tapered, arc-bulged polyline with DASHED and a wide DASHDOT one to PNG and looked at it: the dashes follow the taper and the arc, and the dots show as ticks across the band.

## Test plan
- New `crates/render/tests/wide_pline_linetype.rs`: a 3.0-long, 0.2-wide DASHED polyline fills 0.4 (four 0.5 dashes) instead of 0.6, leaves the first gap empty and keeps the full width; with two 0.6 segments the filled area is 0.2 per segment and 0.19 with PLINEGEN. Both fail on main (area 0.6 / 0.24).

title: -BLOCK erases the selection and asks before redefining (fixes #307)
author: vangel76
body:
Fixes #307.

## The problem
- `-BLOCK` was only an alias of `BLOCK`, and `Session::start` strips the leading `-`. So the command-line `-BLOCK` always converted the selection to a reference to the new block. AutoCAD's `-BLOCK` erases the objects instead. A script that runs `-BLOCK` and then `INSERT`s the block ended up with an extra reference at the base point.
- Typing a block name that already exists replaced that block's definition without asking. AutoCAD asks `Block "<name>" already exists. Redefine it? [Yes/No] <N>:` first.

- **`-block` is now its own command** (alias `-B`, label "Create Block", no menu entry):

title: Right-to-left drawing text: bidi and Arabic-script shaping (Persian, Arabic, Urdu)
author: vangel76
body:
Fixes #287.

## The problem

Drawing text was placed one glyph per code point, left to right. Persian, Arabic and Urdu came out as disconnected isolated letters in reverse order, and numbers and Latin words inside them landed in the wrong place. Our stroke font has no Arabic letters, and on systems with several CJK font weights installed, the bounded per-character fallback search (#173) used up its file budget on CJK fonts before it reached an Arabic font. Arabic in a stroke-font style was then drawn as missing-glyph boxes.

## Changes

- **Bidi** (`crates/fonts/src/bidi.rs`, new): the Unicode Bidirectional Algorithm per line, using `unicode-bidi` (MIT/Apache-2.0, no dependencies). It provides visual runs, per-character levels, L2 reordering and bracket mirroring. The paragraph direction comes from the first strong character, so `قیمت 25 تومان` and `فایل CAD باز` keep their numbers and Latin words in order.
- **Shaping** (`crates/fonts/src/complex.rs`, new): every line that contains right-to-left text is split into visual runs. Each run is then split into pieces by the font that draws them: the text's font, a fallback font (FONTFALLBACK, FONTALT, installed fonts) or the stroke font. Each font piece is shaped with **`harfrust`** before its glyphs are placed. That gives OpenType GSUB/GPOS: init/medi/fina/isol forms, lam-alef and other ligatures, ZWNJ (common in Persian) and ZWJ, mark positioning and mirroring. Because shaping happens per piece and before glyph lookup, Persian in a stroke-font style is joined by the fallback font. Joiners and combining marks stay in the piece before them, and a word stays in one fallback face when that face covers it. Invisible format characters (ZWNJ, LRM/RLM, embeddings, isolates) take no space and no longer draw boxes.
- **Fallback for fonts without OpenType Arabic features:** `harfrust` has no Arabic fallback shaper. When a face has no `init`/`medi`/`fina` lookups but maps the Unicode presentation forms (older fonts), the run is pr…

title: Draw the text of complex linetypes along the line (fixes #312)
author: vangel76
body:
Fixes #312.

## The problem

Complex linetypes with embedded text (the built-in FENCELINE1, gas/hot-water style linetypes read from DXF files, whose text elements survive round trips since #216) drew only their dashes: the renderer treated the text element as part of the gap, so nothing appeared on screen or in PNG/SVG/PDF output.

## Changes

- New `crates/render/src/linetype_text.rs` (kept apart from text shaping; it only calls `cadcraft_fonts::place`). For every run that `linetype::apply` dashes, each text element is placed where the element that carries it ends (the position of the bracket in a `.lin` definition, matching how DXF attaches `74`/`9` to the preceding `49`), at every repeat of the pattern laid out from the start of the run like the dashes:
  - height = element scale (`46`) × the text style's fixed height when it has one × the linetype scale (LTSCALE × CELTSCALE × the PSLTSCALE viewport factor);
  - X/Y offsets (`44`/`45`, × linetype scale) along and across the line;
  - rotation (`50`) relative to the line direction, or absolute when `74` bit 1 is set;
  - font, width factor, oblique and backwards/upside-down from the text style.
  
  The text is shaped once per element and moved to each anchor. A run drawn continuous (pattern below `min_dash`, or > 50 000 repeats) draws no text; previews with `Options::text` off skip it; at most 10 000 texts per run; non-finite scales/offsets/rotations are ignored.
- **Shapes** (`74` bit 4) need SHX shape files, which CADCraft doesn't read: they keep drawing nothing (documented in the module).
- **Upright** (`U=`) rotation isn't drawn specially: the drawing model has no flag for it (the DXF Reference documents only bit 1 for absolute rotation), so such text is drawn as relative.
- `render/src/lib.rs`: the linetype stroke draws the texts after the dashes (7 lines in the `stroke` closure). It passes the entity's resolved colour straight through, so it works unchanged with #285's `Ink`.
- FENCELINE1 (our own definitio…

title: Object snaps find the geometry inside block references (fixes #314)
author: vangel76
body:
Fixes #314.

## The problem

Running object snaps saw only the insertion point of a block reference. `osnap` collects candidates from `EntityKind::prims()`, and for an `INSERT` that returns just the insertion point. Endpoint, Midpoint, Center, Quadrant, Intersection, Perpendicular, Tangent (including deferred) and Nearest never found the lines, arcs and circles inside a block. That rules out snapping to doors, fixtures, title blocks and most geometry in real DWG/DXF files.

## Changes

`crates/engine/src/snap.rs` only:

- Per-object candidate collection moved into a small `Sink::object(kind, xf)`. Top-level objects go through it unchanged (`xf = None`).
- `block_leaves` walks a reference's block the way the renderer draws it:
  - nested references are expanded down to `MAX_BLOCK_DEPTH`
  - MINSERT columns and rows are included
  - attribute definitions are skipped, and so are hidden objects and objects on a layer that is off or frozen (objects on layer 0 follow the reference)
  - a shared budget of 20 000 objects per query bounds the work on hostile files
- `xform_prim` places each primitive exactly:
  - a similarity transform (rotation, uniform scale, mirroring) keeps circles and arcs as circles and arcs; under a mirror the arc's ends swap and its direction flips
  - a non-uniform scale or shear turns them into ellipses and elliptical arcs. `xform_ellipse` finds the new principal axes from the transformed conjugate diameters and shifts the parameters to match, reversing them under a mirror.
  - splines map their control and fit points, which is exact for B-splines
- Block primitives far from the cursor are culled, so the 200-primitive intersection window still holds the nearby geometry.
- Insertion also snaps to a reference's visible attributes.

## Test plan

- New `crates/engine/tests/snap_blocks.rs` (both tests fail on `main`):
  - `snaps_inside_rotated_scaled_and_mirrored_references`: END, MID, CEN, QUA, PER and INS in a rotated, scaled reference; a mirrored, n…

title: Dimensions take viewport layer colours, leader arrows their style's DIMSCALE, attributes their own properties (fixes #313)
author: vangel76
body:
Fixes #313.

## The problem

Three spots in `render/src/lib.rs` resolved properties differently from the rest of the drawing:

1. `dimension()` read the layer colour straight from the layer table, so a dimension inside a layout viewport ignored that viewport's layer colour override (everything else uses `Ctx::layer_color`).
2. The LEADER arrowhead was `DIMASZ × header DIMSCALE`: a leader drawn with a style whose DIMSCALE is 10 lost its arrow size as soon as another style became current, and DIMSCALE 0 gave a zero-size arrow. Dimensions already use the style's DIMSCALE (`DimStyle::effective_scale`).
3. Attributes were drawn with the INSERT's colour at lineweight 0, and shown even when their layer was off.

## Changes

- Dimensions: `ctx.layer_color(layer)` (one line), so ByLayer dimension, extension, arrow and text colours take the viewport override.
- Leaders: arrow size = `DIMASZ × effective_scale(DIMSCALE)` of the leader's style (style DIMSCALE, else the drawing's, else 1), the same rule dimensions use.
- Attributes: the drawing model keeps no colour/layer/lineweight on an attribute itself, and AutoCAD copies them from the attribute definition when it creates the attribute. So each attribute is now drawn with the properties of the block's ATTDEF with the same tag (any case), resolved in the block reference's context: ByLayer = the definition's layer (layer 0 = the block reference's layer, as for block contents, including viewport overrides and frozen layers), ByBlock = the block reference's colour/lineweight, explicit colour/lineweight as set. It is hidden when that layer is off or frozen. An attribute without a definition keeps the reference's colour and now gets its lineweight instead of 0. Lineweights still apply only with `Options::lineweights`.
  - Follow-up, not in this PR: per-attribute overrides read from DXF (`62`/`370` on an ATTRIB) or set by -ATTEDIT need fields on `Attrib`. That touches doc/io/engine and the `Attrib { … }` literals in open PRs, so it s…

title: fonts: embed craft-fonts when built with CRAFT_FONTS_DIR
author: vangel76
body:
Fixes #317.

## The problem

AGENTS.md, `NOTICE` and the packaging scripts (`packaging/env.sh`, `macos/package.sh`, `windows/package.ps1`) say that builds made with `CRAFT_FONTS_DIR` embed the [craft-fonts](https://github.com/storytold/craft-fonts) fonts and ship their OFL licences. No Rust code read the variable, though. Such a build embedded nothing, shipped licences for fonts it didn't contain, and never got the fonts. The web build has no system fonts, so Japanese or Arabic text there was always drawn as missing-glyph boxes.

## Changes

- **`crates/fonts/build.rs`**: craft-fonts' `docs/integration.md` recipe, as in pdfcraft (`crates/fonts/build.rs`) and photocraft (`crates/text/build.rs`).
  - It reads `$CRAFT_FONTS_DIR/fonts/manifest.txt` and generates `CRAFT_FONTS: &[CraftFont]`, one `include_bytes!` per line, in manifest order.
  - It reruns when `CRAFT_FONTS_DIR` or `CRAFT_FONTS_REQUIRED` changes. A bad checkout gives a warning, or an error when `CRAFT_FONTS_REQUIRED=1` is set.
  - If the variable is unset or empty, the slice is empty and the build is unchanged.
  - **Web builds** (wasm32) embed only BIZ UDPGothic Regular and the `Arab` faces (≈5.5 MB, the same set as pdfcraft). The wasm is about 13 MB today and the per-file hosting limit is 25 MiB.
  - **Noto Sans CJK is never embedded.** It is Source Han Sans, an Adobe design, and AGENTS.md bars Adobe fonts. pdfcraft skips it the same way (`BARRED_FAMILIES`).
- **`crates/fonts/src/craft_fonts.rs`** (new): `CraftFont` (same fields as in the siblings) and `CRAFT_FONTS`, re-exported from `cadcraft_fonts`. `CraftFont::stem()` gives the key the font table uses, for example `bizudpgothic-regular`.
- **`crates/fonts/src/ttf.rs`**: the font table's `paths` now map a stem to a `Source`, either an installed `File` or a `Static` font compiled into the binary. The embedded fonts are listed there when the table is first used. That means:
  - name lookup (`find("BIZ UDPGothic")`, `find("BIZ UDPGothic Bold")`) finds the…

title: Grip edits act on the whole selection (fixes #320)
author: vangel76
body:
Fixes #320.

## The problem

With several objects selected, a grip edit only changed the object whose grip was clicked. `Session::grip_edit` always sent `handles: [handle]`, and the stretch path of `grip.move` edits a single object. So:

- stretching the shared corner of two selected lines pulled them apart, where AutoCAD drags every coincident grip of the selection;
- the Move, Rotate, Scale and Mirror grip modes moved one object, where AutoCAD transforms the whole selection about the hot grip.

## Changes

- `grips.rs`, `Session::grip_edit`: passes the hot object first, followed by the rest of the current selection. Stretch uses `handle` plus `handles`. The other modes use `handles` plus `baseHandle`/`index`, so the base is still the hot grip.
- `cmd/gripcmds.rs`, grip stretch (`grip.move` without `mode: "move"`, and `grip.stretch`):
  - after the hot grip is stretched, each other object in `handles` that has a grip on the same point (within 1e-9 relative) stretches that grip to the same place
  - locked objects and edits that would be degenerate are skipped
  - everything happens in one command, so it is one undo step
  - the result also lists the edited handles
- JSON callers that pass only `handle` behave as before: just that object is edited.

## Test plan

- New `crates/engine/tests/grip_selection.rs::grip_edits_act_on_the_selection` (fails on `main`):
  - stretching a shared corner moves both connected lines and leaves a third selected line alone, in one undo step
  - Move and Rotate grip modes transform all three selected lines
  - an unselected line is not dragged along
- Existing `grips_tests` (`grip_modes`, `line_and_circle_grips`, …) pass unchanged.
- `cargo test -j 4 -p cadcraft-engine`: all pass.
- `cargo clippy -j 4 -p cadcraft-engine --all-targets -- -D warnings`: clean.
- `cargo check -j 4 --target wasm32-unknown-unknown -p cadcraft-engine`: OK.
- `rustfmt --edition 2024` on the touched files.

title: Nearest snap picks the closest object in any drawing order (fixes #323)
author: vangel76
body:
Fixes #323.

## The problem

When Nearest (NEA) was on and a circle lay within the aperture, the circle's nearest point always replaced the best candidate found so far, even when that candidate was closer to the cursor. A line 0.1 from the cursor lost to a circle 0.7 away whenever the line had been drawn first. The snapped point therefore depended on drawing order.

## Changes

- `crates/engine/src/snap.rs` (Nearest search in `osnap_with`): every candidate, including the circle's own closest point, now goes through one distance comparison, so the closest point of all nearby objects wins.
- `crates/engine/tests/snap_nearest.rs`: a new regression test. It draws a line and a circle in both orders and checks that the closer line wins, then checks that the circle wins when it is the closer one.

## Test plan

- `cargo test -j 4 -p cadcraft-engine --test snap_nearest` fails on main (it snaps to the circle at (0, 0.8)) and passes with this change.
- `cargo test -j 4 -p cadcraft-engine`
- `cargo clippy -j 4 -p cadcraft-engine --all-targets -- -D warnings`
- `cargo check -j 4 --target wasm32-unknown-unknown -p cadcraft-engine`
- `rustfmt --edition 2024` on the touched files

title: Typed angles follow ANGBASE, ANGDIR and AUNITS (fixes #326)
author: vangel76
body:
Fixes #326.

## The problem

Every typed angle went through `units::parse_angle`, which read a bare number as decimal degrees measured counterclockwise from +X. This applied to polar points `@d<a` / `d<a` and to angle prompts. As a result:

- ANGBASE and ANGDIR were ignored. With 0 = north and clockwise angles, `@10<90` went to (0, 10) instead of (10, 0).
- AUNITS was ignored. In a radians or grads drawing, `@10<1.5708` was read as 1.57°.
- `SETVAR ANGBASE 90` stored 90 into a header variable that, like `$ANGBASE` in DXF (and ANGBASE in DWG/ODA), holds radians.

## Changes

`crates/engine/src/units.rs` adds `AngleSettings`, built from the header's AUNITS, ANGBASE (radians) and ANGDIR. It reads an angle in three ways:

- **`amount`**: the angle's size. A bare number is in AUNITS: 0, 1 and 4 read degrees, 2 grads, 3 radians. Explicit units override AUNITS: `30d`, `45d30'15"`, `0.5r`, `100g`. A leading `-` now negates a whole deg/min/sec angle; before, `-45d30'` was -44.5°.
- **`rotation`**: the amount, turned clockwise when ANGDIR is 1.
- **`direction`**: the amount, measured from ANGBASE in the ANGDIR sense. Surveyor's bearings (`N45dE`) are absolute. The AutoCAD-style overrides `<<a` (degrees) and `<<<a` (AUNITS) measure from +X counterclockwise.

`Session::angle_settings()` returns the settings of the current drawing.

`parse_angle(s)` keeps its signature and meaning: the default settings (degrees from +X, counterclockwise). `prompt::parse_point` also keeps its signature and meaning. The new `prompt::parse_point_with(text, last, &AngleSettings)` handles typed points (`d<a`, `d<<a`, `d<<<a`).

What reads the drawing's settings now:

- **Typed points**: `Session::typed`, and the hot-grip entry in `ui-egui/src/cmdline.rs`.
- **Directions**: TEXT, INSERT and RECTANG rotation, XLINE Ang, ROTATE Reference (both angles), and the ARC tangent direction.
- **Rotation**: the XLINE Reference angle.
- **Amounts (units only)**: ARC included angle, ELLIPSE arc angles and rotation…

title: Save As to an image or PDF exports without renaming the drawing (fixes #327)
author: vangel76
body:
Fixes #327.

## The problem

SAVEAS (and QSAVE with a `path`) to a `.svg`, `.png` or `.pdf` file wrote the export. Then `commit_save` marked the drawing as saved under that file:

- the title became `p2.png`;
- the unsaved changes were cleared, so closing or quitting no longer asked "Save changes?";
- a later Save wrote the PNG again.

No DXF/DWG of the drawing was ever written, so the work could be lost without a prompt.

The desktop Save As dialog offers SVG/PNG/PDF filters, and the MCP `save` tool documents image export by extension, so both lead here. The control channel's `app.save {path}` and `saveas {"path": …}` in scripts do too. `save_reporting` and the `save_reports_not_saved` test already treat an image export as "not a save of the drawing".

## Changes

- `crates/engine/src/cmd/file.rs`: `commit_save` stores the file as before. For a path that isn't a drawing file (`is_drawing_file`: not `.dxf`/`.dwg`/no extension), it stops there. The drawing keeps its name, title and unsaved changes, as with AutoCAD's image export commands. DXF/DWG saves are unchanged.
- The MCP `save` tool description and `docs/mcp.md` say that an image/PDF path exports and leaves the drawing's name and unsaved state alone.
- New test `crates/engine/tests/save_as_export.rs`. It checks:
  - SAVEAS to png/svg/pdf writes each file, and the drawing stays dirty under its own name;
  - QSAVE `{path: …png}` behaves the same;
  - a plain QSAVE still has no file name;
  - SAVEAS to `.dxf` still renames the drawing and clears the dirty state;
  - a later export keeps the `.dxf` name, so QSAVE writes the DXF again.

## Test plan

- `cargo test -p cadcraft-engine --test save_as_export` passes, and fails without the fix (`png: an export must not clear the unsaved changes`).
- `cargo test -j 4 -p cadcraft-engine`, `-p cadcraft-mcp`, `-p cadcraft-ui-egui`: all pass.
- `cargo clippy -j 4 -p cadcraft-engine --all-targets -- -D warnings` and `-p cadcraft-mcp` are clean.

title: JSON handles: reject a malformed handle instead of using the selection (fixes #330)
author: vangel76
body:
Fixes #330.

## The problem

`targets()` in `crates/engine/src/cmd/mod.rs` picks the objects for about 70 commands that take objects in JSON (`erase`, `move`, `copy`, `rotate`, `scale`, `list`, `area`…). It read `handles`, then `handle`, and otherwise used the current selection. A value it couldn't read wasn't an error:

- a `handle` that isn't hex (`"#101"`, `"0x101"`, `""`, `-1`) fell through to the **selection**;
- `handles` that isn't an array (`"handles": "101"`) fell through to the **selection**;
- unreadable entries in `handles` were dropped without a word.

So `erase {handle: "#101"}` replied `{"erased": 2}` after erasing the two selected circles. Over the MCP bridge (`cadcraft-cli mcp --connect`), the fallback is whatever the user has selected in the window.

## Changes

- `targets()`:
  - A `handles` value must be an array. Every entry must be a hex string or a non-negative integer, otherwise the call fails with an error naming the bad value.
  - A `handle` value must also be readable, otherwise the call fails in the same way.
  - The selection is used only when neither key is given, or when it is `null`, so JSON clients that send `null` for an optional parameter keep working.
  - Well-formed handles behave exactly as before. That includes ones that don't exist, which commands still count as 0.
- New test `crates/engine/tests/malformed_handles.rs`. With two selected circles, `erase`/`move` given these values fail and change nothing:
  - `#100`, `""`, `-1` and `0x101` as `handle`;
  - a string as `handles`;
  - `["100", "#102"]` as `handles`.

  It also checks that well-formed handles act on exactly that object, and that `handles: null` still uses the selection.

## Test plan

- `cargo test -p cadcraft-engine --test malformed_handles` passes, and fails without the fix (`erase {"handle":"#100"}: Object {"erased": Number(2)}`).
- `cargo test -j 4 -p cadcraft-engine`, `-p cadcraft-ui-egui`, `-p cadcraft-mcp`: all pass.
- `cargo clippy -j 4 -p cadcraft-engine -…

title: Midpoint, Perpendicular and Tangent snaps on elliptical arcs and splines; Quadrant stays on the arc (fixes #332)
author: vangel76
body:
Fixes #332.

## The problem
Object snaps on ellipses and splines were incomplete: Midpoint never snapped on an elliptical arc or a spline, Quadrant on an elliptical arc offered all four quadrant points of the whole ellipse (two of them off the arc), and Perpendicular / Tangent from a base point only knew lines, circles and circular arcs.

## Changes
- `crates/engine/src/snap/curves.rs` (new submodule of `snap`):
  - **Midpoint** halfway along the length of an elliptical arc or open spline (none for a full ellipse or closed spline, like circles).
  - **Tangent** from a base point to an ellipse or elliptical arc exactly, by mapping the ellipse onto the unit circle (an affine map keeps tangency); only points on the arc count.
  - **Perpendicular** (ellipses, splines) and **Tangent** (splines) numerically: the parameter range is sampled (512 samples), each sign change of the condition is narrowed by 60 bisection steps, and a root is kept only when the normalised condition is really zero there (no false hits at spline kinks). At most 16 solutions per curve; a circle seen from its centre (every point qualifies) gives none. Hostile geometry (NaN, zero axes, invalid splines) gives no snap, never a panic.
- `snap.rs`: Quadrant on an elliptical arc keeps only the quadrant points within its sweep; Midpoint, Perpendicular and Tangent use the functions above. All solutions are offered and the one nearest the cursor wins, as for circles. This also covers circles and arcs that a non-uniformly scaled block reference turns into ellipses (#318).

## Test plan
- New `crates/engine/tests/snap_curves.rs` (an elliptical arc typed as `ellipse a c 0,0 4,0 2 0 90`, a spline typed as `spline 0,0 2,2 4,0`): the elliptical arc's Midpoint halves its length, Quadrant snaps only on the arc, Tangent from (6,1) and Perpendicular from (10,10) land on the arc with the right geometry, the spline's Midpoint, Perpendicular and Tangent. All three tests fail on `main`.
- Unit tests in `snap/curves.rs` (el…

title: MCP: invalid tool arguments are -32602 errors; query_entities counts all matches and windows by geometry (fixes #335)
author: vangel76
body:
Fixes #335.

## The problem

MCP tool calls with arguments that don't fit the tool's schema were guessed at instead of reported: `query_entities` ignored a malformed `window` or a non-string `type`/`layer` and returned every entity, `command_line {}` pressed Enter (repeating the last command), `script {}` succeeded doing nothing. Unknown tools came back as a normal `isError` result rather than the JSON-RPC `-32602` the MCP spec (2025-06-18, Error Handling) uses, and an empty batch `[]` got no reply. `query_entities`' `count` was the page size, so truncation by `limit` was invisible, and its window test was a bounding-box overlap. `list_commands`' filter matched anywhere in the command JSON (QSELECT came first for "circle").

## Changes

- `crates/mcp/src/tools.rs`: `call_tool` checks the arguments against the tool's own `inputSchema` (object, `required`, and `type`/`items`/`minItems`/`maxItems`/`minimum` of each given property; `null` = not given) and returns `Err` for protocol errors: unknown tool, non-object `arguments`, missing or mistyped argument. The `query_entities` schema now describes `window` as two `[x, y]` pairs and adds `crossing`, `offset` and `minimum: 0` on `limit`/`offset`. `list_commands` filters on id, label and aliases.
- `crates/mcp/src/server.rs`: those errors are answered as JSON-RPC `-32602`; an empty batch is a single `-32600` Invalid Request (JSON-RPC 2.0 §6). Tool failures (bad point, unknown command) stay `isError` results.
- `crates/engine/src/cmd/inquiry.rs` (`entities`, also reached via the control channel's `engine.execute`): malformed `window`, non-string `type`/`layer`, non-integer or negative `limit`/`offset` and a non-boolean `crossing` are `BadParams` errors. The result is `{count (all matches), returned, offset, entities}`. A window matches objects whose geometry is inside it or crosses it; `crossing: false` means entirely inside.
- `crates/engine/src/select.rs`: the per-object window/crossing test of `select_window_with` moved …

title: Dimensions snap; justified text snaps and grips at its alignment point; grid snap follows SNAPBASE/SNAPANG; OSNAPHATCH (fixes #334)
author: vangel76
body:
Fixes #334.

## The problem
- Dimensions offered no object snaps at all; AutoCAD snaps into a dimension's geometry (Endpoint on the dimension and extension line ends, Node on the definition points).
- TEXT justified other than left-baseline, as read from DXF, snapped (Insertion) and showed its grip at group 10 (the computed start point) instead of the alignment point (group 11). Text created in CADCraft wasn't affected because both points coincide.
- Grid snap always started at 0,0 along the axes: no SNAPBASE / SNAPANG.
- Hatch boundaries snapped; AutoCAD leaves hatches out of object snaps while OSNAPHATCH is 0, its default.

## Changes
- `snap.rs`: a dimension with a block (read from a file) snaps to the block's objects, expanded through the block-reference expansion from #318; one without a block snaps to the lines generated for it (`render::dimension_in`): Endpoint on their ends, Midpoint on straight pieces, and Intersection / Nearest / Perpendicular through the nearby-primitive list. Node on the definition points its kind uses.
- `Text::justify_point()` (doc): the alignment point for justified text, the start point for left-baseline, aligned and fit text. The Insertion snap (text and attributes) and the grips of TEXT, ATTDEF and attributes use it (grip edits move by the grip's delta, so they keep working).
- `snap::grid_snap` takes the grid's base and angle; `snap::grid_frame` reads SNAPBASE and SNAPANG (degrees) from the drawing. New header defaults SNAPBASE 0,0 and SNAPANG 0; SETVAR now accepts `x,y` typed for any point header variable (it used to store the text).
- New session variable OSNAPHATCH (default 0): hatches, including those inside blocks, are left out of object snaps unless it is 1. The canvas passes it as `snap::mode::HATCH`, a flag outside the OSMODE bits, so `snap::osnap` keeps its signature.

Not changed: the displayed grid doesn't turn with SNAPANG yet (only snapping does).

title: Refuse edits whose result has infinite or undefined coordinates (fixes #338)
author: vangel76
body:
Fixes #338.

## The problem

Inputs to the modify commands are checked for being finite, but their results aren't. Finite inputs can still overflow: moving a circle by `[1e308, 1e308]` twice put its centre at infinity, and nothing complained. Inspect then showed `null` coordinates, the extents went `null`, and a DXF save wrote the centre as `0.0`, so the object moved to the origin on reopen. Scaling, rotating or mirroring a far-out object, arrays with huge spacing, and large offsets do the same. JSON parameters and typed values themselves are already safe: `serde_json` can't carry NaN or infinity, and typed points/numbers reject `nan`, `inf` and `1e999`.

## Changes

One check after commands, rather than one per transform:

- New `crates/engine/src/finite.rs`: `first_non_finite(before, after)` finds the objects a command changed (model space, layouts, changed blocks). Chunks shared with the previous drawing are skipped, so only edited objects are looked at. An object fails if any number in its serialized fields is NaN or infinite (a small serde `Serializer` that only looks at floats, so every entity type is covered without listing fields) or its extents overflow (a circle at 1e308 with radius 1e308). `Session::refuse_non_finite` puts back the drawing and selection and returns `BadParams` "the result is too large: object … would get infinite or undefined coordinates. Nothing was changed".
- `crates/engine/src/lib.rs`: `Session::execute` runs the check for undoable commands after the command and its associativity/constraint updates, before the undo step, so a refused edit records no undo step. This covers every JSON call (MCP `execute`, control channel) and grip edits, which go through `execute`. `finish` runs it when an interactive command ends and echoes the message. Commands outside undo (UNDO/REDO, views) aren't checked, so undoing back to an imported object that already had odd values still works.

title: INSERT inserts exploded (*NAME) and drawing files (fixes #340)
author: vangel76
body:
Fixes #340.

## The problem
`-INSERT` accepted only the name of a block already in the drawing. `*NAME` (insert exploded) and a drawing file (`C:\parts\bolt.dxf`, `bolt=C:\parts\bolt.dwg`) printed `Block "…" not found.` and stayed at the name prompt, so in a script the insertion point, scale and rotation that followed were each read as another block name. The JSON form had no way to insert a file.

## Changes
- **`*NAME`**: the block's objects are inserted as separate objects. After the insertion point INSERT asks one scale factor (`Specify scale factor for XYZ axes <1>`) and the rotation, and no attribute values. JSON: `name: "*NAME"` sets `explode`.
- **Drawing files** (new `crates/engine/src/cmd/blocks/insert_file.rs`): a path (it has a folder separator or a .dwg/.dxf extension and isn't the name of a block), `NAME=path` or `NAME=` (the file `NAME`, trying .dwg then .dxf) is read through the host's io read hook, like OPEN, so the engine stays I/O-agnostic. It defines a block named after the file (or `NAME`) from the file's model space, with the file's `$INSBASE` as the base point. The layers, linetypes, text/dimension/multileader/table styles and blocks the file brings are added; a name this drawing already has keeps this drawing's definition, and colliding anonymous blocks get fresh names. Handles are new and associative dimension links are dropped. The definition happens on a copy of the drawing and is applied only if it succeeds (an invalid name or a block that would contain itself changes nothing).
- A plain path whose block already exists asks `Block "bolt" already exists. Redefine it? [Yes/No] <N>`. No keeps the existing definition. `NAME=path` redefines without asking. A file that can't be read is reported, and INSERT asks for the name again.
- JSON: `insert {file, name?, at, …}` defines (or redefines) the block from the file and inserts it, without any dialog. The params doc is updated.

title: JSON draw/annotation commands refuse invalid sizes and coincident points (fixes #343)
author: vangel76
body:
Fixes #343.

## The problem

The JSON forms of several draw and annotation commands accepted invalid sizes and coincident points and reported success. `Circle::new` and `Arc::new` silently made a negative radius positive. `donut` made its diameters absolute. Negative fillet, chamfer and width values were clamped to 0 without a message. A non-integer polygon `sides` count was replaced by 4, and a zero hatch scale was clamped to 1e-9. Coincident points produced zero-size polygons, zero-length lines and zero-radius dimensions. `ddptype` and `dimstyle` stored out-of-range PDMODE, DIMTXT, DIMASZ and DIMSCALE values.

## Changes

- `cmd/mod.rs`: two small helpers.
  - `size_param(cmd, p, key, zero_ok)` returns `None` when the key is absent, otherwise a finite number > 0 (≥ 0 with `zero_ok`). Any other value is an error: `` `key` must be positive `` / `` `key` must be zero or positive ``.
  - `distinct_points` drops consecutive repeated points.
- CIRCLE: `radius`/`diameter` are checked before `Circle::new`. The final radius must be > 1e-12, the same bound as the `circle.*` variants.
- ARC: a negative `radius` is refused before `Arc::new`. A zero radius still gives the #85 message.
- POLYGON: a `sides` value that is present but not a whole number is refused (it was replaced by 4). `radius` must be positive, and `edge` endpoints must differ.
- DONUT: `inside` ≥ 0, `outside` > 0, and `inside` ≤ `outside`.
- RECTANG: `fillet`, `width` and both `chamfer` distances must be ≥ 0.
- PLINE: `width`, `startWidth` and `endWidth` must be ≥ 0.
- LINE: repeated points are dropped, as the interactive LINE ignores a point picked twice. The call fails when fewer than 2 different points remain, and no closing line is drawn back to the same point.
- SPLINE: needs 2 or more different fit points.
- HATCH/GRADIENT: `scale` must be > 0. TABLE: `rowHeight` and `colWidth` must be > 0 when given.
- DIMRADIUS/DIMDIAMETER: `point` must differ from `center`. DIMANGULAR (3-point form): `p1` and `p2` mus…

title: TL/ML/BL text is placed by its alignment point (fixes #342)
author: vangel76
body:
Fixes #342.

## The problem
The DXF Reference makes group 11 (second alignment point) the point a TEXT is placed by for every justification other than baseline-left. Group 10 is then a point computed on the baseline. The renderer (`cadcraft_fonts::place`) and `text_box` in `crates/doc/src/extents.rs` (extents, window selection, picking) used group 10 for every **Left** text and then shifted it again by the vertical alignment. So TL and ML text from a DXF was drawn, measured and picked one alignment offset too low, and BL one offset too high. For TL that is a whole text height. Text drawn with our own TEXT command didn't show it, because it stores the same point in both fields.

## Changes
- `fonts::place` and `doc::extents::text_box` place TL/ML/BL text from its alignment point, like every other justification except baseline-left. Aligned and fit text still spans group 10 to group 11. `text_box` uses `Text::justify_point()` from #337, so the renderer, extents and picking now agree with the Insertion snap and the grip.
- `dxf_read::mirror_text`: a mirrored (extrusion 0,0,-1) TL/ML/BL text turns right-justified with its alignment point kept. Before, it used group 10, which put it off by the same offset.
- `properties.set {position}` on a TEXT moves the whole text so its justification point lands on `position` (insertion and alignment point together). Before, it set only group 10, which doesn't move justified text. Without this, a TL text drawn by TEXT would stop moving through Properties now that it is placed by its alignment point.

## Test plan
- New `crates/io/tests/text_left_justify.rs`: TL, ML and BL TEXT read from DXF, with group 10 computed as AutoCAD writes it. The rendered box and the extents sit at the alignment point. A mirrored TL text keeps its top-right at the alignment point. It fails on main (TL drawn at y −2…−1 instead of −1…0; mirrored TL one height low without the reader change).
- New `crates/engine/tests/text_left_justify.rs`: a TL text drawn by T…

title: Control channel: a timed-out request is cancelled, and the reply says whether it ran (fixes #345)
author: vangel76
body:
Fixes #345.

## The problem

The control server waits 60 s for the app and then replies `{"ok": false, "error": "timeout"}`. The request stays in the app's queue, though, and runs whenever the UI thread gets to it. A client that retries after the timeout applies the change twice, and a bare `"timeout"` doesn't tell it whether a retry is safe. This is the server-side twin of #102. #146 stopped the MCP bridge from resending a mutation whose reply was lost, and reported "may or may not have been applied" instead.

## Changes

- `crates/ui-egui/src/control.rs`: `ControlRequest` carries a shared state (queued / started / cancelled).
  - `ControlRequest::new` now returns a `PendingReply` instead of a bare `Receiver`.
  - `ControlRequest::begin()` moves queued → started. It returns false when the request was already cancelled.
  - `PendingReply::wait(timeout)` returns the reply. On timeout it tries to move queued → cancelled:
    - That works when the app hasn't started the request: it never runs, and the reply is `{"ok": false, "error": "timeout", "state": "not-run"}`.
    - Otherwise the request was already running. A reply that arrived at that moment still counts. If none did, the reply is `{"ok": false, "error": "timeout", "state": "may-have-run"}`, and the late result is discarded (the receiver is gone).
- `crates/ui-egui/src/lib.rs` (`drain_control`): skips requests whose `begin()` fails.
- `apps/cadcraft/src/control_server.rs`: uses `pending.wait(60 s)`.
- `crates/mcp/src/backend.rs`: when a reply has a timeout `state`, the bridge error says either that it is safe to send again, or, using #146's wording, that the call may or may not have been applied and the drawing should be inspected first. The bridge still never retries by itself.
- `docs/control-protocol.md`: documents the two timeout replies.

## Test plan

  - a request that times out before the app starts it replies `not-run`, and…

title: DWG and DXF keep ANGBASE/ANGDIR, fillet/chamfer, elevation and the snap grid (fixes #349)
author: vangel76
body:
Fixes #349.

## The problem

- Saving as DWG and reopening reset `ANGBASE`, `ANGDIR`, `FILLETRAD`, `CHAMFERA`, `CHAMFERB`, `ELEVATION` and `THICKNESS` to 0. The DWG holds them, and acadrust's DWG reader puts them into its document. Its DXF writer (0.6.3 and current `main`) leaves them out of the HEADER section, so the DXF our reader gets from the bridge doesn't have them.
- `SNAPBASE` and `SNAPANG` (used by grid snap since #337) were never saved, in DXF or DWG. Since R13 they're stored in the `*ACTIVE` VPORT record, which we wrote with a fixed 0,0 snap base and no rotation, and never read.

## Changes

- `crates/dwg`: after acadrust writes the DXF, `dwg_to_dxf` adds those seven variables to its HEADER section from acadrust's header model. It skips any variable the writer already wrote, so a future acadrust that writes them stays correct. If the text isn't laid out the way acadrust writes it, it's left unchanged. The opposite direction (DXF → DWG) already kept them.
- `crates/io` writer: the `*ACTIVE` VPORT record carries the snap base (13/23) from `SNAPBASE` and the snap rotation (50, degrees) from `SNAPANG`.
- `crates/io` reader: the first `*ACTIVE` VPORT record sets `SNAPBASE` and `SNAPANG` (finite values only).

`LWDEFAULT` isn't saved. AutoCAD keeps it as a per-user setting, not in the drawing. The unit variables (`AUNITS`, `AUPREC`, `LUNITS`, `LUPREC`, `INSUNITS`, `MEASUREMENT`) and `LTSCALE`, `DIMSCALE`, `PDMODE` and `PDSIZE` already survived DWG; the new test covers them too.

## Test plan

- New `crates/io/tests/dwg_header_vars.rs`: one drawing with non-default values of all the variables above, round-tripped through DXF and through DWG (`write(.., "x.dwg")` → `read`). Both tests fail on `main` and pass with the fix.
- `cargo clippy -j 4 -p cadcraft-dwg -p cadcraft-io --all-targets -- -D warnings`
- `cargo test -j 4 -p cadcraft-dwg -p cadcraft-io`

title: Control channel: headless and app reply alike to cmdline.input, state and app.open (fixes #351)
author: vangel76
body:
Fixes #351.

## The problem

The app's control channel and the headless MCP backend (`cadcraft-cli mcp`) serve the same methods, but their replies differed:

- `cmdline.input` with a refused line: headless reported it only in `error`, with an empty `output`. The app echoed it into `output` and the history, and had no `error` field.
- The command-line state from headless had no `accept`, `buffer` or `historyExpanded`.
- Headless `app.open` without a `path` reached the OPEN command, which then asked for `path` or `data`. The app answered `missing path` itself.

## Changes

I used the fuller form on both sides and only added fields, so nothing a client reads goes away.

- Both backends return the same command-line state: `prompt`, `running`, `keywords`, `accept`, `buffer`, `history`, `historyExpanded`. Headless has no command-line widget, so it always sends `buffer: ""` and `historyExpanded: false`.
- `cmdline.input` on both: a refused line is echoed to the history and `output`, as a user sees it, and the message is also in `error`. `error` is present only when the line was refused. `CadApp::cmdline` now returns the error it echoed, and callers that ignore the result are unchanged.
- Headless `app.open` without a string `path` fails with `missing path`, like the app.
- `docs/control-protocol.md` has a new "Command-line replies" section describing the shared shape, and the MCP `command_line` tool description mentions `error`.

The changes in `control.rs` and `lib.rs` are limited to the `cmdline.input` handler and `CadApp::cmdline`. They merge cleanly with #345's request-queue changes in the same files.

## Test plan

- New `crates/mcp/tests/cmdline_parity.rs` (headless) and `crates/ui-egui/tests/control_cmdline.rs` (the app's `control::handle` on a headless `CadApp`). Each checks the same three things: for a refused line, the key set and that the error is in `output` and the history; for an accepted line, no `error` and `accept`/`buffer` present, and `cmdline.state` has…

body:

These prompts all read a bare number as degrees counterclockwise from +X, so in a radians drawing `ROTATE … 1.5708` turned the objects by 1.57°. title: Copy and paste between drawings with their layers and blocks; PASTEORIG, PASTEBLOCK; right-click menu (part of #325)
author: vangel76
body:
Part of #325.

## The problem

- **Copying between drawings lost what the objects refer to.** The clipboard was already shared by the open drawings, but it held only the objects. Pasting into another drawing put a line on a layer the target didn't have onto a new default layer, so its colour and linetype were lost. A block reference ended up pointing at a block the target didn't have. Dimension and text styles were dropped the same way.
- **Cmd/Ctrl+C, X and V did nothing on the desktop.** egui delivers these keys as `Copy`, `Cut` and `Paste(text)` events rather than key presses, so the shortcut table never saw them. Only the Edit menu and typed commands worked.
- **PASTEORIG** (paste at the same coordinates) had no menu prompt machine and no checks. It wasn't in the right-click menu either, because the canvas had none: right-click was Enter, clear selection, or repeat.

## Changes

**Engine**
- New `cmd/clipboard.rs`. With the copied objects, the session clipboard keeps the layers, linetypes, text, dimension, multileader and table styles, and blocks (nested ones too) they use, taken from the source drawing. Pasting adds the ones the target lacks, as AutoCAD does:
  - a name the target already has keeps the target's definition;
  - a generated (`*U`, `*D`) block whose name is taken gets a fresh one;
  - pasted objects get new handles, and links to objects in the source drawing (associative dimension points) are dropped.
- **PASTECLIP** asks for an insertion point, which is where the clipboard's base point lands. The JSON form takes `at`.
- **PASTEORIG** pastes at the original coordinates without asking. As in AutoCAD, it works only in a drawing other than the one the objects were copied from: there it is greyed out in menus and refused when typed or called.
- **PASTEBLOCK** (Edit > Paste as Block, Cmd+Shift+V): the clipboard becomes a new `A$C…` block, with the clipboard's base point as its base, inserted at a point.

title: QDIM: one snap index per call, cap the input (fixes #356)
author: vangel76
body:
Fixes #356.

## The problem

With DIMASSOC on, each dimension QDIM added went through `add_dim` → `assoc::reassociate`, which scans the whole space for objects under the definition points. Every dimension adds an entity, so QDIM over many objects was quadratic (20,000 lines: about 28 s in a debug build). There was no cap on the input size either. DIMCONTINUE/DIMBASELINE had the same problem and were fixed in #281.

## Changes

- `crates/engine/src/cmd/annotate.rs` (`run_qdim`): builds `assoc::SnapIndex` (from #281) once per call when DIMASSOC is on and attaches `p13`/`p14` through it. The index picks the same snap as `find_snap`, and dimensions are no snap targets, so it stays valid while QDIM adds them.
- Like DIMCONTINUE/DIMBASELINE, QDIM refuses more than 100,000 objects (`handles`), or objects that give more than 100,000 distinct points, before anything is created (reuses `MAX_CHAIN`).

## Test plan

- New `crates/engine/tests/qdim.rs`:
  - Lines end to end, with a point on every joint and a circle around every midpoint: QDIM's associations equal the ones DIMREASSOCIATE (a full scan) gives for the same dimensions, and every point is attached.
  - 20,000 lines give 20,000 dimensions (0.5 s; about 28 s before the change). There are no timing asserts.
  - 100,001 handles, and a polyline with 100,002 vertices, are refused with an error that names the cap, and nothing is added.
- `cargo test -j 4 -p cadcraft-engine`, `cargo clippy -j 4 -p cadcraft-engine --all-targets -- -D warnings`, `cargo check --target wasm32-unknown-unknown -p cadcraft-engine`, `rustfmt --edition 2024` on the touched files.

title: Attributes keep their own layer, colour, linetype and lineweight; -ATTEDIT Layer/Color (fixes #358)
author: vangel76
body:
Fixes #358.

## The problem

An ATTRIB is an entity with its own layer, colour, linetype and lineweight, but `Attrib` had no fields for them. #313 draws attributes with their ATTDEF's properties. As a result:

- Properties set on one attribute in a DXF (groups 8/62/420/370/6 on the ATTRIB) were dropped on reading.
- Saving wrote every ATTRIB on its block reference's layer, with no colour, linetype or lineweight. Other programs showed attributes defined on another layer, or with a colour, differently from CADCraft.
- -ATTEDIT's Layer and Color options said "not available yet".

## Changes

- **doc**: `Attrib.props: AttribProps` holds an optional `layer`, `color`, `linetype` and `lineweight`. It is serde-defaulted and skipped when empty, so saved sessions and JSON are unchanged for untouched attributes. `AttribProps::over(&Common)` lays them over the definition's properties.
- **render**: an attribute is drawn with its own properties where set, else its definition's. ByBlock and layer 0 behave as before (the reference's). An attribute without a definition or properties is drawn exactly as before.
- **DXF read**: an ATTRIB's 62/420, 370 and 6 become its own colour, lineweight and linetype when present. Its layer (8) counts when it differs from the block reference's layer, because an attribute defined on layer 0 sits on the reference's layer. That is also what older CADCraft files wrote.
- **DXF write**: each ATTRIB gets the properties it is drawn with: its own, else its definition's, with layer 0 becoming the reference's layer. A ByLayer that replaces something else in the definition is written explicitly (62 = 256, 370 = −1, 6 = ByLayer), so it survives reopening. The entity groups 8/6/62/420/370 move into a shared `layer_and_props` helper, with identical output for other entities.
- **-ATTEDIT** (one at a time) now offers `[Value/Layer/Color/Next]`:
  - Layer asks for an existing layer name. The default is the attribute's current layer, and an unknown name is refused…

title: Control channel: cmdline.key replies like cmdline.input (fixes #360)
author: vangel76
body:
Fixes #360.

## The problem

When `cmdline.key` Enter was refused (for example, Enter repeats a command that is no longer available), headless (`cadcraft-cli mcp`) failed the whole call with `"ok": false`. The app's control channel dropped the error: it replied `"ok": true` and nothing reached the history. Pressing Enter in the app's command line does echo the error. Neither reply had `output`.

## Changes

- `crates/ui-egui/src/control.rs` and `crates/mcp/src/backend.rs` (`cmdline.key`): a refused Enter is echoed to the history, as the command-line widget does. The reply is the command-line state plus `output` (the lines Enter/Escape added) and `error`, which is present only when Enter was refused. This is the shape #352 (#351) gives `cmdline.input`. The call itself succeeds.
- `docs/control-protocol.md`: the `cmdline.key` row says it replies like `cmdline.input`.

#352 is merged now. This branch merges cleanly onto current main, and with it `cmdline.key` and `cmdline.input` reply with the same fields. The tests below pass on the merge.

## Test plan

- New `crates/mcp/tests/cmdline_key.rs` (headless) and `crates/ui-egui/tests/control_cmdline_key.rs` (app). Each has the same two tests:
  - After `close`, Enter (repeats CLOSE, which needs a drawing) replies ok with the `cmdline.state` fields plus `output` and `error`, and the error is in `output` and `history`.
  - Enter and Escape during CIRCLE reply with the state fields plus `output` (`*Cancel*`) and no `error`.
  - All four tests fail on main and pass with the change.

title: Keep egui on the System theme preference so the OS appearance is followed live (#301)
author: MarekSpodBiedry
body:
Fixes #301.

With View > Interface Theme > Use System Setting, `theme::apply` handed egui the resolved concrete theme (`ctx.set_theme(Light)`). egui then sends `ViewportCommand::SetTheme(Light)`, egui-winit calls `window.set_theme(Some(..))`, and on macOS winit installs an explicit window appearance and stops emitting `ThemeChanged`. So after the first frame the app never saw a later OS Light/Dark change until restart.

**Fix**
- `theme::apply` takes a `follow_system` flag. For the System choice it sets `egui::ThemePreference::System` (egui maps that to `SystemDefault`, i.e. no window override), so winit keeps reporting OS changes. Fixed Light/Dark choices still set the concrete preference, unchanged.
- `CadApp::logic` re-applies when the preference mode changes, not only when the shown theme changes (System showing Dark -> Dark must still pin the window; Dark -> System must unpin it).
- Our own palette resolution is unchanged: `ThemePref::resolve` still drives `Tokens`, and egui's own fallback for an unknown OS report (`fallback_theme`, Dark) matches `SYSTEM_FALLBACK`.

**Test**
`system_theme_keeps_egui_on_the_system_preference`: System -> egui preference is `System` (was `Light` before the fix), Dark -> `Dark`, back to System -> `System`.

The native OS appearance change itself cannot be exercised in a unit test; the test checks the preference egui receives, which is what decides whether the window is pinned.

title: DIMBASELINE spacing follows DIM* overrides and DIMSCALE 0 (fixes #364)
author: vangel76
body:
Fixes #364.

## The problem

DIMBASELINE offset each new dimension line by `DIMDLI × DIMSCALE` read from the bare dimension style. That had two effects:

- Since #129, `SETVAR DIMSCALE` / `SETVAR DIMDLI` are stored as overrides on new dimensions, so they never reached the baseline spacing. With `DIMSCALE 10`, the text is 1.8 high but the dimensions were stacked 0.38 apart, so they overlapped.
- A style with DIMSCALE 0 gave `0.38 × 1e-9` and put every baseline dimension on the same line. DIMSPACE's default spacing used the same `scale.max(1e-9)` expression.

## Changes

- `chained()` in `crates/engine/src/cmd/annotate.rs` builds the spacing from the continued dimension's style with its overrides applied. It multiplies by `effective_scale` with the drawing's DIMSCALE, the same scale the renderer draws the dimension at. A non-finite result falls back to 0.38.
- DIMSPACE's default spacing uses `effective_scale` too.

## Test plan

- New `crates/engine/tests/dim_baseline_spacing.rs`: baseline spacing checked for the plain style (0.38), `SETVAR DIMSCALE 10` (3.8), `SETVAR DIMDLI 1` (1.0) and a style with DIMSCALE 0 (0.38); DIMSPACE default checked with DIMSCALE 0 (0.76). It fails on `main` and passes with the fix.
- `cargo clippy -j 4 -p cadcraft-engine --all-targets -- -D warnings`: clean.
- `cargo test -j 4 --no-fail-fast -p cadcraft-engine`: all pass except `purge_prompts::verify_asks_for_each_name_and_absent_types_take_their_tokens`, which fails the same way on `main` without this change.
- `cargo check -j 4 --target wasm32-unknown-unknown -p cadcraft-engine`: ok.
- `rustfmt --edition 2024` on the touched files.

title: Exploded dimension text and DXF dimension blocks match the drawn text (fixes #367)

When a dimension is exploded, and in the anonymous `*D` block that DXF save writes for each dimension (the block other programs draw), the text height came from the bare style's `DIMTXT × DIMSCALE` (`style.text_height * style.scale.max(1e-9)`). That height ignored:

- the dimension's overrides: `SETVAR DIMSCALE` / `DIMTXT` (stored as overrides since #129) and DIMOVERRIDE;

EXPLODE also always wrote `rotation: 0.0`, so aligned text (DIMTIH off) on a vertical dimension turned horizontal and lay across the dimension line.

They write its `text_height`, and the text style comes from the overridden style.
- EXPLODE keeps the drawn text angle (`text_angle`). It no longer adds an empty MTEXT when the dimension text is suppressed. The DXF block already skipped empty text.

title: ZOOM inside a layout viewport acts on the viewport; nXP sets its scale (fixes #370)
author: vangel76
body:
Fixes #370.

## The problem

Inside a layout viewport (`MSPACE`), `ZOOM` worked on the whole drawing window instead of the viewport:

- Extents, All, Window and Object fitted to the window's aspect and the paper view's height. After `ZOOM E` most of the model sat outside the viewport and was clipped.
- In, Out and nX zoomed about the model point under the middle of the window, so the content drifted out of the viewport.
- nXP was read as nX. `ZOOM 1/50XP`, the usual way to set a viewport to 1:50, scaled whatever zoom was already there.

## Changes

- `DocState` (`crates/engine/src/lib.rs`) gets the view that ZOOM works on. Inside an active, unlocked MSPACE viewport this is the viewport's own model view: its centre, its height and its aspect (`zoom_viewport`, `zoom_frame`, `zoom_aspect`). `set_zoom_frame` turns that view back into the screen view that the existing `store_view` mapping writes to the viewport, so view history and ZOOM Previous keep working.
- `ZOOM` (`crates/engine/src/cmd/view.rs`) and `Session::zoom_extents` use these:
  - Extents, All, Window and Object fit the viewport.
  - In, Out, nX and Center keep the viewport's centre or height.
  - nXP (JSON: `{"mode": "scale", "factor": n, "xp": true}`) sets the viewport's scale to n paper units per model unit.
- Unchanged:
  - A locked viewport keeps its scale, and ZOOM moves the sheet instead (as before).
  - The Model tab and paper space behave as before. nXP outside a viewport still acts like nX.

## Test plan

- New `crates/engine/tests/zoom_viewport.rs`:
  - `ZOOM E`, `2X`, `0.1XP`, `1/50XP` (applied twice) and `W` inside a viewport give the viewport's expected view centre and height, and the sheet never moves. This test fails on main.
  - A locked viewport and the Model tab keep their old behaviour.
- `cargo clippy -j 4 -p cadcraft-engine --all-targets -- -D warnings`: clean.

title: Undo/redo of LAYOUT Rename/New keeps the session on a layout that exists (fixes #371)
author: vangel76
body:
Fixes #371.

## The problem

`Session::undo` and `Session::redo` swap in the earlier or later drawing, but they leave `DocState::space` alone. Two cases left the session on a layout name that no longer existed:

- Undoing `LAYOUT Rename` while the renamed layout was current.
- Undoing `LAYOUT New` after switching to the new layout.

The tab then showed nothing (no sheet, no viewports), and every command that adds an entity failed with `no such space Paper("…")` until you picked another tab. Redo had the same problem the other way round.

## Changes

- New `DocState::follow_layout` (`crates/engine/src/lib.rs`), run after undo and redo swap the drawing. It does nothing if the current layout still exists. Otherwise:
  - If the layout was renamed (same tab order, and a name the drawing did not have before), the session follows it to its other name and keeps its paper view. AutoCAD also stays on the tab, under its old name.
  - Otherwise the session goes back to the Model tab and leaves MSPACE.

## Test plan

- New `crates/engine/tests/undo_layout_tab.rs`. Both tests fail on main:
  - Undoing a rename of the current layout stays on it under its old name: same paper view, sheet drawn, and `MVIEW` works after a later undo. Redo follows it back to the new name, and `LINE` works there.
  - Undoing the current layout's creation returns to Model (MSPACE cleared), and `LINE` works.
  - Undoing a rename of a layout that is not current leaves the current tab alone.
- `cargo clippy -j 4 -p cadcraft-engine --all-targets -- -D warnings`: clean.
- `cargo test -j 4 -p cadcraft-engine --no-fail-fast`: all pass.

title: Dimension text: DIMRND rounds only the measurement; no DIMPOST on angles (fixes #373)
author: vangel76
body:
Fixes #373.

## The problem

`linear_text` built the tolerance and alternate-unit number formats by copying the primary format, so both inherited DIMRND (and DIMZIN):

- DIMRND 0.5 with a ±0.1 tolerance showed `10.50±0.0000`.
- With DIMALT on, 10.3 in showed `[261.50]` mm, rounded to the primary 0.5 increment, instead of `[261.62]`.

AutoCAD rounds only the measurement by DIMRND. Alternate units have their own DIMALTRND, DIMALTU and DIMALTZ, and tolerances have DIMTZIN. CADCraft modelled none of these four variables.

DIMPOST was also added to angular dimensions (`90°mm`). Prefix and suffix are settings for linear dimensions only. Angular dimensions have their own format, precision and zero suppression.

## Changes

- `crates/doc/src/tables.rs`: new `DimStyle` fields and DIM* names, all defaulting to AutoCAD's initial values:
  - `tolZeroSuppression` (DIMTZIN, 0)
  - `altRound` (DIMALTRND, 0)
  - `altUnit` (DIMALTU, 2 = decimal)
  - `altZeroSuppression` (DIMALTZ, 0)

  SETVAR, `-DIMSTYLE`/`dimstyle`, DIMOVERRIDE and per-dimension overrides pick them up through `DIMVARS`.
- `crates/io/src/dxf_ext.rs`: the DXF Reference DIMSTYLE group codes 148 (DIMALTRND), 273 (DIMALTU), 284 (DIMTZIN) and 285 (DIMALTZ). They are used for DIMSTYLE records and DSTYLE override xdata.
- `crates/render/src/dim.rs`:
  - Tolerances are not rounded and use DIMTZIN.
  - Alternate units use DIMALTRND, DIMALTZ and DIMALTU. DIMALTU 4/5 are stacked architectural/fractional, 6/7 are the same unstacked, and 8 is decimal.
  - Limits are still rounded by DIMRND because they are measured distances.
  - The angular branch no longer applies DIMPOST. A text override (`<> TYP`) still wraps the angle.
- `crates/io/src/tests.rs`: `full_dim_style` sets the new fields to non-default values, so `dimstyle_roundtrips_every_field` and `autocad_header_dim_variables_are_not_overrides` cover them.

title: Angular dimensions keep each leg's extension line; centre mark only outside (fixes #374)
author: vangel76
body:
Fixes #374.

## The problem

- **Angular dimensions.** When the arc location lies outside the sweep from the first leg to the second, `dimension_geometry` builds the arc from leg 2 to leg 1. The extension lines, DIMSE1/DIMSE2 and DIMBLK1/DIMBLK2 still took the arc's start as leg 1. Each extension line was therefore sized from the other leg's endpoint. With DIMANGULAR at vertex 0,0, legs 10,0 and 0,2, and arc location -3,-3:
  - the only extension line was drawn along leg 1, which already crosses the arc;
  - leg 2, which stops short of the arc, had no extension line;
  - DIMSE1 had no visible effect, and DIMSE2 removed leg 1's line.
- **Centre marks.** Radius and diameter dimensions always drew the DIMCEN mark. The AutoCAD documentation of DIMCEN and of the Symbols and Arrows tab says that for DIMRADIUS and DIMDIAMETER the mark is drawn only when the dimension line is placed outside the circle or arc.

## Changes

`crates/render/src/dim.rs` only:

- **Angular.** The arc's two ends, each with its outward tangent, are paired with leg 1 and leg 2, swapped when the arc runs from leg 2 to leg 1. Each leg then gets its own extension-line length, DIMSE1/DIMSE2 flag and DIMBLK1/DIMBLK2 arrowhead.
- **Radius/diameter.**
  - The centre mark, or the centre lines when DIMCEN is negative, is drawn only when the dimension line is outside the circle. That is a radius dimension whose line leads from the arc out to text outside the circle.
  - A radius with its text moved inside has no mark.
  - A diameter dimension also has no mark, because its line is drawn through the centre. CADCraft doesn't model DIMTOFL; it always draws the diameter line inside, as AutoCAD does with DIMTOFL on.

Typed `LAYOUT` / `-LAYOUT` had no prompts. It ran the JSON default (a list) and ended at once, so the option and names typed after it ran as commands. `LAYOUT N Sheet9` gave `unknown command n` and `unknown command Sheet9`, and no layout was created.

title: fix(geom): use scale-aware circle-circle intersections
author: Ni-zav
body:
## Problem

Circle-circle intersections use fixed absolute tolerances that can
incorrectly classify small intersecting circles as tangent or
non-intersecting.

The calculation also squares radii directly, potentially causing
overflow for large but finite drawing coordinates.

## Root Cause

The intersection calculation relies on:
- An absolute EPS threshold for center separation.
- Fixed 1e-9 and 1e-12 tolerances.
- Unscaled squared-radius arithmetic.

These assumptions fail across different drawing scales.

## Changes

- Normalize radii and center distances before calculating intersections.
- Replace fixed distance thresholds with scale-aware comparisons.
- Prevent overflow from directly squaring large radii.
- Reject non-finite intersection results.
- Preserve valid secant and tangent behavior.

## Regression Tests

Added two tests covering:
- Small intersecting circles and separated circles.
- Large finite circles whose squared radii would overflow.

## Validation

- Changes committed and pushed.
- Remote commit verified.
- Branch compared against upstream main.
- Rust tests not executed (Cargo unavailable).
- CI pending.

No public issue.

title: fix(geom): preserve boundary vertices far from the origin
author: Ni-zav
body:
## Problem

Boundary detection can fail for drawings located far from the
world origin.

For example, a square near coordinates (1e12, 1e12) can lose
its distinct vertices during boundary graph construction.

This affects boundary detection used by HATCH, BOUNDARY, and REGION.

## Root Cause

The region graph quantizes absolute coordinates using:

    round(coordinate / tolerance) as i64

With large coordinates and small tolerances, the quantized values
exceed i64::MAX.

Integer conversion saturates, causing distinct vertices to share
identical graph keys.

## Changes

- Quantize graph vertices relative to the local bounding-box origin.
- Preserve tolerance-based vertex indexing.
- Avoid unnecessary modifications to graph traversal.
- Add regression coverage for georeferenced geometry.

## Regression Tests

Added a focused test covering:
- Enclosing-loop detection at large coordinates.
- Preservation of four distinct square vertices.
- Correct boundary area.
- Boundary detection without spurious islands.

## Validation

- Changes committed and pushed.
- Remote commit verified.
- Branch compared against upstream main.
- Rust tests not executed (Cargo unavailable).
- CI pending.

## Limitations

This addresses large absolute coordinate offsets.
Drawings whose coordinate span itself exceeds the i64 quantization
range require additional handling.

No public issue.

title: fix(geom): keep finite-scale tolerance and midpoint math stable
author: Ni-zav
body:
## Problem

Several geometry operations produce incorrect results for large but
finite coordinates:

- Vec2::near can report distant points as coincident.
- Vec3::len can overflow to infinity.
- Vec3::normalized can consequently return a zero vector.
- Bounds2::center can overflow when its endpoints have opposite signs.

These problems affect geometry calculations in drawings with
extreme coordinate ranges.

## Root Cause

Distance and length calculations square large floating-point values,
which can overflow even when the actual distance is representable.

Likewise, midpoint calculations can overflow while subtracting
opposite-sign endpoints.

## Changes

- Use Euclidean distance instead of squared-distance comparisons
  in Vec2::near.
- Reject negative and non-finite coincidence tolerances.
- Use hypot-based calculations for Vec3 lengths.
- Calculate bounding-box midpoints without overflowing
  opposite-sign coordinate differences.

## Regression Tests

Added tests for:

- Large finite points that must not compare equal.
- Valid large-distance tolerance comparisons.
- Negative and infinite tolerances.
- Large finite 3D vector normalization.
- Bounding-box midpoints near floating-point limits.

## Validation

- Changes committed and pushed.
- Remote branch verified against upstream main.
- No conflicting upstream changes detected.
- Rust tests not executed because Cargo is unavailable locally.

No public issue linked; independently identified geometry defects.

title: fix(select): include solid interiors in crossing-window selection
author: Ni-zav
body:
## Problem

Crossing selection fails to select SOLID and TRACE entities when
the selection window lies entirely inside their filled area.

The window does not intersect the entity's outline, so the
existing geometry-intersection test returns no match.

This differs from the expected behavior of crossing selection,
which should include filled geometry intersecting the window.

## Root Cause

Selection checks polygon boundaries but does not account for
a crossing window located wholly inside a filled polygon.

## Changes

- Detect crossing windows contained within SOLID and TRACE fills.
- Test containment against the actual polygon.
- Avoid false positives from triangular entities whose bounding
  rectangles include empty space.
- Preserve strict window-selection behavior.
- Keep existing text and block selection behavior unchanged.

## Regression Tests

Added tests covering:

- Crossing-window selection inside a SOLID.
- Crossing-window selection inside a TRACE.
- Selection through the complete selection API.
- Strict window selection remaining unchanged.
- Triangular bounding-box areas outside the actual fill.

## Validation

- Changes committed and pushed.
- Remote branch verified against upstream main.
- No conflicting upstream changes detected.
- Rust tests not executed because Cargo is unavailable locally.

No public issue linked; independently identified selection defect.

title: Point prompts: FROM, M2P/MTP, point filters, * prefix and <angle override (fixes #392)
author: vangel76
body:
Fixes #392.

## The problem

The precision-input modifiers AutoCAD users type at point prompts were missing (docs/gaps.md U3, an alpha blocker): `FROM`, `M2P`/`MTP`, the point filters `.x` … `.yz`, the `*` world-coordinate prefix and the angle override `<a`. Each was reported as unknown input or an invalid point.

While frames are pending, the session shows their prompt instead of the command's (through the prompt guard, so `current_prompt`, `prompt_text`, the rubber-band base and Dynamic Input all follow). It collects the points the frames need and finally hands one point to the command. Every command gets this for free, from the command line, scripts, the control channel and clicks.

  - `<a`, `<<a`, `<<<a` (read like the angle of `@d<a`): echoes "Angle Override: a" and keeps the command's prompt. A typed distance then runs along that angle from the base point, a picked point is projected onto it, and typed coordinates win. Keywords still reach the command.

body:
Part of #397.

## The problem

Every option TRIM and EXTEND list at their prompt (cuTting edges / Boundary edges, Fence, Crossing, mOde, Project, eRase) answered "<option>: not available yet", and the JSON forms only knew a single `handle` + `pick`. TRIM always behaved like a half Quick mode (all objects are cutting edges) with Standard-mode errors, and there was no Edge or Undo. This is part of the alpha blocker in docs/gaps.md F1 / Top-10 #5.

## Changes

The prompt machine moves from `modify.rs` into a new `cmd/trimextend.rs`. The trim/extend geometry stays in `modify.rs`, which now takes an `Edges { only, implied }` instead of `Option<&[Handle]>`.

- **mOde** (`Enter a trim mode option [Quick/Standard]`) sets TRIMEXTENDMODE (shared by TRIM and EXTEND, remembered in the drawing like OFFSETERASE).
  - **Quick** (default): all objects are edges. If no cutting edge crosses the picked object, TRIM erases it, as Quick mode does in AutoCAD.
  - **Standard**: the command opens with `Select cutting edges ... Select objects or <select all>:` (EXTEND: boundary edges), where Enter alone selects all. An object no edge crosses is left alone and the command reports why.
- **cuTting edges / Boundary edges**: pick the edges at any point, without switching the mode. Enter alone means all objects.
