title: Object snap tracking, Extension, Parallel and Apparent Intersection snaps (fixes #379)
author: vangel76
body:
Fixes #379.

## The problem

Object snap tracking didn't exist (gaps.md U1, an alpha blocker). The F11 button flipped a flag that nothing read. The Extension and Parallel snaps were declared but never produced a point. Apparent Intersection was the same as Intersection.

## Changes

**Engine** (`crates/engine/src/snap/tracking.rs`, new; the UI only draws):
- **Acquiring points.** Rest the cursor on a running snap point for 0.4 s (`DWELL`) and it is acquired. Rest on it again and it is released. At most seven points are kept (`MAX_ACQUIRED`), and the oldest goes first. With POLARMODE bit 8 you acquire by holding Shift instead. Leaving a point prompt clears them.
- **Paths.** Acquired points send alignment paths: horizontal and vertical, or every polar angle with POLARMODE bit 2. Polar tracking from the base point uses the same path machinery. Its angles are POLARANG increments plus POLARADDANG with POLARMODE bit 4, measured from ANGBASE.
- **What snaps, in order:** the crossing of two paths, then a path crossing an object, then the nearest point on one path. Paths must come within 6 px of the cursor (the old polar tolerance). Crossings must be within APERTURE. `Track` returns the point, the paths and the object name, for the tooltip.
- **EXT.** Rest on a line or arc end, then the line runs on as a ray and the arc runs round its circle (the arc itself is left out). This works with OTRACK off too.
- **PAR.** Rest on a line, then a path parallel to it runs through the base point, both ways.
- **APP** (2D):
  - In `osnap`, objects near the cursor snap where their extensions would meet. Lines, arcs, circles and xlines count; tessellated ellipse and spline chords don't.
  - An object you rest on sends its whole extension. Where that crosses another object or path, the cursor snaps to an "Apparent Intersection".
  - With only APP running, real crossings are reported as APP.
- **`Session::snap_cursor(raw, &CursorQuery)`** is the one cursor update: running snaps (and acquisit…

title: Object snap overrides at point prompts, Shift/Ctrl+right-click snap menu, Tab cycling (fixes #393)
author: vangel76
body:
Fixes #393.

**Stacked on #402 (point modifiers, #392): merge #402 first.** Until then, this PR's diff also shows #402's commit. The second commit is this change.

## The problem

Typed object snap overrides at a point prompt weren't supported (docs/gaps.md U4, an alpha blocker). `END`, `MID`, `CEN` … `NON` arrived as plain input. There was also no Shift/Ctrl+right-click object snap menu and no Tab cycling through candidate snaps.

title: Plot styles: colour-dependent tables (monochrome, grayscale) apply to PDF plots and layouts (part of #410)
author: vangel76
body:
Part of #410.

## The problem

A layout's plot style table was stored and round-tripped through DXF, but nothing read it: PDF plots, layout PNG/SVG exports and the layout on screen always used object colours and lineweights, so sheets couldn't come out monochrome or with pen-assigned lineweights (docs/gaps.md F14, an alpha blocker).

## Changes

- **Model (`crates/doc/src/plotstyle.rs`):** `PlotStyleTable` (colour-dependent or named) of `PlotStyle`s: colour override (object or RGB), grayscale, screening %, linetype override (object or name), lineweight override (object or mm×100), end, join and fill style. Built-in tables are our own definitions: `default.ctb` (object properties), `monochrome.ctb` (everything black) and `grayscale.ctb` (the grey of each colour's Rec. 709 luminance). `plot_style_table(d, name)` finds a page setup's table; empty or `None` means none.
- **Resolution (`crates/render/src/plotstyle.rs`):** while the display list is built, each object gets the style of its index colour. A true colour uses the style of its nearest index colour, and colour 7 prints black. The style sets the colour (override, grey, then screening toward the paper white), the lineweight (only when lineweights are plotted) and the linetype. Sub-colours (dimension line/text colours, MTEXT inline colours, gradient ends, hatch backgrounds) get the style of their own colour. `Options::plot_style_table` passes a table in. With no table passed, `build` of a layout uses the layout's table when its page setup has **Display plot styles** on.
- **PDF (`crates/io/src/pdf.rs`):** PLOT/EXPORTPDF (and anything plotting through them) use the page setup's table. A new `plotStyleTable` option overrides it, and `"None"` plots object colours.
- **Layouts:** a new `PageSetup::show_plot_styles` ("Display plot styles") is read and written as DXF plot layout flag 2 (DXF Reference, PLOTSETTINGS group 70). With it on, the screen canvas and the PNG/SVG exports of the layout show the table.

title: SPLINE: Knots, start/end Tangency, toLerance and Object (part of #408)
author: vangel76
body:
Part of #408.

## The problem

SPLINE's `Knots`, `Object`, `start Tangency`, `end Tangency` and `toLerance` options printed "<option>: not available yet" (docs/gaps.md F1). A fit-point spline was always a chord-length interpolation with free ends.

## Changes

- **geom** (`spline_fit.rs`, new): fit-point construction moved out of `spline.rs` and extended. Behaviour with default options is unchanged (a unit test checks the default output is identical).
  - **Knot parametrisation:** Chord, Square root (centripetal) or Uniform, for open and closed (periodic, #240) splines.
  - **End tangents:** each tangent adds a derivative constraint to the global interpolation. The ends are clamped, so `C'(0) = p/u_(p+1)·(P1−P0)`. Knots are averaged with the end parameter counted twice. The tangent is stored as a unit direction and scaled by the chord length.
  - **Fit tolerance:** with a tolerance above 0 the spline is a least-squares approximation with the ends kept exact (and the end tangents, by fixing the neighbouring control point). It uses the knot placement from The NURBS Book eq. 9.69. Bisection finds the fewest control points that keep every fit point within the tolerance. If nothing short of interpolation meets the tolerance, the spline interpolates.
  - These settings are stored in `Spline::fit_opts` (`FitOptions`, `#[serde(default)]`). `Spline::refit` rebuilds with them, so grip edits and SPLINEDIT Move/Refit/Open/Close keep the settings. `Spline::transform` turns the tangents on rotate/mirror/scale. Reverse swaps them and flips their direction; Purge clears them.
- **engine** (`cmd/spline_opts.rs`, new, plus small hunks in `draw.rs`' `SplineM`):
  - `Knots` asks "Enter knot parameterization [Chord/Square root/Uniform] <current>:" and remembers the answer in `SPLKNOTS`; the "Current settings" line shows it.
  - `start Tangency` and `end Tangency` take a point or a typed angle (through `s.angle_settings()`), and Enter leaves that end free. The end tangent finishes the sp…

title: MTEXT: Height, Justify, Line spacing, Rotation, Style, Width, Columns (part of #408)
author: vangel76
body:
Part of #408.

## The problem

MTEXT's "Specify opposite corner or [Height/Justify/Line spacing/Rotation/Style/Width/Columns]:" offered seven options. Each one printed "<option>: not available yet", so scripts that set them before the text didn't work (docs/gaps.md F1).

## Changes

- **engine** (`cmd/mtext_opts.rs`, new; `MTextM` in `draw.rs`): each option asks its question and goes back to the opposite-corner prompt. #239's behaviour is unchanged: one paragraph per line, and an empty line ends the text.
  - **Height:** "Specify height <current>:" takes a number or a point (its distance from the first corner) and updates TEXTSIZE, as TEXT does.
  - **Justify:** "Enter justification [TL/TC/TR/ML/MC/MR/BL/BC/BR] <current>:". The insertion point becomes the box's attachment point (MC is the middle of the box, and so on). Before this, the text always had a top-left attachment.
  - **Line spacing:** "Enter line spacing type [At least/Exactly]", then "Enter line spacing factor or distance <1x>:". `1.5x` is a factor; a plain number is the distance between lines (1x = 5/3 of the height). Factors outside 0.25x–4x are refused.
  - **Rotation:** "Specify rotation angle <0>:" takes a picked point (the angle from the first corner) or a typed angle read through `s.angle_settings()` (#328). The box rubber-band turns with it, and the opposite corner is measured in the turned frame.
  - **Style:** "Enter style name or [?] <current>:" takes an existing text style (case-insensitive). `?` lists the styles, and an unknown name is reported and asked again.
  - **Width:** "Specify width:" takes a number or a point and replaces the opposite corner. The first point becomes the insertion point and the text prompt follows. A width of 0 means no wrapping.

title: Autosave (SAVETIME, SAVEFILEPATH) and Drawing Recovery after a crash (fixes #406)
author: vangel76
body:
Fixes #406.

## The problem

CADCraft had no autosave and no crash recovery (docs/gaps.md F4, Top-10 #8): if the app or the machine went down, every unsaved change was lost, and there was no SAVETIME to set.

## Changes

- **`crates/engine/src/autosave.rs`** (new):
  - **SAVETIME** (minutes, default 10, 0 = off, at most 600) and **SAVEFILEPATH** (the autosave folder) are system variables (`setvar`, `getvar`, the command line). They are profile settings, process-wide and not saved in the drawing, like FONTALT.
  - `Autosaver::plan(session, now, minutes, dir)` decides without any I/O: a drawing with unsaved changes is written SAVETIME minutes after the first change not yet autosaved; a drawing changed since its last autosave is written again after the next interval; the file is deleted when the drawing has no unsaved changes left (saved, or undone back to the saved state) or is closed. `next_due` tells the host when to wake up.
  - Files are DXF (so CADCraft reads them) named `<drawing>_<instance>_<uid>.sv$`, written through the existing io write hook on a background thread (temporary file, then rename). A running app keeps `<instance>.lock` fresh (every minute while it has autosave files).
  - `recoverable(dir, own)` lists the files of apps that stopped: no lock file, or one not refreshed for five minutes. A copy of the app running at the same time keeps its files. `discard` deletes a file and the dead app's lock once it has no files left. `shutdown` (normal exit) finishes writes in progress and deletes this app's files and lock.
- **RECOVER** gains `copy: true` and `title`: the drawing opens as an unsaved copy without a file name (closing asks to save it), after AUDIT's fixes; the result includes the drawing's `uid`.
- **ui-egui** (`autosave.rs`, a few lines in `lib.rs`): the app runs the autosaver every frame (and asks egui to repaint when the next autosave is due); at start it lists files from a crashed app in a **Drawing Recovery** window: per drawing its name, t…

author: vangel76
body:

After #412, colour-dependent tables apply, but parts of #410 were still missing:

title: Groups: GROUP, UNGROUP and GROUPEDIT; erased members leave their groups (part of #417)
author: vangel76
body:
Part of #417.

## The problem
Groups had a drawing model (`Drawing::groups`) and a DXF round trip of the ACAD_GROUP dictionary, but no commands: there was no way to make, edit or remove a group, and erasing a member left a stale handle in its group.

## Changes
- New `crates/engine/src/cmd/groups.rs`:
  - **GROUP** (alias `G`, Tools ▸ Group): typed, `Select objects or [Name/Description]:`; `Name` asks `Enter a group name or [?]` (refuses taken or invalid names and asks again; `?` lists the groups), `Description` asks for free text; Enter makes the group. Without a name the group is unnamed (`*A1`, `*A2`…). With a pickfirst selection an unnamed group is made at once. JSON: `{name?, description?, handles?, selectable?}` → `{name, members}`.
  - **UNGROUP** (Tools ▸ Ungroup): `Select group or [Name]:` — a picked object's group (the most recent one holding it) or a group by name; a pick that is in no group is reported and asked again. With a pickfirst selection every group holding a selected object is ungrouped. JSON: `{name: "A" | "A,B" | [names]}` or `{handles?}`.
  - **GROUPEDIT**: pick or name a group, then `[Add objects/Remove objects/REName]`. Removing the last member deletes the group. JSON: `{name, add?, remove?, rename?}` (the new name is checked before anything changes).
  - **groups.list**: `{groups: [{name, description, selectable, unnamed, members}]}`.
- Post-command pass (`groups::after_command`, called next to the constraint/associativity passes in `Session::execute` and when an interactive command finishes): members that no longer exist leave their groups and groups left empty are deleted. It returns at once when the drawing has no groups or did not change; undo restores the groups with the objects.
- Ukrainian labels for the new menu items/commands (`uk.tsv`, required by the i18n coverage test).

Still to come in the follow-up PR #424 for #417: PICKSTYLE (picking a member selects its selectable group, Ctrl+Shift+A), `-GROUP` with its ?/Order/Add/Remove/…

title: Groups: PICKSTYLE group selection, Ctrl+Shift+A and -GROUP options (fixes #417)
author: vangel76
body:
Fixes #417.

## The problem
With GROUP, UNGROUP and GROUPEDIT in place (#422), picking a group member still selected one object: there was no PICKSTYLE group selection, no Ctrl+Shift+A toggle, and no `-GROUP` command-line editor.

## Changes
- **PICKSTYLE** (`crates/engine/src/cmd/groups/pick.rs`, `Settings::pickstyle`, SETVAR/GETVAR): with bit 1 on (the default 1), a click, a selection window, or ALL/Last/Previous at a "Select objects" prompt also selects the other visible members of the picked object's selectable groups, in the space being edited. Shift+click removes the whole group. Unselectable groups are picked one object at a time. GROUPEDIT and -GROUP still pick single members. Expansion builds a member→group map once per pick, so a large window stays linear. Bit 2 (associative hatch) is stored but not used yet.
- **`pickstyle` command**: typed, it asks "Enter new value for PICKSTYLE <n>:" (0–3; asks again for other values). JSON `{value?}`; with no value it toggles group selection, which is what **Ctrl+Shift+A** (Cmd+Shift+A on macOS) runs. It runs transparently, like the F-key toggles.
- **-GROUP** (`crates/engine/src/cmd/groups/dash.rs`, alias `-G`): `Enter a group option [?/Order/Add/Remove/Explode/REName/Selectable/Create] <Create>:`
  - Create: name (`*` or Enter makes an unnamed group), description, objects.
  - ?: names with wildcards, default `*`.
  - Order: positions from/to (0-based) and a count.
  - Add and Remove: pick objects.
  - Explode: ungroups.
  - REName: old name, then the new one.
  - Selectable: asks a Yes/No question to toggle it.
  
  JSON: `{option, name, ...}` for every option. The JSON form never prompts, and out-of-range positions are errors.

title: DXF/DWG at a chosen version 2000–2018 and binary DXF (part of #421)
author: vangel76
body:
Part of #421.

## The problem
Saving was locked to one version: DXF always R2000 (AC1015) ASCII, DWG always AutoCAD 2004 (AC1018, the bridge's minimum). There was no way to write DXF/DWG 2007–2018, and no binary DXF output (binary DXF could only be read).

## Changes
- **`cadcraft-dxf`**: `Version` (2000/2004/2007/2010/2013/2018 ↔ AC1015…AC1032; `parse` takes a year, `R2018` or an `$ACADVER` code; `for_acadver` maps a file's version to the nearest writable one). `write_ascii_as(tags, utf8)` writes R2007+ text as UTF-8 instead of `\U+` escapes. `write_binary(tags, utf8)` writes binary DXF from the public DXF Reference: sentinel, 2-byte little-endian group codes, values typed by group-code range (string, real, int16/32/64, bool byte, length-prefixed binary chunks split at 255 bytes); values are converted to their code's kind, so text held at a numeric code is stored as a number. `is_binary`. The binary parser now reports an empty body as "not a DXF file".
- **`cadcraft-io`**: `write_with(d, name, &SaveOptions { version, binary })`. DXF at any version keeps the existing R2000 structure (later versions only add optional groups) with that `$ACADVER`, UTF-8 from 2007. `save_version(d)`: without a version, a drawing saves in its own — the file's `$ACADVER` (nearest writable), 2018 for a new drawing. `write` (the save hooks) now uses it; DWG stays at least 2004 unless 2000 is asked for (R2000 DWG can't hold true colours, transparency or table styles). `write_dxf` / R2000 ASCII output is byte-identical to before (tested).
- **`cadcraft-dwg`**: `dxf_to_dwg_as(dxf, "AC1032")` writes the DWG at the chosen version; the writer now runs under `catch_unwind` like the reader. Two acadrust 0.6.3 gaps at 2010+ DWG are bridged here (found by the new tests): merged table cells are read only into `merged_ranges` (copied onto the cells, ranges clamped to the table), and table-style title/header suppression lives only in the style flags (synced both ways).
- `dwg_keeps_true_colours_and_tra…

title: TOLERANCE: GD&T feature control frames (fixes #420)
author: vangel76
body:
Fixes #420.

## The problem
CADCraft had no TOLERANCE command (`docs/gaps.md` F8). You could not draw geometric tolerancing (GD&T feature control frames), and "Dimension > Tolerance..." had no command behind it. TOLERANCE entities in opened DXF files were kept only as unknown data, so they were not drawn and were dropped on save.

## Changes
- **Model** (`crates/doc/src/gdt.rs`): a new `EntityKind::Tolerance` with the insertion point, X direction, dimension style and frame string, following the public DXF Reference (group 1: `%%v` separates compartments, `^J` separates lines, symbols are written as `{\Fgdt;…}` codes). It includes:
  - A parser that skips unknown formatting codes and caps string length, line count and compartment count.
  - A composer that builds the frame string from structured fields.
  - A layout that boxes each compartment and stacks lines, with the insertion point at the middle of the first line's left edge. Text height and padding come from DIMTXT/DIMGAP × DIMSCALE.
- **Symbols are our own geometry.** All 14 geometric characteristics, the diameter symbol, the circled M/L/S material conditions and the circled P (projected tolerance zone) are drawn from code: lines, circles, arcs and filled arrowheads. No GDT SHX font, Autodesk shapes or text are used.
- **Render** (`crates/render/src/tolerance.rs`): text is measured with the dimension style's font. Frames are drawn in DIMCLRD and symbols and text in DIMCLRT; ByBlock means the entity's own colour, as for dimensions. `tolerance_in` is public so explode can reuse it.
- **DXF**: TOLERANCE is read and written with codes 3, 10, 1, 11 and subclass `AcDbFcf`. A zero or non-finite direction falls back to +X.
- **Command `tolerance`** (alias `tol`, menu Dimension > Tolerance...):
  - JSON form: `symbol`, `tol1`/`tol2` (as `"%%c0.1(M)"` or `{value, diameter, material}`), up to 3 `datums`, `line2`, `height` + `projected`, `datumId`, `rotation`, `style`, or a raw `text`.

author: vangel76
body:
Fixes #421.

Builds on #426 (this branch contains its commit; merge #426 first, then this diff is only the second commit).

After #426 the io layer can write DXF/DWG at any version 2000–2018 and binary DXF, but nothing reached it: SAVEAS had no way to ask for a version or binary DXF, and the UI had no version setting.

title: PolarSnap, relative polar angles, Extension on ellipse and spline ends, tracking options in Drafting Settings (fixes #441)
author: vangel76
body:
Fixes #441.

Builds on #445 (TT/TK), whose commits this branch contains; the new work is the last commit. Review/merge #445 first.

## The problem
`docs/gaps.md` U1/U9: there was no PolarSnap, POLARMODE's relative-to-last-segment bit did nothing, Extension ignored elliptical arcs and splines, and Drafting Settings had none of the tracking options (additional angles, tracking on all polar angles, angle measurement).

## Changes
- **PolarSnap**: new system variables `SNAPTYPE` (0 grid, 1 PolarSnap) and `POLARDIST` (≥ 0). With snap mode on and SNAPTYPE 1, a point sliding along one straight tracking path (polar, alignment, extension, parallel) moves in steps of POLARDIST measured from the path's point (the snap X spacing when POLARDIST is 0); the grid snap is skipped, so off the paths the cursor is free. Direct distance entry still follows the path.
- **POLARMODE bit 1 (relative to last segment)**: the session keeps the last segment given at a point prompt (`Session::last_segment`, its base point and the point); while the base point is that segment's end, polar angles and additional angles are measured from its direction. Anywhere else they stay absolute. Alignment paths from acquired points stay absolute. (`TrackConfig::relative_to`; `TrackConfig::new` unchanged.)
- **Extension on elliptical arcs and open splines**: an elliptical arc end sends a new `PathShape::Ellipse` path around the rest of the ellipse (foot point refined with Newton steps; crossings come from the tessellation, like other ellipse geometry). An open spline end sends a ray along its end tangent (the control-polygon leg where the knots are clamped, else a finite difference). The canvas draws the ellipse path near the cursor.
- **Drafting Settings** (thin, same direct-settings pattern as the rest of the dialog): Snap type (Grid snap / PolarSnap) and Polar distance; Additional angles with the POLARADDANG list (typed text kept until it parses); Object Snap Tracking Settings (Track orthogonally only / Trac…

title: OVERKILL: tolerance, ignored properties, overlapping and end-to-end lines and arcs, polyline segments (fixes #439)
author: vangel76
body:
Fixes #439. (Last of three: #446 draw order, #449 MATCHPROP; the narrowed `docs/gaps.md` F19 row assumes those land too.)

## The problem
OVERKILL only deleted objects whose JSON was identical (comparing each object with every earlier one, O(n²)). It had no tolerance, couldn't ignore properties, left overlapping collinear lines and arcs alone, didn't touch polylines, and had no typed options (`docs/gaps.md` F19).

## Changes
- **Duplicates** within a tolerance (numbers rounded to it; default 1e-6), optionally ignoring colour, layer, linetype, ltscale, lineweight, thickness, transparency or plot style. Hashed, so linear.
- **Lines**: a line lying on another collinear one is deleted; partially overlapping ones are combined (`partialOverlap`, default on); lines meeting end to end are combined when asked (`endToEnd`, default off). Lines are bucketed by direction (sorted, with the wrap angle at an odd angle) and offset, then checked against the group's longest line, so the work stays O(n log n).
- **Arcs/circles** bucketed by circle: a circle covers the arcs on it, arcs on another arc are deleted, overlapping (or, when asked, touching) arcs are combined, across 0° too; arcs that close the circle become a circle.
- **Polylines** (`plines`, default on): zero-length segments dropped and consecutive collinear straight segments joined.
- **Associativity** (default on): objects an associative dimension follows are never deleted or changed, and win over their duplicates.
- Objects on locked layers are left alone. Result: `{deleted, duplicates, overlapping, segments, message}`.
- Typed `OVERKILL` / `-OVERKILL`: "Select objects", then "Enter an option to change [Done/Ignore/tOlerance/Plines/parTial overlap/Endtoend/Associativity] <Done>" with Yes/No sub-prompts, a tolerance prompt and an Ignore toggle prompt; echoes the duplicates and overlapping objects deleted. No dialog.

Part of #448.

ARRAY, ARRAYRECT and ARRAYPOLAR only made separate copies. ASsociative, Levels and polar ROWs printed "not available yet", so an array could not be kept as one object or edited later (`docs/gaps.md` F5).

## Changes
- **Model** (`crates/doc/src/array.rs`): `ArrayParams` (rectangular: columns, rows, spacing, axis angle, row elevation; polar: centre, items, fill angle, rotate items, rows, row spacing, row elevation; levels and level spacing for both; replaced items for ARRAYEDIT) kept on the array's anonymous block (`Block::array`). It lists where every item goes and builds the item references. Sizes are capped (`MAX_ARRAY_ITEMS`); parameters from files are checked with `is_valid` before use.
- **Structure**: an associative array is one block reference to an anonymous array block (`*U…`). That block holds one block reference per item, and each item points to an anonymous source block holding the source objects. Other programs see ordinary nested blocks. MOVE, COPY, ROTATE, SCALE and MIRROR transform the block reference. A copied array shares the blocks and is associative too.
- **ARRAYRECT / ARRAYPOLAR**:
  - ASsociative asks "Create associative array [Yes/No] <Yes>". The default follows ARRAYASSOCIATIVITY (on unless set to 0). The JSON form has `associative` (default true) and returns the array's `handle`.
  - Levels asks for the count, then the spacing (or Total). Polar ROWs asks for the count, the spacing (or Total) and the elevation. Rectangular row elevation is kept.

  - ASsociative = No still makes copies, and polar rows work there too. Levels need an associative array.
  - Items × rows × levels × objects count toward MAXARRAY. Objects nested deeper than `MAX_BLOCK_DEPTH` allows are refused.
- **EXPLODE** of an associative array gives the source objects of every item as plain objects. A replaced item stays a block refer…

title: Add shared workspace docking to CADCraft
author: skylartaylor
body:
Add configurable `craft-ui` layouts around CADCraft’s drawing, ToolSets, Layers and Properties panels. Keep application commands and drawing state authoritative while panels move, group, close and reopen.

- Explicit Properties/Layer commands reveal an existing inactive tab or restore its saved location; grouped hidden panels retain their order.
- Keep the real workspace available during body callbacks, including typed commands, and discard stale docking actions after a callback replaces the layout.
- Clamp command/history overlays within narrow drawing areas and preserve pointer ownership for visible controls.
- Retain current native startup, preferences, theme and document-close behavior.

Depends on [craft-libs #6](https://github.com/storytold/craft-libs/pull/6); the manifest and lockfile pin the same immutable shared revision.

Validation on the refreshed merged source: all six `cargo xtask ci` gates pass, with 917 tests passed, zero failed/ignored and 11 WASM crate checks. The existing docking and control suites pass 15 tests and generate 28 fresh populated captures; sampled Dark floating/redocked and keyboard-focus images were inspected. Keyboard traversal and translation coverage pass. Light/System preferences and tokens have automated coverage; Light visual and attended native GUI acceptance remain unverified.

The upstream refresh preserves Ukrainian UI translations, dynamic input and Tab capture, drawing-unit and plot-style preferences, system cursors, and document-close handling alongside the shared workspace.


An unsupported or malformed saved docking field now falls back independently, preserving toolbar/palette preferences, toolset selection, collapsed groups and history size. Runtime state commands remain strict.

author: vangel76

Fixes #451.

Stacked on #454 (associative hatches + DXF 97/330): this branch contains its two commits; the new work is the last commit. Merge #454 first, or this one alone.

## The problem
Besides associativity (#454), hatching lacked the editing options listed in `docs/gaps.md` F13: the pattern origin couldn't be set, small gaps in a boundary made pick-point hatching fail (no HPGAPTOL), several picked areas always became one hatch, the island style couldn't be chosen, and HATCHEDIT only forwarded pattern/scale/angle to `properties.set`.

title: Viewports: polygonal, object and clipped viewports, VPCLIP, MVIEW ON/OFF/Lock/Restore (part of #453)
author: vangel76
body:
Part of #453.

## The problem
Layout viewports could only be rectangles (`docs/gaps.md` F15): no polygonal or object viewports, no VPCLIP, and MVIEW lacked ON/OFF, Lock, Restore and the 2/3 arrangement prompts. DXF files with clipped or turned-off viewports lost the clip boundary and the on/off state.

## Changes
- **Model** (`cadcraft-doc`): `Viewport` gains `clip: Option<Handle>` (the paper-space entity whose outline clips the viewport, DXF 340) and `on: bool` (serde defaults keep old JSON readable); `Viewport::default()`.
- **Render**: `clip::PolyClip` clips polylines, fills (against a slab triangulation of the outline), points and infinite lines to an arbitrary even-odd polygon, with edges bucketed in horizontal bands. `clip::boundary_polygon` tessellates a closed polyline (with arcs), circle, full ellipse or closed spline, thinned to at most 4096 vertices. A clipped viewport draws model space through that outline and no rectangle border (the boundary entity draws itself); the rectangle remains the fast path. A viewport turned off draws only its border. PNG, SVG and PDF output all come from the same display list.
- **MVIEW**: Polygonal (start point, then points with Arc/Line/Close/Undo; tangent arcs as polyline bulges), Object (closed polyline, circle, ellipse, spline), ON/OFF and Lock (pick viewports or their clip boundaries), Restore ("not available yet": no named viewport configurations), and the arrangement prompt after 2/3. JSON form: `{option: polygonal|object|on|off|lock|restore, points?, bulges?, object?, handles?, locked?}`. New menu item View > Viewports > Polygonal Viewport (`mview.polygonal`).

title: ARRAYEDIT and ARRAYCLOSE for associative arrays (fixes #448)
author: vangel76
body:
Fixes #448. Builds on #455 (associative array model, ASsociative/Levels/polar ROWs, DXF round trip), which this branch contains. Merge #455 first; this diff then shrinks to the second commit.

## The problem
After #455, arrays are associative objects, but nothing could edit them after creation: there was no ARRAYEDIT and no way to edit the source objects or replace items.

## Changes
- **ARRAYEDIT** (`crates/engine/src/cmd/array/edit.rs`, menu Modify ▸ Object ▸ Array): select an array, then change it option by option until eXit. One undo step reverts the whole edit.
  - Rectangular: Source / REPlace / Base point / Rows / Columns / Levels / RESet / eXit.
  - Polar: also Items / Angle between / Fill angle / ROTate items.
  - Rows, Columns and Levels take a count, then a spacing or Total; Rows also takes a row elevation.
  - Base point moves the array's reference point without moving the items.
  - REPlace: select objects and a base point (Enter = their centre), then pick items to replace. "Source objects" replaces the source of every item. The selected objects stay in the drawing.
  - RESet restores replaced items.
  - Source: pick an item. Its source objects are placed in the drawing for editing, and objects drawn meanwhile join them.
- **ARRAYCLOSE**: "Save changes to array? [Yes/No]". Saving makes the objects the new source; discarding removes them. Only one Source edit can be open at a time, and other ARRAYEDIT changes wait until it is closed.
- **JSON** `arrayedit {handle, cols, rows, colSpacing, rowSpacing, axisAngle, rowElevation, levels, levelSpacing, items, angle, angleBetween, rotate, center, base, reset, replace: {handles, base, items: [[i,j,level]…] | "source"}, source: {item}}` and `arrayclose {save}`. Programmatic calls never prompt.
- Every change builds a new array block for the edited block reference, so copies that shared the old block keep it. Anonymous blocks nothing uses any more are removed.

title: UNDO Mark/Back, BEgin/End, Auto and Control; MREDO; UNDOCTL (part of #461)
author: vangel76
body:
Part of #461.

## The problem
UNDO listed Auto, Control, BEgin, End, Mark and Back at the command line, but only the count worked (`docs/gaps.md` U10). MREDO was just an alias of REDO, and there was no UNDOCTL.

## Changes
- **Mark / Back**: Back undoes to the last mark (the mark goes with it, so repeated Backs step back mark by mark). With no mark it asks before undoing everything; the JSON form takes `confirm` (default yes, as the prompt's default). Marks that were undone away and then overwritten by a new step are dropped.
- **BEgin / End**: the steps in between become one undo step labelled "Group". BEgin while a group is open ends that group and begins a new one (as AutoCAD documents it); End with no group does nothing; U/UNDO inside an open group ends it and undoes the whole group; saving ends an open group.
- **Control All / None / One**: None discards undo information and records nothing (U and UNDO report that undo is off, and the UNDO prompt asks for the control option straight away); One keeps only the last step (the prompt offers a count or Control). Combine and Layer (Yes/No) and **Auto** (ON/OFF) are stored and reported in UNDOCTL; they change nothing else because every command already records a single step and zooms/pans record none.
- **UNDOCTL** (1 on, 2 one step, 4 Auto, 8 group open, 16 combine zoom/pan, 32 combine layer; 53 by default) and **UNDOMARKS** are read-only system variables.
- **MREDO** is its own command: "Enter number of actions or [All/Last]", JSON `{count}` or `{all: true}`. REDO keeps `{count}`.
- JSON: `undo {count?} | {mode: mark|begin|end} | {mode: back, confirm?} | {mode: auto, on} | {mode: control, control: all|none|one|combine|layer, on?}`. No dialogs.

Design: marks and the open group are depths into the drawing's undo stack, held in a new `DocState::undo_ctl` (`crates/engine/src/undoctl.rs`). `Session::execute` and interactive commands record their step through `DocState::push_undo`, which applies Control and the existing 2…

title: DXF: native MULTILEADER read and write instead of LEADER + MTEXT (fixes #459)
author: vangel76
body:
Fixes #459.

## The problem
Multileaders weren't native objects in DXF (`docs/gaps.md` FF2). MLEADER was saved as LEADER + MTEXT/INSERT, so a save and reopen turned every multileader into loose pieces. MULTILEADER entities in an opened DXF/DWG were kept as unknown data: you couldn't see or edit them as multileaders.

## Changes
- **New `crates/io/src/dxf_mleader.rs`** holds the mapping between the MLeader model and the MULTILEADER entity from Autodesk's public DXF Reference.
  - **Reader.** It walks the nested `300 CONTEXT_DATA{` / `302 LEADER{` / `304 LEADER_LINE{` sections and reads:
    - leader lines from the arrowhead, the landing point and the dogleg length
    - the leader type (straight, spline or none)
    - MText content: contents, location, height, width, rotation (13 direction or 42), line spacing and style, and the attachment, taken from the text side (171) and the landing attachment (174/175, or 173/95 at entity level)
    - block content: block, location, scale and rotation
    - the arrowhead size
  - **Names behind handles.** Text style and block names come from STYLE / BLOCK_RECORD handles. The MLEADERSTYLE name and the block attribute values (330/177/44/302, placed like their ATTDEF) are filled in once the objects are read. That also works for multileaders inside block definitions.
  - **Writer.** It emits the same structure plus the entity-level groups: style handle, override flags, leader type, landing/dogleg switches, content type, text style, block handle and attribute values. The block's 4×4 transform goes in the 47 groups.

title: SETVAR/GETVAR: header variables the commands keep, TRANSPARENCYDISPLAY, dimension variables in SETVAR ? (fixes #461)
author: vangel76
body:
Fixes #461 (together with #464, which adds the UNDO options, MREDO and UNDOCTL).

## The problem
Commands keep about thirty system variables in the drawing header and read them with a default (CIRCLERAD, OFFSETDIST, POLYSIDES, HPNAME/HPSCALE/HPANG, CHAMFERC/D, CHAMMODE, TRIMMODE, EDGEMODE, PROJMODE, DONUTID/OD, SPLINESEGS, SPLKNOTS, WIPEOUTFRAME, LWDEFAULT…). GETVAR called them unknown until a command had set them, SETVAR wrote any value unchecked (an angle like HPANG was even stored as typed degrees where the commands expect radians), and `SETVAR ?` didn't list them or the dimension variables.

## Changes
- `crates/engine/src/sysvars/table.rs`: one table row per variable with its kind (choice, integer range, real with minimum, angle, hatch pattern, block name, read-only text) and the default the commands use (imperial or metric where they differ, by MEASUREMENT). GETVAR reports the default, SETVAR checks the value (`invalid value for POLYSIDES (3 to 1024)`), angles are shown and typed in degrees (text follows AUNITS) and kept in radians, HPNAME must be a library pattern, INSNAME `.` clears it, CPLOTSTYLE is read-only (PLOTSTYLE sets it).
- TRANSPARENCYDISPLAY joins the session variables (same table, Settings-backed).
- `SETVAR ?` also lists the dimension variables of the current style (GETVAR already answered them).
- `sysvars.rs` only gains hooks: `mod table;`, a lookup at the start of the header fallback in `get`/`set`, `is_read_only` and `list`.

**Count (new drawing):** `SETVAR ?` lists **140** variables (was 64); GETVAR answers **148** names (was 118, counting the dimension variables and read-only state variables).

title: EXTEND, JOIN and LENGTHEN on elliptical arcs and splines (part of #466)
author: vangel76
body:
Part of #466.

## The problem
The modify commands stopped at elliptical arcs and splines (`docs/gaps.md` F6): EXTEND refused splines, LENGTHEN and JOIN accepted only lines, arcs and polylines, and trimming a closed spline left two pieces instead of one. FILLET Trim/Multiple and CHAMFER Angle/mEthod already landed with #248, so that part of the F6 row was stale.

## Changes
- **geom (`crates/geom/src/nurbs.rs`, new):** NURBS operations the editing commands need, all textbook algorithms written from the mathematics: first derivative and unit tangent, Boehm knot insertion, split / sub-curve, clamping of periodic splines, Bézier decomposition, degree elevation, end-to-end join (degrees matched, weights rescaled at the junction), exact rational splines for lines and circular/elliptical arcs, straight extension along an end tangent, Gauss–Legendre arc length and its inverse; ellipse arc length and parameter-at-length. Loops are capped; degenerate input gives `None`, never a panic or NaN. The engine's `split_spline`/`sub_spline`/`reverse_spline` now delegate to it.
- **EXTEND:** an open spline runs on along its end tangent to the nearest boundary edge; closed splines are refused.
- **LENGTHEN:** elliptical arcs along the ellipse (DElta, Percent, Total, DYnamic/To; the Angle options stay arc-only), open splines (shorter cuts along the curve, longer runs on along the end tangent). Measuring reports their exact length.
- **JOIN:** elliptical arcs on one ellipse (also with the major axis reversed, or a circle-like ellipse rotated) merge into a larger arc, or the full ellipse; gaps close and the widest gap stays open. Lines, arcs, polylines, elliptical arcs and splines that connect end to end become one exact spline; the first object keeps its handle. The command-line message names the result ("2 objects joined into 1 spline").
- **TRIM:** a closed spline leaves one open spline (the remainder joined across the seam).

title: FILLET with elliptical arcs and splines (part of #466)
author: vangel76
body:
Part of #466. Stacked on #469 (its two commits show here until it merges; the new work is the last two commits).

## The problem
FILLET refused elliptical arcs and splines ("Fillet works on lines, arcs and circles"), although AutoCAD fillets ellipses, elliptical arcs and splines with each other and with lines, arcs and circles. CHAMFER's refusal ("Chamfer currently works on lines.") read like an unfinished feature, while AutoCAD does not chamfer curves either.

## Changes
- **geom (`crates/geom/src/fillet.rs`, new):** `tangent_circles(c1, c2, r, picks)` returns every circle of radius `r` tangent to two curves (infinite lines, whole circles and ellipses, splines within their domain), or the curves' crossings for `r = 0`. The centre lies on an offset of each curve; sampled offsets are intersected (chunked box culling) for seeds, and Newton's method on the exact offset curves refines each one (finite-difference Jacobian, capped iterations, splines clamped to their domain). Degenerate curves, NaN/negative radii and hostile magnitudes yield no solutions.
- **FILLET:** an elliptical arc or spline with a line, arc, circle, elliptical arc or spline. The solution touching nearest the picks is used (as for arcs today). Elliptical arcs keep the picked side of the touch point, or extend round the ellipse from the nearer end; splines are split at the touch point (knot insertion from #469); whole ellipses, circles and closed splines stay whole. Radius 0 meets the objects at their crossing; TRIMMODE 0 (No trim) leaves them as they were. The new code is in `modify2/curve_edits.rs`; `fillet_curves` gains a three-line dispatch.
- **CHAMFER:** one clear message that it takes lines (and polylines with the Polyline option) and cannot chamfer arcs, circles, ellipses or splines.
- Docs: `geometry-parity.md` fillet/chamfer rows (section 55% → 65%), `gaps.md` F6 narrowed to polyline segments with other objects.

FILLET and CHAMFER only took a polyline as a whole (the Polyline option). Picking two segments of one polyline, or a polyline's end segment and a line, failed with "Fillet works on lines, arcs and circles" / "Chamfer currently works on lines.", which AutoCAD users do all the time to round or cut a single corner, or to close a polyline onto a line.

title: Named views (VIEW), Zoom Realtime and Dynamic, ZOOMFACTOR (part of #463)
author: vangel76
body:
Part of #463.

## The problem
`docs/gaps.md` U11: there were no named views (VIEW), ZOOM's Realtime default and Dynamic option didn't exist (Dynamic fell back to a window), and the wheel zoom step couldn't be changed (ZOOMFACTOR). The DXF VIEW table dropped a view's paper space flag, its layout and its twist.

## Changes
- **VIEW / -VIEW** (`crates/engine/src/cmd/view/named_views.rs`, View > Named Views..., alias `V`): Save, Window, Restore, Delete (wildcards), `?` and sEttings > Layer snapshot; Orthographic says not available yet (CADCraft views are 2D). JSON: `view {option: save|window|restore|delete|list|settings, name, names, p1, p2, layerSnapshot}`.
  - A view remembers its space: model space (also a model view saved inside an MSPACE viewport) or the layout it was saved in. Restoring switches to that space, fits the saved area and goes into the view history (Zoom Previous returns), like ZOOM; it isn't an undo step.
  - Layer snapshot (on by default, like the View Manager): a layer state `*VIEW <name>` saved with the view, restored with it, deleted with it.
- **ZOOM Realtime**: Enter at ZOOM's first prompt (or View > Zoom > Realtime, `zoom.realtime`) starts it. The canvas turns vertical primary-button drags into `Session::realtime_zoom` (up zooms in, half the height = 2x, about the view centre); Esc or Enter ends. One view-history entry for the whole drag session. JSON: `{factor}`.
- **ZOOM Dynamic** (keyword, View > Zoom > Dynamic, `zoom.dynamic`): zooms out to show the extents and the current view; the view box follows the cursor, a point places it, the next sizes it (left edge stays), Enter shows the box. Zoom Previous skips the overview. JSON: `{center, height}`.
- **ZOOMFACTOR** (3–100, default 60, a session setting like AutoCAD's profile variable): scales the mouse wheel step via `Session::wheel_zoom_factor`; 60 keeps today's step.
- **DXF VIEW table**: 70 bit 1 (paper space view), 50 (twist, degrees), the layout name as CADCraft xdata next to the existing…

title: Annotative scaling: DXF and status bar annotation scale list (fixes #468)
author: vangel76
body:
Fixes #468. Builds on #486 (its commits are included here; review/merge #486 first, then this PR shows only the last commit).

## The problem
After #486 annotative scaling works in a session, but a saved DXF lost the scale list, the current annotation scale, ANNOALLVISIBLE and every object's supported scales, and the status bar had no annotation scale list.

## Changes
- **Scale list in DXF** (public DXF Reference): the `ACAD_SCALELIST` dictionary of `SCALE` objects (300 name, 140 paper units, 141 drawing units, 290 unit-scale flag) is written and read, with a `SCALE` class entry. A metric file without a scale list gets the metric defaults.
- **Multileader styles:** the annotative flag (MLEADERSTYLE group 296) is written and read.

It is only written when something differs from a new drawing; payloads are capped and invalid scales skipped.

title: DXF: reopen-and-save keeps one *D block per dimension and stable handles (fixes #495)
author: vangel76
body:
Fixes #495. Also covers gap FF7 in `docs/gaps.md` ("`*D` dimension blocks duplicate on re-save; handles regenerate every save"). The row is narrowed to what is still open.

## The problem

- **`*D` blocks pile up.** On read, a dimension's anonymous geometry block (`*D1`, group 2) is kept as an ordinary block. On save, the writer gave every dimension a new `*D` name that no existing block used, and it also wrote the old block again. Each open → save cycle therefore added one unreferenced `*D` block per dimension (12.5 → 14.0 → 15.5 → 17.0 KB in the issue).
- **Handles drift on every save.** Table records, block records and objects are numbered from `handseed + 0x1000`. The reader then set `handseed` from the file's `$HANDSEED`, and that value already counts those structural handles. So every re-save moved all of those handles up by roughly 0x1000. Entity handles were already kept.

## Changes

- `dxf_write`, new `dim_block_plan`, run before block records get their handles:
  - A dimension in model or paper space whose `dm.block` names a `*D` block regenerates its geometry **under that name**. The new geometry reuses the old block's entity handles, in order, through `reuse_handles`.
  - `*D` blocks that nothing else references are no longer written. References that count: INSERTs anywhere, multileader block content, and dimensions inside block definitions.
  - User blocks, including unused ones, are untouched. A `*D` block that an INSERT uses is kept.
  - Freshly drawn dimensions get new `*D` names as before.
- **Handle seed:** the writer saves the drawing's own next handle in a `CADCRAFT_HANDSEED` XRECORD in the named object dictionary, next to the existing `CADCRAFT_*` XRECORDs. When a file has it, the reader uses it in place of `$HANDSEED`. As before, the seed is only ever bumped up, and entity handles still push it higher, so files edited elsewhere stay safe. With no XRECORD (other programs' files) nothing changes.
- **Hostile seeds:** structural handle allocation…

title: Web: opt-in embedding bridge for host pages (?host=parent)
author: CyberFox-81
body:
A page that frames CADCraft on the same origin can now open drawings in it and store what it saves, through postMessage, instead of saves becoming browser downloads. Built for a Nextcloud integration, but nothing in it is host-specific.

Only the web shell changes:
- cadcraft:open from the parent goes through the upload inbox, like a picked or dropped file (with the same size check)
- in host mode the engine's delivery hook (set_deliver) posts files to the parent (cadcraft:save) instead of downloading them; the engine counts a drawing saved as it does after a download
- cadcraft:dirty reports unsaved changes; cadcraft:ready and cadcraft:failed report start-up
- in host mode the app starts on the Start tab instead of Drawing1

Enabled only by ?host=parent inside a frame; only the parent window on the page's own origin is heard or answered. Without it nothing changes.

title: DXF: read pre-2007 files in their $DWGCODEPAGE (CJK, Cyrillic, Central European…) (fixes #505)
author: vangel76
body:
Fixes #505.

## The problem
Text in a pre-2007 DXF is in the code page its header names (`$DWGCODEPAGE`). The reader decoded every file as UTF-8, falling back to Latin-1 byte by byte, so Cyrillic, Central European, Greek, Turkish, Thai, Japanese, Chinese and Korean drawings opened with garbled text, layer names and block names (`docs/gaps.md` FF4, top-10 row 4).

## Changes
- **`crates/dxf` (L0), new `codepage` module.** A pure function, `cadcraft_dxf::decode_code_page(bytes, name)`, plus the reader wiring:
  - **ASCII DXF:** a file that is valid UTF-8 is read as UTF-8, as before. That covers R2007+ files, pure-ASCII files, and older files from writers that ignored the code page, including the DWG bridge (acadrust writes UTF-8 under the DWG's code page name). Any other file is decoded from the `$DWGCODEPAGE` value. The value comes from a scan of the raw bytes that stops at the end of the HEADER. Decoding happens **before** the escapes are processed, so a Shift-JIS trail byte 0x5C (表 is `95 5C`) is never read as the start of a `\U+` escape.
  - **Binary DXF:** `$ACADVER` and `$DWGCODEPAGE` are picked up as the header tags go by (both come first and are ASCII). R2007+ strings are UTF-8. Strings in older files use the code page, strictly, so a short Cyrillic name that happens to be valid UTF-8 still decodes right. With no code page the reader falls back to UTF-8 if valid, else 1252.
  - **Code pages:** ANSI_874/932/936/949/950/1250–1258, ISO 8859-1…9, Macintosh and DOS866 go through `encoding_rs`, along with the aliases GB2312, BIG5, KSC5601/KOREAN, DOS932 and UTF8. DOS437, DOS850 and DOS852 use 128-entry tables for the upper half (the IBM PC code page definitions).
  - **Unknown code page** (Johab ANSI_1361, the other DOS pages, anything unrecognised): the text is read as ANSI_1252 and the reader logs a `log::warn!`. Unchanged ANSI_1252 files now decode as real Windows-1252 rather than Latin-1, so 0x80–0x9F become € – “ ” etc. instead of C1 control characters.
  - **`…

title: Dimension styles: fit, text movement, suppressed halves, fixed extension lines, linetypes and lineweights and more DIM variables (part of #507)
author: vangel76
body:
Part of #507.

## The problem

Dimension styles modelled about half of AutoCAD's DIMSTYLE variables. The ones detailers use to control fit (DIMATFIT, DIMTIX, DIMSOXD, DIMTOFL), text movement (DIMTMOVE), suppressed dimension-line halves (DIMSD1/2), fixed-length extension lines (DIMFXL/DIMFXLON), tolerance justification (DIMTOLJ), angular zero suppression (DIMAZIN), the arc length symbol (DIMARCSYM), leader arrows (DIMLDRBLK), and dimension and extension line linetypes and lineweights (DIMLTYPE, DIMLTEX1/2, DIMLWD/DIMLWE) were missing. DIMTVP and DIMJOGANG were missing too. SETVAR, DIMOVERRIDE and DXF didn't have them, and the layout ignored them.

## Changes

- **Model** (`crates/doc/src/tables.rs`): 21 new `DimStyle` fields, each with its DIM* name in `DIMVARS`. That puts them in SETVAR/GETVAR, the header overrides that new dimensions take, DIMOVERRIDE and `-DIMSTYLE` status. Values are range-checked (DIMATFIT 0–3, DIMTMOVE/DIMTOLJ/DIMARCSYM 0–2, lineweights -3…211 or ByLayer/ByBlock/Default, DIMJOGANG 5–90°, DIMFXL ≥ 0). ISO-25 gets DIMTOFL on and DIMTOLJ 0, as in the public ISO defaults.
- **Layout** (`crates/render/src/dim.rs`):
  - Linear and aligned fit: when text and arrows don't both fit, DIMATFIT decides what moves out: both, arrows first, text first, or best fit. Best fit keeps the old placement except that text that fits alone now stays inside. DIMTIX keeps the text inside. DIMSOXD drops outside arrows. With arrows outside, the line between the extension lines is drawn only with DIMTOFL; outside it, short stubs.
  - Radius and diameter dimensions with outside text use DIMTOFL too. With it, the line runs through the circle or in from the centre. Without it, there is just the leader and the DIMCEN mark, as AutoCAD's Standard style draws a diameter.
  - DIMSD1/DIMSD2 leave out half the dimension line and its arrow. DIMFXLON/DIMFXL give fixed-length extension lines. DIMTVP lifts centred text by text heights, and the line stays unbroken from 0.7 up.
  - DIMTMOV…

title: MLINE: multiline entity, MLSTYLE and MLEDIT (part of #510)
author: vangel76
body:
Part of #510.

## The problem

MLINE drew two loose polylines. There was no multiline object and no multiline style, so a wall could not be edited as one object, styles (element offsets, colours, linetypes, caps, fill) did not exist, and other programs saw two polylines instead of an MLINE (`docs/gaps.md` F21).

## Changes

- **Model** (`crates/doc/src/entity/mline.rs`): `EntityKind::MLine` holds vertices, justification (Top/Zero/Bottom), scale, the closed and suppressed-cap flags, and per-segment breaks (`MLineCut`). It carries a copy of its `MLineStyle`: elements (offset, colour, linetype), start/end caps (line, outer arc, inner arcs, angle), joints and fill. Because of that copy, snapping, selection, extents and trimming work from the entity alone. `MLine::geometry()` gives the element pieces, the caps and joints, and the fill loops. Miters keep sharp corners finite.
- **Styles**: `Drawing::mline_styles` always has STANDARD (our own generic two-line style, offsets ±0.5). `CMLSTYLE`, `CMLJUST` and `CMLSCALE` are kept and written to the header.

  - `MLSTYLE` (Format ▸ Multiline Style..., JSON form) creates styles, changes them, copies them from another style, renames them and deletes them. Like the reference, it refuses to change, rename or delete a style that is in use, and refuses to delete STANDARD or the current style.
  - `MLEDIT` (Modify ▸ Object ▸ Multiline..., alias `-mledit`) has a JSON form and command-line prompts. It does closed, open and merged crosses, closed and open tees, the corner joint (two multilines that continue into each other become one), add and delete vertex, cut single, cut all and weld all.

title: Dimension text: degrees/minutes/seconds angles round at the displayed precision
author: webdevtodayjason
body:
Angular dimensions in degrees/minutes/seconds (DIMAUNIT 1) rounded to whole seconds and then dropped the seconds or minutes that were not shown. At whole-degree or minute precision the text could be one unit low: 45.75° showed as 45°, 29°59'40" as 29°59' at minute precision, and 359.6° as 359°. The decimal-degree format already rounds (45.75° shows 46°), so the two formats disagreed.

The value is now rounded at the unit being shown (degree, minute or second) before it is split, so carries run into minutes and degrees. The DIMADEC mapping is unchanged: 0 shows degrees, 1 and 2 minutes, 3 and up seconds.

References: [DIMAUNIT](https://help.autodesk.com/cloudhelp/2026/ENU/AutoCAD-Core/files/GUID-30F44A49-4250-42D1-AEF2-5E2914ADB02B.htm) and [DIMADEC](https://help.autodesk.com/cloudhelp/2026/ENU/AutoCAD-Core/files/GUID-E5C2F9AA-5017-4111-A485-E0456225D691.htm).

## How it was tested

- New tests in `crates/render/src/units.rs` fail on main (45.75° at precision 0 gives 45° instead of 46°; 29°59'40" gives 29° instead of 30°) and pass with the change. They cover carries at degree and minute precision and the existing non-negative sweep behaviour.
- `cargo test -p cadcraft-render`: all tests pass.
- `cargo xtask ci`: all 6 steps passed (fmt, clippy, test, assets, layers, wasm).

title: HELIX: helix entity drawn as a spline (part of #510)
author: vangel76
body:
Part of #510.

## The problem

HELIX made a 3D polyline, so the helix could not be edited as a helix, and other programs saw a polyline instead of a HELIX (`docs/gaps.md` F21).

## Changes

- **Model** (`crates/doc/src/entity/helix.rs`): `EntityKind::Helix` stores the base centre, base and top radius, height, turns, start angle, twist (CCW = right-handed) and constraint (turn height / turns / height). `Helix::spline3()` is the cubic spline through points on the helix, 8 per turn. Its knots are evenly spaced, so the height of each control point (taken at its Greville abscissa) makes the 3D spline pass exactly through those points. `Helix::spline()` is the same spline seen from above.
- **HELIX command** (JSON form and the existing prompts: Diameter, Turns, turn Height, tWist) now makes the object. Sizes are checked; turns stay within 500.
- **Edits**:
  - Drawing, snaps, selection and extents work through the spline.
  - MOVE, ROTATE and SCALE work as expected (SCALE scales radii and height). MIRROR also reverses the twist.
  - Grips: the centre moves the helix, the base grip sets the base radius and start angle, and the top grip sets the top radius.
  - EXPLODE and FLATTEN turn the helix into its spline.
- **DXF** (public DXF Reference):
  - HELIX is written as the spline (AcDbSpline, 3D control points and knots), then the helix data (AcDbHelix: axis base point 10, start point 11, axis 12, radius 40, turns 41, turn height 42, handedness 290, constraint 280).
  - A `HELIX`/`AcDbHelix` CLASS record is written when the drawing has helices.
  - On read, the spline and helix groups (which reuse codes 40–42) are told apart by their subclass markers. The top radius is how far the end of the spline lies from the axis.
  - Hostile values are made finite and the turns are clamped.

## Limits

- The helix's axis is the Z axis, as everywhere else in CADCraft. A foreign helix with a tilted axis is read upright.
- The AcDbHelix release numbers (90/91) are written as 29/63, the va…

title: Dimension edits: DIMEDIT Oblique/New/Rotate/Home, DIMJOGGED, DIMJOGLINE, DIMBREAK, DIMINSPECT (part of #507)
author: vangel76
body:

There were no jogged radius dimensions (DIMJOGGED), jogged linear dimensions (DIMJOGLINE), dimension breaks (DIMBREAK), oblique extension lines (DIMEDIT Oblique) or inspection dimensions (DIMINSPECT). DIMEDIT itself was missing too; only DIMTEDIT existed.

title: Dynamic Input options menu (DYNPROMPT), second-value lock; INS on ATTDEF/MLEADER, GCEN on closed splines (part of #519)
author: vangel76
body:
Part of #519.

## The problem
Dynamic Input had no options menu: at a prompt with keywords (CIRCLE's 3P/2P/Ttr, LINE's Undo…) there was no way to see or pick them at the cursor. Only the first pointer-input value could be locked, and DYNPROMPT didn't exist. On the snap side (gaps.md U8), Insertion ignored attribute definitions and multileaders, and Geometric Center worked only on closed lightweight polylines.

## Changes

Enter, Space or a click sends the keyword, the same way a click on it at the command line does. Escape or typing closes the menu. The tooltip shows a small down-arrow sign (drawn in code) when the prompt has options, and it stays where it is while the menu is open so the pointer can reach it. title: QDIM: Staggered, Baseline, Ordinate, Radius, Diameter, datumPoint and Edit (fixes #507)
author: vangel76
body:
Fixes #507, together with #514 (DIMSTYLE variables) and #522 (DIMEDIT, DIMJOGGED, DIMJOGLINE, DIMBREAK, DIMINSPECT). This PR is based on `main` and is independent of those two.

## The problem

QDIM made only continuous linear dimensions, through the JSON form. It had no Staggered, Baseline, Ordinate, Radius or Diameter mode, no datum point, no Edit, and no command-line prompt sequence.

## Changes

New `crates/engine/src/cmd/annotate_qdim.rs`; the old `run_qdim` moved there. `qdim {handles?, at, mode?, vertical?, datum?, add?, remove?, tolerance?}`:

- **Continuous**: as before. Without `vertical`, the orientation now follows the line position like DIMLINEAR, so a position beside the geometry gives vertical dimensions. The existing callers keep their horizontal results.
- **Staggered**: symmetric pairs nested from the middle out. The innermost pair sits at the line position; each further pair is DIMDLI further out.
- **Baseline**: from the first point, or from the point nearest `datum`, to every other point. Each dimension is DIMDLI further from the geometry.
- **Ordinate**: one ordinate dimension per point, measured from the origin or from `datum`. The leaders run to the line position. Horizontal mode gives X datums, vertical mode Y datums.
- **Radius / Diameter**: one dimension for every selected circle and arc, pointing toward the line position.
- **Edit**: `remove` drops dimension points (the nearest within `tolerance`, which is the pick box at the prompt). `add` adds points.
- **Prompt sequence**: "Select geometry to dimension", then "Specify dimension line position or [Continuous/Staggered/Baseline/Ordinate/Radius/Diameter/datumPoint/Edit/seTtings] <current mode>". It previews the current mode at the cursor.
  - datumPoint asks for the new datum.

title: REGION: region entity, UNION/SUBTRACT/INTERSECT, MASSPROP (fixes #510)
author: vangel76
body:
Fixes #510.

This is the third and last part of #510, after #517 (MLINE, MLSTYLE, MLEDIT) and #521 (HELIX). The three PRs are independent of each other: each one applies to `main` on its own, they don't conflict with each other, and merged together they build and pass clippy and the tests.

## The problem

REGION turned closed objects into closed polylines. There was no region object, no way to combine regions, and no MASSPROP (`docs/gaps.md` F21).

## Changes

- **Model** (`crates/doc/src/entity/region.rs`): `EntityKind::Region` is a set of closed loops of lines and arcs (`HatchLoop`, with bulges), each marked as an outer loop or an island. It has:
  - area: outer loops minus islands, with exact arcs;
  - perimeter, bounds and a containment test;
  - `renest()`, which sets the outer/island flags from how the loops nest;
  - `props()` for MASSPROP: centroid, plus the second moments about the origin and about the centroid.
- **Commands**:
  - `REGION` now replaces each closed object with a region (the same JSON form as before).
  - `AREA` measures regions.
  - `MASSPROP` (Tools ▸ Inquiry ▸ Region/Mass Properties) reports, as JSON and as a text block: area, perimeter, bounding box, centroid, moments and product of inertia, radii of gyration, and the principal moments and directions about the centroid.
  - `UNION`, `SUBTRACT` and `INTERSECT` (Modify ▸ Solid Editing; select prompts, with SUBTRACT asking twice). They combine regions whose boundaries don't cross or touch: separate pieces, regions inside regions, holes and islands in holes. In that case every loop lies wholly inside or outside the other region, and the result keeps the loops that bound it. An empty result erases the regions. Overlapping boundaries report "not available yet" and leave the drawing unchanged.
- **Edits**:
  - Regions draw as their outline, and snap and select through it.

title: Grip dimensional input: length, angle and radius fields while stretching a grip, DYNDIVIS/DYNDIGRIP (part of #519, stacked on #440)
author: vangel76
body:
Fixes #519 (together with #523).

> **Stacked on #440, which is stacked on #435.** Grip editing has to be an engine command (`GRIP`, #435) before its prompts can carry the stretched grip. This branch is based on `feat/425-grip-menus` (#440) so it merges cleanly with that PR's changes to the same GRIP prompt. Until those land, the diff here includes their commits; the change in this PR is the last commit only ("Grip dimensional input…"). Please merge #435 and #440 first.

## The problem
While a grip is stretched, AutoCAD's dimensional input shows the dimensions the stretch changes (a line's new length and angle, a radius…) as fields you can type into. CADCraft showed only the generic pointer boxes, so you couldn't make a line 15 long by dragging its end grip and typing 15. This is the last item of gaps.md U2.

## Changes
- **Engine (`grip_dims`, new module).** For the grip the prompt stretches, it lists the dimensions in cycle order:
  - a line end: resulting length, length change, absolute angle and angle change, all measured from the other end;
  - a polyline vertex: the straight segments on either side;
  - a circle quadrant: the radius and its change.

  Each dimension parses its typed value (lengths in the drawing's units; absolute angles and angle changes per AUNITS/ANGBASE). `resolve` turns locked values into the grip's point: one locked value holds the grip to a circle or ray around its anchor, and two pin it where they cross, taking the crossing nearest the cursor. The middle grip of a line, several hot grips, and the MOVE/ROTATE/SCALE/MIRROR modes have no dimensions.
- **`Prompt.grip`.** The GRIP STRETCH prompt with a single hot grip now names that grip as (object, grip index), so any front end can find it. It is skipped in JSON when empty.

Part of #525.

External references were not supported: an xref BLOCK kept its path through a DXF save (#213), but the referenced drawing was never loaded or drawn, and there was no way to attach, reload, unload, detach or bind one (`docs/gaps.md` F2, alpha blocker).

title: feat(text): MTEXT paragraph formatting (indents, tabs, lists) and columns
author: vangel76
body:
Part of #532.

## The problem
MTEXT had no paragraph formatting and no columns (`docs/gaps.md` F9). The `\p` paragraph codes real drawings use for indents, tab stops and bulleted or numbered lists were skipped, so lists lost their hanging indent and tab characters drew nothing useful. `\N` column breaks were plain paragraph breaks. MTEXT's Columns option said "not available yet", and the DXF column groups were dropped on read and never written.

## Changes
- **Layout (fonts)**: a new `mtext/para.rs` handles paragraph codes and columns. It only runs when the contents contain `\p` or a tab, or the MTEXT has columns, so the existing path is untouched. A test checks that the new path gives exactly the old geometry for plain contents. What it lays out:
  - `\p…;` paragraph properties from the DXF Reference's MTEXT inline codes: `i` first-line indent, `l` left indent, `r` right indent, `q` alignment (l/c/r/j/d), `t` tab stops (with `c`/`r`/`d` kinds), and `b`/`a` space before and after. Values are in text heights and stay in effect until changed.
  - Tab characters go to the next stop. A hanging indent's left indent also acts as a stop, so `\pxi-3,l3,t3;1.<tab>Item` works. After the last stop, tabs fall every 4 text heights.
  - Justified and distributed lines.
  - `\N` column breaks.
  - Static columns (fixed count; text past the last column runs on below it) and dynamic columns (added as needed, one height or manual heights), with gutter and right-to-left flow.
- **Model (doc)**: `MText.columns: Option<MTextColumns>` holds the type, count, gutter, height, auto height, manual heights and flow-reversed flag. `MText.width` is the column width. Columns scale with the entity, and extents span all columns.
- **DXF (io)**: MTEXT columns are read and written as groups 75/76/78/79/48/49/50. When reading, a group 50 that comes after the column type is a column height, not the rotation, and an embedded object's groups (after 101) are ignored. Contents encode a tab as `^I` and a ca…

author: vangel76
body:
Part of #534 (cell styles, formulas, TABLEEXPORT; table breaking and data links follow in a second PR).

## The problem
TABLE objects had one text height and margin per table style and nothing else (`docs/gaps.md` F11): no cell styles (fill, colours, alignment, borders, number format), no formulas, no way to export a table.

## Changes
- **Model (`crates/doc`):** `CellStyle` (text style, height, colour, fill, alignment 1–9, horizontal/vertical margins, six borders with visibility/colour/lineweight in the DXF order, number format General/Decimal/Percent/Text with precision, merge flag) in `tables/cellstyle.rs`. `TableStyle.cell_styles` holds custom styles and Title/Header/Data only where they differ from what the style's text height and margin imply, so plain styles stay plain (and DWG round trips keep comparing equal). `Table.row_styles`, `TableCell.style` and `TableCell.formula` (all `serde(default)`, skipped when empty). `Table` gets a `Default`.
- **Layout (`crates/render/src/table.rs`):** `table_geometry` lays out fills, borders and texts from the cell styles and is shared by the display list and the DXF writer's `*T` block. Borders between differently styled cells follow the bottom/top (right/left) borders; inside borders apply between cells of the same style; merged cells have no inner borders. Table scaling (SCALE changes the table's text height) scales every cell style height and margin. Tables above 1,000,000 cells draw their outline only.
- **Formulas (`crates/engine/src/cmd/table/formula.rs`):** text starting with `=` (or the `formula` parameter of `table.set`) is stored as the formula; the cell shows the value, formatted by its cell style. Sum, Average, Count, Min, Max, Abs, Round, `A1` / `$A$1` references, ranges, `+ - * / ^`, parentheses, unary signs. title: DXF: keep full-circle, spline and clockwise ellipse hatch edges (fixes #492, #493, #494)
author: tsangiotis
body:
Fixes #492, fixes #493, fixes #494.

All three are in the edge-boundary branch of `hatch` in `crates/io/src/dxf_read.rs`.

## The problems

- **#492, full-circle arc edge.** An arc edge from 0 to 360 starts and ends on the same point. It got one bulge (`tan(TAU/4)`, effectively infinite) between two identical vertices, and the closing-duplicate check then removed one of them: the loop became a single vertex.
- **#493, spline edges.** The DXF order is 94, 73, 74, 95, 96, then the 40 knots, then the 10/20 control points. The reader skipped to 96 and expected a 10 next, found 40s, and collected no control points, so the curve was dropped (a closed spline loop came back empty).
- **#494, clockwise ellipse edges.** Group 73 was skipped (`i += 8`), so every ellipse edge was drawn counterclockwise and a clockwise half-ellipse filled the opposite side of its chord.

## Changes

- **Arc:** a sweep of a full turn goes in as two half circles (bulge ±1 each).
- **Spline:** degree, knots, control points (with their 42 weights when rational) and fit points are read in order, bounded by their counts, and the spline is built from them. If the knots don't form a valid spline, it falls back to fit points (when there are no control points) or to `Spline::from_control` as before. A first point that repeats the previous edge's end is not repeated.
- **Ellipse:** group 73 is read. A clockwise edge's parameters are mirrored the same way the arc branch already mirrors a clockwise arc's angles: the ccw sweep from `-end` to `-start`, walked backwards.

## Tests

`hatch_edges_keep_full_circles_splines_and_clockwise_ellipses` checks the model extents of each case: the 0–360 circle, a Bézier spline closed by a line (peaks at y = 3), and the 0–180 half-ellipse clockwise (lower half) and counterclockwise (upper half). It fails on main.

I also ran a probe built from the three issues' repro scripts against a release `cadcraft-cli`, measuring each imported loop's area:

title: Constraints: DOF report, G2 Smooth, ellipse/spline/block geometry (part of #546)
author: vangel76
body:
Part of #546.

## The problem

The parametric solver (`docs/gaps.md` F25) had no degrees-of-freedom report or fully-constrained status, Smooth was only tangency (G1), and ellipses, elliptical arcs, splines and block references could not take part in constraints.

## Changes

Our own solver code throughout (textbook numerics: Householder QR with column pivoting, B-spline end derivatives from derivative control points; no GPL solver code consulted).

- **DOF analysis** (`crates/constraints/src/dof.rs`, new `constraints.dof` command, `dof` summary in `constraints.inspect`):
  - per connected component: free parameters minus the rank of the constraint Jacobian (rows and columns balanced first; difference noise in columns is not mistaken for a direction);
  - per object: the rank of the Jacobian's null space restricted to the object's own parameters, i.e. how many independent ways it can still move;
  - status `unconstrained` / `under` / `fully` / `over` (redundant equations), plus a message (`Fully constrained`, `4 degrees of freedom remaining`, `Over-constrained: 1 redundant equation`).
  - `{handles?|handle?}` defaults to the selection, else every constrained object; unconstrained objects report their own parameter count.
- **Redundancy hint**: a redundant constraint is still refused, and the message now names the constraints it duplicates (each one whose removal would make it independent), not every constraint on the same objects. A Fix that locks parameters other constraints already determine is now refused too (it used to slip through because it adds no residual rows).
- **Ellipses and elliptical arcs** (`model.rs`, `residual.rs`, `curves.rs`): centre, axis ends (`v0`–`v3`) and arc ends as constraint points; point on ellipse; line tangent to an ellipse (support function); circle/arc/ellipse tangent to an ellipse through two auxiliary contact parameters (settled before residuals are measured, so `all_satisfied` stays exact); Concentric; Horizontal/Vertical on the ma…

title: feat(text): fields (FIELD, UPDATEFIELD, DWGPROPS) and SPELL
author: vangel76
body:
Part of #532.

## The problem
CADCraft had no fields and no spell check (`docs/gaps.md` F9). FIELD, UPDATEFIELD and SPELL were missing, and a field code in a text was drawn as its raw code.

## Changes
- **Field codes (`cadcraft_doc::fields`)**:
  - Finds, parses and rewrites field codes in text, using the publicly documented syntax: `%<\AcVar Date \f "d.M.yyyy">%`, and `%<\AcObjProp Object(%<\_ObjId 2A>%).Area \f "%lu2%pr2">%` (nested fields, quoted formats).
  - Two parts are our own format:
    - The object id is the object's handle in hex.
    - Each field keeps its last value in the code as `\CcValue "…"`. A drawing therefore shows its fields without evaluating them again, and the value survives DXF and copy/paste with the text.
  - Unclosed codes are plain text. Nesting is capped at 8 and fields per text at 1000.
- **Rendering**:
  - TEXT, MTEXT and attributes are drawn with their field values (`####` when there is no value).
  - While `FIELDDISPLAY` is 1 (the default), field values get a grey background. On MTEXT it covers the field glyphs only; it is found by laying the values out in a marker colour. On TEXT and attributes it covers the whole text.
  - The background is never drawn when plotting.
- **FIELD** (Insert > Field...):
  - Places a multiline text holding a field. Field types:
    - Date (format pictures `yyyy MM M MMMM dd d dddd HH hh mm ss tt`, text in quotes)
    - SaveDate (`TDUPDATE`)
    - Filename

title: Constraints: CONSTRAINTINFER while drawing and editing, DOF status on the canvas (fixes #546)
author: vangel76
body:
Fixes #546.

**Stacked on #550** (DOF report, G2 Smooth, ellipse/spline/block geometry): this branch contains #550's commit plus one commit; review the last commit, or merge #550 first.

## The problem

With CONSTRAINTINFER on, nothing was inferred while drawing (the setting existed in CONSTRAINTSETTINGS but did nothing, and the variable could not be read or set), and the constraint bars and canvas did not show how constrained the geometry is.

## Changes

- **CONSTRAINTINFER** (`crates/engine/src/cmd/constraints.rs` `infer_after`, `crates/constraints/src/auto.rs` `infer_placed`):
  - after a command drew or edited objects (new or changed in the current space), what it placed *exactly* onto existing geometry is constrained: Coincident (end to end, midpoint, centre, or onto the object), Tangent, Perpendicular (also a T onto the middle of a line), Parallel (the nearest exactly parallel line) and Horizontal/Vertical; consecutive LINE segments join; MOVE/grip edits that land on geometry are inferred too;
  - snapped points are exact, so tight tolerances (1e-9 relative, 1e-7°) see every snap — running snaps, typed overrides, tracking — and ortho/polar, whichever way the point came in. That keeps the hook tiny: nothing in the point-input path changes (other open PRs work there), only the post-command hook;
  - each candidate goes through `cs::add`, so redundant ones are skipped (a TAN snap keeps Tangent; the end-on-curve coincidence it implies adds nothing);
  - the inferred types are filtered by the AutoConstrain types (CONSTRAINTSETTINGS), as AutoCAD does; commands that change constraints themselves, and commands placing more than 50 objects (arrays, pastes), are skipped; undo takes the inferred constraints with the command.
- `CONSTRAINTINFER` system variable (GETVAR/SETVAR, 0/1, stored in the drawing's parametric settings) and a `constraintinfer` command so typing the variable name works (`Enter new value for CONSTRAINTINFER <0>:`; JSON `{value?}`).

title: Support files: user .lin linetypes and .pat hatch patterns (part of #552)
author: vangel76
body:
Part of #552.

## The problem
CADCraft could only use its own built-in linetypes and hatch patterns. A user who has their own `.lin` linetype file or `.pat` hatch pattern file (from their office standards, a client, an earlier CAD setup) had no way to load them (`docs/gaps.md` FF9).

## Changes
- **Readers** (`cadcraft_doc::library::files`): `parse_lin` and `parse_pat` follow the publicly documented LIN and PAT text formats: `*NAME[,description]` headers, `;` comments, `A,dash,gap,…` linetype lines, `angle, x, y, dx, dy[, dashes…]` pattern lines.

author: vangel76

Part of #563.

## The problem
COUNT only counted block references placed directly in model space. References inside other blocks, in layouts, or in a selection were not counted, and there was no way to count "objects like this one", highlight what was counted, or put the counts in the drawing (`docs/gaps.md` F22).

author: vangel76
body:
Part of #564.

## The problem
Plot style tables store an end, join and fill style for every style, but plots ignored them (`docs/plot-styles.md`: "stored but not applied yet"). Wide lines always printed with round ends and joins, and filled areas were always solid.

PDF output from PLOT / EXPORTPDF was one sheet per file with no layers and no links (docs/gaps.md FF10): drawing layers were flattened, a set of layouts needed one file each, and entity hyperlinks were lost.
