title: CLI: cadcraft-cli exits quietly when stdout is closed early
author: switch87
body:
Fixes #537.

## The bug

```sh
set -o pipefail
cadcraft-cli commands | head -c 20 >/dev/null
echo $?
```

```
thread 'main' panicked at library/std/src/io/stdio.rs:1166:9:
failed printing to stdout: Broken pipe (os error 32)
101
```

Every stdout write goes through `println!`, which panics on the first write after the reader is gone. `commands` prints a few thousand lines, far more than a pipe buffer holds, so the reader is closed mid-stream and the process dies instead of finishing its work. A one-entity `info` piped to `head` survives only because it fits in the buffer.

## The fix

Port of the approach FilmCraft took in storytold/filmcraft#297:

- `outln!` replaces every `println!` on stdout. It writes through `writeln!`, and on error hands the error to `stdout_failed`.
- A write error of kind `BrokenPipe` marks stdout as gone and nothing more: later output is dropped instead of retried. The work continues — the remaining `--cmd` results, `--save` and `--export` still happen, so `cadcraft-cli run … --save out.dxf | head` keeps the drawing.
- Any *other* stdout write error is reported on stderr (`cadcraft-cli: can't write to stdout: …`) and flips `STDOUT_ERROR`, which `main` turns into exit status 1.
- A failing command still reports 1 (and a usage error 2) whether or not anyone reads stdout, so `--keep-going`-style pipelines keep their exit codes honest. `eprintln!` output is untouched: stderr is what diagnostics are for.

## Proof

Built both ways on the same branch, same command:

| tree | result |
|---|---|
| `upstream/main` | panic `failed printing to stdout: Broken pipe (os error 32)`, exit 101 |
| this branch | no output, exit 0 |

## Tests

New `apps/cadcraft-cli/tests/cli.rs`:

- `closed_stdout_ends_quietly` — spawns the CLI with a piped stdout, reads 10 bytes, drops the reader (exactly `| head -c 10`), and asserts exit 0 with an empty stderr for `commands`, `commands ellipse` and `--version`.
- `closed_stdout_still_runs_the_commands_and_saves` — with std…

title: Plotters: device configurations with paper sizes and printable areas (fixes #564)
author: vangel76
body:
Fixes #564. The first part (plot style ends, joins and fill patterns) is in #566.

## The problem
CADCraft had no plotter devices. Plots always went to PDF on a standard paper size, and margins could be set only by hand per layout. Users couldn't define their own output devices or paper sizes with printable areas (`docs/gaps.md` F14).

## Changes
- **Device files** (`cadcraft_doc::PlotterConfig`, new `docs/plotters.md`): our own documented JSON format `*.plotter.json` with a format marker. A file holds the name, output (`pdf`/`png`/`svg`), resolution (dpi), default orientation, default paper, and the papers with margins (printable area). Reading fixes hostile values: sizes, margins, a 1 MB cap, unique paper names, at most 512 papers. Binary `.pc3` files are not read.

- **Host store hook** `cmd::plotters::set_plotter_store` (list/read/write/delete by file name). Without a hook, native builds use `<settings dir>/plotters`, the same settings directory and `CADCRAFT_CONFIG_DIR` convention as the workspace file. The web keeps devices in memory for the session. File names are cleaned, so names can't escape the folder.
- **PLOTTERMANAGER** (File ▸ Plotter Manager...) has actions `list`, `get`, `new` (from a device, or the built-in device for an output), `set` (fields; add/replace/remove papers; default paper), `delete`, `load` (text) and `save` (text or path). title: PDF export: real text in embedded TrueType subsets (part of #560)
author: vangel76
body:
Part of #560. Stacked on #567 (PDF layers, several sheets, hyperlinks): the first commit here is #567's, and the change of its own is the second commit, `PDF: text as text in embedded TrueType subsets`.

## The problem
Plotted PDFs drew all text as filled outlines or strokes (docs/gaps.md FF10). It couldn't be selected, searched or copied, and every glyph cost a polygon in the file.

## Changes
- **Shaping reports font glyphs** (`cadcraft-fonts`): `Shaped::text` lists every outline glyph as a `TextGlyph` (face, glyph id, character, outline index, origin and em axes). It survives placement (alignment, rotation, width factor, obliquing, backwards / upside down), MTEXT layout, dimension text (`DimGeometry::text_runs`), attributes, tables and fallback-font glyphs. Block and viewport transforms carry it along too.
- **Plot display lists record the glyphs** (`cadcraft-render`): `DisplayList::texts` / `PlotText` say which filled outline primitive stands for which glyph (plots with TEXTFILL on). Model text seen through a viewport comes along as well; a glyph cut by the viewport edge stays a clipped outline. Screen lists are unchanged.
- **The PDF writer embeds font subsets** (`cadcraft-io`, new `pdf/fonts.rs`):
  - one `Type0` font per face, with `Identity-H` encoding over a `CIDFontType2` (`/CIDToGIDMap /Identity`), `/W` widths, a font descriptor with `/FontFile2`, and a `ToUnicode` CMap, so copy and search give the right characters (BMP and beyond);

  - text sits inside its layer's optional-content section, and the plot style colour applies.

title: SETVAR accepts point objects for SNAPBASE, LIMMIN, LIMMAX and INSBASE (#485)
author: MarekSpodBiedry
body:
Fixes #485.

SETVAR's generic header-variable path turned only JSON arrays into points, so an `{x, y[, z]}` object (the shape GETVAR returns for SNAPBASE, LIMMIN, LIMMAX and INSBASE) was rejected as an invalid value. That arm now takes objects too and passes them to the same `as_pt` converter, which already handles both forms. SNAPUNIT and GRIDUNIT already accepted objects through `as_pt`, so the point variables now match them.

Test: `setvar_point_variables_take_point_objects` writes GETVAR's own value back for each of the four variables, checks that `{x: 5, y: 7}` reads back as `(5, 7, 0)`, and checks that a non-numeric coordinate is still rejected.

title: SETVAR keeps text variables such as CLAYER as text, so a layer named 10 can be selected (#484)
author: MarekSpodBiedry
body:
Fixes #484.

`sysvars::set` turns typed text that looks like a number into an integer or real before it looks at the header variable's type. For numeric variables this is right, but it has no case for text variables. So `setvar CLAYER 10` stored the number 10. `getvar` then returned `10` as a number, and new objects went to layer `0`, because the CLAYER text lookup falls back to its default when the stored value is not text.

The change adds a `Str` case beside the existing `Real`, `Int` and `Point` cases that keep a known variable's type stable. A text variable keeps what was typed. If a JSON number is passed, it is stored as its text. The JSON command and the typed SETVAR prompt both go through this setter, so the change fixes both.

Covers the restoration check in the issue:
- `setvar {"name":"CLAYER","value":"10"}` then `getvar` returns the string `"10"`, and the next object is on layer `10`.
- `setvar CLAYER 0` returns the string `"0"`.
- Typed `SETVAR CLAYER 10` at the command line also gives `"10"`.
- Numeric variables are unchanged: `setvar LUNITS "3"` still gives the number `3`.

Test: `setvar_clayer_keeps_numeric_layer_name` in `crates/engine/src/tests.rs`. It fails without the fix because CLAYER comes back as the number 10.

title: Dimension Space asks for the base, the dimensions and the spacing instead of failing (#483)
author: MarekSpodBiedry
body:
Fixes #483.

Dimension > Dimension Space (and DIMSPACE typed at the command line) had no prompt machine, so starting it ran the JSON command with no parameters and stopped at once with "`base` dimension is required".

DIMSPACE now has an interactive machine (`DimSpaceM` in `crates/engine/src/cmd/annotate.rs`), built from the same `SelectPhase` that the other selection commands use:

1. **Select base dimension** - one pick; an object that is not a dimension is refused with "Select a dimension." and the prompt comes back.
2. **Select dimensions to space** - normal object selection, ended with Enter (an empty selection ends the command).
3. **Enter value or [Auto] <Auto>** - a non-negative spacing, or Enter / Auto for the default (twice DIMDLI, scaled as before).

It then calls the existing `run_dimspace` with `{base, handles, spacing}`, so the spacing logic and the JSON form (`dimspace {"base":..., "handles":[...], "spacing":...}`) do not change. The menu, the command line, scripts and the control channel all reach this same machine through `Session::start`.

With the fixture from the issue (dimensions at y = 5 and y = 9, spacing 2), the base stays at y = 5 and the other dimension moves to y = 7, the same result as the JSON control.

### Test

`dimspace_prompts_for_its_inputs` in `crates/engine/src/cmd/annotate_tests.rs` builds the fixture from the issue, starts `dimspace` with no parameters, checks each prompt, picks the base, picks the other dimension, enters 2, and checks the base at y = 5 and the target at y = 7. Without the fix `start("dimspace")` returns the missing-base error, so the test fails. The existing `dimtedit_and_dimspace` and `dim_baseline_spacing` tests keep covering the JSON form.

title: dimstyle.rename and delete: cover dimensions inside block definitions (#482)
author: MarekSpodBiedry
body:
Fixes #482.

`dimstyle.rename` found the dimensions and leaders to update with `dims_using`, which walks only model space and the layouts. Dimensions inside block definitions kept the old style name, so after a rename they pointed at a style the drawing no longer defines, and the saved DXF kept that stale reference.

Changes in `crates/engine/src/cmd/props.rs`:

- New `block_dims_using` lists the dimensions and leaders in block definitions that use a style.
- `run_dimstyle_rename` also renames the style on those entities (copy-on-write through `Arc::make_mut`, the same way the linetype branch of `rename` already updates block entities). `rename {"table":"dimstyle"}` goes through the same function, so it is fixed too.
- `run_dimstyle_delete` uses the same check, so it now refuses to delete a style that only a block's dimension uses, instead of leaving that dimension with an undefined style.

Test: `dimstyle_rename_updates_block_dimensions` follows the steps in the issue: a dimension in style DS is turned into block BD, then the test checks that `dimstyle.delete DS` is refused and that after `dimstyle.rename DS -> DS2` the dimension inside BD uses DS2. Without the fix, both checks fail.

title: Properties: changing a block's scale moves and resizes its attributes (#481)
author: MarekSpodBiedry
body:
Fixes #481.

`properties.set` with `scale` on a block reference set the new scale but left the attached attribute text where it was, at its old height. SCALE and INSERT at the same scale both carry the attributes along, so the reference and its annotation drifted apart after a Properties edit.

The block-reference branch of `properties.set` now scales each attribute's text about the insertion point by `new / old` before storing the new scale. It uses the same text transform that SCALE applies to attributes. Only the attributes are touched: the insertion point, rotation and MINSERT row/column spacing behave as before. The property value stays absolute, so 2 -> 3 is a factor of 1.5.

Scope: positive uniform scales, as the issue reports. Negative (mirroring) scale values keep their current behaviour; mirroring attribute text is a separate decision. Rotation edits not rotating attributes is #473, which stays separate.

Tests (`crates/engine/tests/props_insert_scale_attribs.rs`), both from the issue's restoration check:
- scale 1 -> 2 at the origin: attribute moves to (20,0), height 5, value `hello` kept;
- reference at (7,11) with scale 2 -> 3: attribute moves to (37,11), height 7.5, insertion point unchanged.

Both fail on main (the attribute stays at its old position and height).

title: Properties: reject a malformed lineweight instead of setting 0.25 mm (#480)
author: MarekSpodBiedry
body:
Fixes #480.

`properties.set` parsed `lineweight` inline and fell back to `0.25` when a string could not be read, so `"lineweight": "notanumber"` reported `{"changed":1}` and overwrote the object's lineweight (ByLayer or 0.70 mm) with an explicit 0.25 mm.

It now uses the same `parse_lw` that `layer.set` already uses (made `pub(super)` in `layer.rs`) and returns `bad lineweight`, the same error `layer` and `lweight` give for this input. The value is parsed before the drawing is touched, so on error nothing changes.

Valid input behaves as before: numbers (`0.70`), strings with or without `mm` (`"0.70 mm"`), and `ByLayer` / `ByBlock` / `Default`. Leaving `lineweight` out still leaves it alone.

Test: `crates/engine/tests/props_bad_lineweight.rs` sets `"notanumber"` on a fresh circle and on one already set to 0.70 mm, and checks that the call fails and the lineweight stays the same. It also checks that `0.70`, `"0.35 mm"` and `"ByBlock"` still work. Before the fix the malformed call succeeds, so the test fails.

title: Quick Dimension from the menu asks for the objects and the dimension line location (#479)
author: MarekSpodBiedry
body:
Fixes #479.

**Cause.** `qdim` had no `interactive` prompt machine, so Dimension > Quick Dimension (and typing `qdim`) ran the JSON form with null parameters and failed at once with ``invalid parameters for `qdim`: `at` ([x, y]) is required``.

**Fix.** A small `QdimM` prompt machine in `crates/engine/src/cmd/annotate.rs`: "Select objects" (or the pickfirst selection), then "Specify dimension line position", then the existing `run_qdim` with `{handles, at}`. It uses the same `SelectPhase` flow as `ArrayM` and `SelectRun`: an empty selection ends the command, and objects picked at the prompt don't stay selected afterwards. The JSON form is unchanged. No new QDIM modes; the `vertical` option is still JSON-only.

**Tests** (`annotate_tests.rs`):
- `qdim_accepts_selection_and_location_interactively`: the issue's repro (line [0,0]-[10,0], location [0,5]) through the bare `qdim` command now produces the dimension with extension origins [0,0] and [10,0] and definition point [0,5]. Before the fix `cmdline("qdim")` returns the missing-`at` error.
- `qdim_cancelled_before_location_creates_nothing`: cancelling after the selection but before the location leaves the drawing unchanged (the issue's cancel check).

`every_interactive_command_starts_and_cancels` now covers `qdim` too.

title: Align Text > Angle asks for the angle instead of failing with a missing-parameter error (#478)
author: MarekSpodBiedry
body:
Fixes #478.

Dimension > Align Text > Angle starts `dimtedit.angle` with no parameters. The command had no interactive form, so `Session::start` ran it with null parameters and `run_dimtedit` stopped with "`angle` (degrees) is required", even with a dimension preselected.

`dimtedit.angle` now has an interactive form: `TEditM::angle()`, the same machine the main DIMTEDIT command uses, started in its Angle step. A single preselected dimension is taken at once (pickfirst, as in DIMTEDIT) and the user is asked "Specify angle for dimension text". With no preselection it first asks "Select dimension". The angle is read with the same angle settings as DIMTEDIT's Angle option.

Not changed: `dimtedit.angle {"angle": 30}` and other JSON calls still run the command directly, and Home/Left/Center/Right keep their current behaviour (they already work on a preselected dimension).

Test: `align_text_angle_menu_entry_asks_for_the_angle` in `crates/engine/tests/dimtedit_prompts.rs` starts `dimtedit.angle` with the dimension preselected, types 30 and checks that the text rotation is 30 degrees. It also checks the "Select dimension" prompt with nothing selected. Without the fix, `start("dimtedit.angle")` returns the missing-angle error.

title: Hatch: skip repeated boundary loops so repeated picks keep the fill (#477)
author: MarekSpodBiedry
body:
Fixes #477.

HATCH (SOLID) and GRADIENT fill loops even-odd, so when two picks in the same region (or the same object selected twice) added the same boundary loop twice, the two copies cancelled out and the hatch had no fill.

Now the repeated loop is added only once:

- **Internal points** (`points` and the interactive "Pick internal point"): a loop is skipped when the same loop, with the same outer/island role, is already in the list. A pick inside an island still adds that island as its own outer loop, as before, so the island stays filled.
- **Selected objects** (`handles` and the interactive "Select objects"): an object that is selected twice is counted once.

Both commands share `make()` and `HatchM`, so the fix covers HATCH and GRADIENT on every entry path.

Tests:
- `repeated_picks_do_not_duplicate_boundary_loops`: for HATCH SOLID and GRADIENT, three points in one rectangle and the same handle twice each give one loop; one point in each of two rectangles still gives two loops. It fails without the fix.
- `picking_inside_an_island_keeps_its_own_loop`: a pick in the region around an island plus a pick inside the island keeps every loop from both picks.

title: properties.set rejects a linetype that is not loaded (#476)
author: MarekSpodBiedry
body:
Fixes #476.

`properties.set` wrote any `linetype` string onto the selected objects. An unloaded name such as `NOPE` replaced a valid DASHED assignment, reported `{"changed":1}`, drew as a continuous line and survived DXF save and reopen.

Now an explicit object linetype must be `ByLayer`, `ByBlock` or a linetype loaded in the drawing. Any other name returns `linetype `NOPE` is not loaded` and leaves every object unchanged. This is the same check and message that `linetype {"current": ...}` already uses, and the Properties palette only offers these names. The name is checked before anything else changes, so a rejected call also does not create the layer passed in `layer`. A loaded name is stored with its defined spelling, the same way `dimStyle` is already resolved in this command.

Test: `properties_set_rejects_unloaded_linetype` in `crates/engine/src/cmd/props.rs`. It loads DASHED and assigns it to a line, checks that `NOPE` is rejected and the line keeps DASHED, and checks that `ByBlock` and `ByLayer` are still accepted. Without the fix the `NOPE` call succeeds and the test fails.

title: INSERT with explode records one undo step (#475)
author: MarekSpodBiedry
body:
Fixes #475.

An exploded JSON INSERT (`"name": "*B"` or `"explode": true`) ran EXPLODE through `Session::execute`, which recorded its own undo snapshot inside the INSERT. The history got two entries for one operation, and the second Undo brought back the intermediate block reference.

`run_insert` now calls the EXPLODE command body directly, so only INSERT records an undo step. Other commands already do this when one command runs another (`SelectRun::run` in `machines.rs`, RENAME in `props.rs`). The interactive `-INSERT *B` path already used `explode_insert` and was not affected. A separate INSERT followed by EXPLODE still records two steps.

Test: `exploded_json_insert_is_one_undo_step` in `crates/engine/tests/insert_file.rs` runs the issue's fixture for both JSON forms. It checks for exactly one new undo entry, then empty model space with B still defined after the first Undo, then the original Line and no B after the second Undo. Without the fix, the second Undo leaves a block reference and the test fails.

title: layer.delete: clear the deleted layer from viewport freeze and colour overrides (#474)
author: MarekSpodBiedry
body:
Fixes #474.

`layer.delete` removed the layer from the layer table, but layout viewports kept it in their frozen list and colour overrides. Those stale entries were saved to DXF. A new layer with the same name then picked them up, so its geometry was hidden or plotted in the old colour.

`layer.delete` now calls the same helper that `laydel`/`laymrg` already use (`merge::forget_in_viewports`, made `pub(super)`), so all delete paths behave the same. `PURGE` deletes layers through `layer.delete`, so it is fixed as well.

Test: `layer_delete_clears_viewport_overrides_for_the_layer` in `crates/engine/tests/layer_merge_delete.rs`. It deletes an empty layer that a viewport freezes and checks that the viewport keeps only the other layers' settings. Then it recreates a layer with the same name and checks that the layer is not frozen. The test fails without the fix.

title: Properties: turn a block reference's attribute text with its Rotation edit (#473)
author: MarekSpodBiedry
body:
Fixes #473.

Setting a block reference's Rotation in Properties (`properties.set` with `rotation`) changed only the reference's angle. Its attribute text kept its old position and angle, so the text no longer matched the block.

Now the setter works out the turn (new angle minus old angle) and applies it to each attribute the same way ROTATE does through `transform_text`:

- the text's insertion point and its alignment point (when set) rotate around the reference's insertion point;
- the turn is added to the text angle (`norm_angle`, as in `transform_text`);
- value, height and the other text settings stay as they were.

With the fixture from the issue, the attribute moves from (10,0) to (0,10) and its angle goes from 0 to 90 degrees, the same as the ROTATE and INSERT-with-rotation controls.

The Properties palette in the UI sends this same `properties.set` command, so the fix covers it too.

### Test

`block_rotation_property_turns_attribute_text` in `crates/engine/src/tests.rs` builds the fixture from the issue (ATTDEF at (10,0), BLOCK, INSERT with value `hello`), sets Rotation to 90 and checks that the reference angle is 90 degrees, the attribute is at (0,10) with a 90-degree angle, and that its value and height (2.5) did not change. Without the fix the attribute stays at (10,0), so the test fails.

title: Text style rename: update text inside block definitions (#472)
author: MarekSpodBiedry
body:
Fixes #472.

`style.rename` (and `rename {"table":"textstyle"}`, which calls it) moved TEXT, MTEXT, ATTDEF and insert attributes in model space and layouts to the new name, but skipped block definitions. Text in a block kept pointing at the old name, which no longer exists, so it fell back to default style settings (the issue's backwards-text example renders differently after the rename).

Changes in `run_style_rename` (`crates/engine/src/cmd/props.rs`):
- Block definitions are walked too, the same way `layer.set` repoints layers in blocks (`Arc::make_mut` only on blocks that actually use the style). This covers TEXT, MTEXT and ATTDEF in a definition, and the ATTRIBs of an insert nested in another block.
- MLeader text is repointed as well. `text_styles_in_use` (the `style.delete` guard) already counts MLeader text as a use of the style, but the rename skipped it, so its text was left on the old name in every space.
- Model space and layouts behave as before.

Test: `text_style_rename_follows_block_definition_text` puts a TEXT, an MTEXT and an ATTDEF on a backwards style into a block (`keep: "delete"`, so there is no insert), renames the style, and checks that all three in the definition now use the new name and that the renamed style is still backwards. Without the fix all three keep the old name.

title: dimstyle.delete refuses a style used by a dimension inside a block (#471)
author: MarekSpodBiedry
body:
Fixes #471.

`dimstyle.delete` checked whether a style is in use with `dims_using`, which only looks at model space and the layouts. A dimension that had been turned into a block (`block {"keep":"convert"}`) lives only in the block definition, so the check missed it. The style was deleted, and the block dimension kept a reference to a style that no longer existed, also after save and reopen.

The delete guard now also looks at the dimensions and leaders inside block definitions, the same way PURGE (`blocks/purge.rs`) already counts block-definition entities when deciding whether a dimension style is unused. The error is the existing "dimension style `DS` is in use" message, so it matches the model-space case.

`dims_using` itself is unchanged, because `dimstyle.rename` uses its handles with `modify_entity`, which only reaches model space and layouts. Rename has the same gap for block dimensions; that is reported separately in #482.

Test: `dimstyle_delete_refuses_style_used_by_block_dimension` in `annotate_tests.rs` follows the issue's steps (style DS, a linear dimension, convert it to block BD, make Standard current) and checks that deleting DS fails and DS is still defined. Without the fix the delete succeeds and the test fails. The existing `dimstyle_commands` test still covers the model-space refusal and deleting an unused style.

title: STYLE typed with no arguments opens the Text Style dialog instead of an error (#535)
author: MarekSpodBiedry
body:
Fixes #535.

Typing `style` or `st` with no arguments, or choosing **Format > Text Style...**, ran the JSON form of `style` with no parameters and failed with `'name' is required`. The menu entry hit the same error, because it goes through the same route.

Now `style` and `st` open a **Text Style** dialog, in the same way as `linetype`, `tablestyle` and `mleaderstyle` (`managers::route`). The dialog reuses the shared `style_manager` used by Table Style and Multileader Style:
- a list of text styles, with the current one in bold, plus **Set Current** and **New**
- the selected style's height (0 = ask), width factor, backwards and upside down

Every change goes through `app.run("style", {...})`, so it can be undone and scripted. The JSON form (`style {"name": "SCHEM", "font": "Arial"}`) is unchanged, and programmatic calls never open the dialog.

Not in the dialog: font, oblique angle, vertical and annotative. They stay available through the JSON form. The shared style manager only has number, checkbox and choice fields, and a font picker would be a separate change.

Tests (`crates/ui-egui/tests/style_dialogs.rs`):
- `menu_items_open_their_dialogs`: `style` from the menu opens `textstyle` and draws it, and typing bare `style` or `ST` returns no error and opens the dialog. This fails on main.
- `json_calls_never_open_the_dialogs`: `style {"name": "SCHEM", "font": "Arial"}` still creates the style and opens no dialog.

title: OFFSET: full ellipse copy goes to the side of the picked point (#501)
author: MarekSpodBiedry
body:
Fixes #501.

OFFSET put a full ellipse's copy on the wrong side: an outside side point gave an inward copy and an inside point an outward one. Circles and arcs were fine.

**Cause:** `offset_kind` tessellates the ellipse counter-clockwise, and `offset_points` moves each sample along `tangent.perp()`, which is the left normal. On a counter-clockwise curve the left normal points inward. The ellipse branch passed `-dist` for an inside point and `+dist` for an outside point, which is backwards.

**Fix:** swap the sign (`inside` → `+dist`, outside → `-dist`) and add a comment on the convention. The result now matches the circle and arc branches next to it, where inside means `radius - dist`. The JSON command, the interactive OFFSET prompt and its preview all call `offset_kind`, so this one change fixes all three.

**Test:** `crates/engine/tests/offset_ellipse_side.rs` uses the issue's fixture (center 0,0, ratio 0.5, distance 2). It covers a horizontal major axis `[10,0]` and a vertical one `[0,10]`, each with an outside and an inside side point. It checks that the far end of the major axis lands at 12 for the outside point and 8 for the inside point. All four cases fail without the fix.

title: Web: ?cpu selects the CPU canvas instead of installing the GPU canvas (#500)
author: MarekSpodBiedry
body:
Fixes #500.

`packaging/web/README.md` documents `?cpu` as "Force the CPU canvas path", but the web startup in `apps/cadcraft-web/src/main.rs` never looked at it: whenever eframe handed over a wgpu render state, `app.set_wgpu` installed the custom GPU canvas.

The change:
- With a `cpu` flag in the URL query, startup skips `app.set_wgpu`. The canvas then takes its existing CPU path (primitives drawn as egui shapes), as `gpu.rs` describes for "no wgpu render state handed to the app". Without the flag nothing changes; `?webgl` still only selects the WebGL2 backend and keeps the GPU canvas.
- eframe itself still presents through wgpu, so the WebGPU/WebGL2 prerequisite stays as it is (the issue asks for exactly that).
- The flag is read by a small `wants_cpu` helper that matches the whole `cpu` parameter (`?cpu`, `?sample&cpu`, `?cpu=1`), not any substring, so a future flag containing "cpu" will not switch the canvas by accident.
- The module doc lists the `?cpu` flag next to `?webgl` and `?sample`. The README already documents it, so it needs no change.

Test: `cpu_flag_is_detected` in `apps/cadcraft-web/src/main.rs` checks the flag parsing for `?cpu`, `?cpu&sample`, `?sample&cpu`, and for queries without the flag (empty, `?sample`, `?webgl&sample`, `?gpucpu`). Only the native (non-wasm) build runs it; the startup closure itself is wasm-only.

title: Control cmdline.key Escape also ends a clicked grip (#499)
author: MarekSpodBiedry
body:
Fixes #499.

`cmdline.key` with `{"key":"escape"}` only called `Session::cancel`, which cleared the selection but left `app.canvas.hot_grip` set, so the next `ui.click` on the canvas still applied the cancelled grip edit to the line.

Escape on the control channel now does what the keyboard Escape in `cmdline::keyboard` already does: when a clicked grip is hot, it ends the grip, clears the typed buffer and echoes `*Cancel*`, and keeps the selection; with no hot grip it cancels as before (running command, or clears the selection). So two Escapes via `cmdline.key` behave like two Escape key presses.

Only the `cmdline.key` Escape branch in `crates/ui-egui/src/control.rs` changes. `ui.key` Escape already went through the keyboard handler and is unchanged; the documented contract in `docs/control-protocol.md` ("Press Enter or Escape") already describes the new behaviour.

Test: `control::tests::cmdline_key_escape_ends_a_clicked_grip` sets a hot midpoint grip on a selected line with a typed `3`, sends `cmdline.key` Escape and checks that the grip and buffer are gone, `*Cancel*` is echoed and the selection kept; a second Escape clears the selection. It fails on main (the grip stays hot).

title: Parameters Manager: keep a pending expression when the window loses focus (#498)
author: MarekSpodBiedry
body:
Fixes #498.

`parametric::expr_field` kept its pending text only while `Response::has_focus()` was true. That is false for every frame the OS window is unfocused, although the text edit still holds keyboard focus in egui memory. So one unfocused frame dropped the buffer, the field came back with the stored expression, and Enter committed nothing.

The field now reads focus from `Memory::has_focus`, which is what the sibling `palettes::edit_field` already does for the same reason. Commit on Enter or on real focus loss (`Response::lost_focus`) is unchanged, so moving focus to another widget inside the app still commits a changed, nonempty expression.

`expr_field` is shared, so this also covers the other places that use it: Quick Properties fields, the numeric fields in the managers, and the Page Setup scale.

Test: `pending_expression_survives_window_blur` types `+2` into a field holding `1`, blurs and refocuses the window, checks the buffer is still `1+2`, then presses Enter and checks `1+2` is returned. On main the buffer comes back as `1` and the test fails.

title: Command line keyboard input works while the command line is hidden (#497)
author: MarekSpodBiedry
body:
Fixes #497.

The command line's keyboard handler (`cmdline::keyboard`) was only called from `cmdline::show`, which the canvas skips when the command line is hidden (`show_command_line` off, via `ui.set`, `ui.toggle.cmdline` or the menu). So with the command line hidden, Escape no longer cancelled a running command and typing a command name followed by Enter did nothing.

The canvas now calls `cmdline::keyboard` every frame, right where `cmdline::show` used to call it, and `show` only draws the overlay. With the command line shown nothing changes: the handler runs at the same point in the frame as before. The handler still returns early when a text field has keyboard focus.

## Tests

`crates/ui-egui/tests/hidden_command_line.rs` (based on the reporter's probe) runs full app frames through `raw_input_hook`, `logic` and `ui`, for both the shown and hidden command line:
- start LINE, send `ui.key` Escape: the command is cancelled;
- send `ui.text` "LINE" and `ui.key` Enter: LINE starts and is recorded in the typed-command history.

Without the fix, the hidden case fails on the Escape assertion.

title: ui.click and ui.key: deliver the requested modifiers to egui so shift:true acts as a held Shift (#496)
author: MarekSpodBiedry
body:
Fixes #496.

`ui.click` with `shift:true` queues `PointerButton` events whose `modifiers` say Shift, but the canvas reads `ctx.input(|i| i.modifiers)` to choose the snap menu over the shortcut menu and to remove a picked object from the selection. In egui 0.36 that state only changes on `Event::ModifiersChanged` and stays the same across frames, so the requested Shift never reached the canvas.

`CadApp::raw_input_hook` now does this:
- Before it injects a synthetic pointer button or key, it emits `ModifiersChanged` with that event's modifiers when they differ from what egui holds. A Shift+right-click then opens the object snap menu, and an idle Shift-click on a selected object removes it under default PICKADD.
- When the synthetic events no longer need those modifiers, it emits `ModifiersChanged` with the real (`raw.modifiers`) value again. Without this step, egui would keep the injected Shift and later real clicks would count as Shift-clicks. A physically held key is restored in the same way.

`ui.key` goes through the same hook, so its `cmd`/`shift`/`alt` also reach the live modifier state. `ui.drag` and `ui.pointer` do not change: `ui.drag` sends no modifiers, and `ui.pointer` already applies `shift` directly.

Test: `synthetic_shift_click_holds_shift_for_the_frame` sends a synthetic Shift-click through the hook. It checks that egui sees no Shift on the move frame, sees Shift on the press and release frames, and sees no Shift again on the next frame. On `main` the press assertion fails.

title: Page Setup: report unsupported layout plot areas as not available yet (#491)
author: MarekSpodBiedry
body:
Fixes #491.

Layout plotting always prints the whole sheet, but `pagesetup` accepted `extents`, `display`, `window` and `limits` as the plot area and reported them back as selected, so the plot silently ignored the choice.

- `pagesetup` now rejects a change to a non-`layout` plot area with "plot area `<v>` is not available yet; layouts plot the whole sheet (`layout`)", the same "not available yet" wording unfinished features use elsewhere. A value already stored on the layout (for example read from a DXF) can still be re-sent unchanged, so DXF round trips keep their setting.
- The Page Setup dialog's plot area combo offers only `layout`.
- Region plotting itself is not added, as the issue asks.

Test: `pagesetup_paper_table` checks each of the four areas is rejected with "not available yet" and that `Layout` (any case) is still accepted. It fails without the fix.

title: Plot: apply an explicit scale to non-fitted layout plots (#490)
author: MarekSpodBiedry
body:
Fixes #490.

With `fit:false`, a layout plot built its paper mapping with a fixed `s: 1.0` instead of the scale `plot_scale` had just computed, so `plot {"fit":false,"scale":0.5}` on a layout printed 1:1. The model-space branch and the curve-tolerance estimate already used the numeric scale; only the non-fitted layout mapping dropped it.

- `crates/io/src/pdf.rs`: the non-fitted layout `Map` now uses the computed `s`. With no `scale` given, `plot_scale` still returns 1.0, so default layouts stay 1:1; `fit:true` and model space are unchanged. The sheet size and origin are unchanged too. The module comment now mentions the scale.
- `crates/engine/src/cmd/exchange.rs`: Plot Preview (`preview`) had the same hard-coded `1.0` in its layout branch, so it showed 1:1 while the plot was scaled. It now uses the same `plot_scale` value, so the preview matches the PDF.

Tests:
- `crates/io/tests/plot_layout_scale.rs` follows the issue's restoration check. A 90-unit line on Layout1 of a metric drawing plots at 90, 45 and 180 mm for scales 1, 0.5 and 2, and at 90 mm when no options are given. Without the fix, all three scales give 90 mm.
- `preview_applies_an_explicit_layout_scale` (engine): the layout preview at `scale: 1` is identical to the default, and `scale: 0.5` gives a different image. Without the fix, the two images are identical.

title: Select: pick pattern hatches on their visible strokes (#489)
author: MarekSpodBiedry
body:
Fixes #489.

A pattern hatch (ANSI31 and the like) could only be picked on its boundary loops, because `hit_polylines` gave the hatch's boundary segments only. A click directly on a drawn pattern stroke missed the hatch, while a line with the same endpoints was picked.

`hit_polylines` now also adds the hatch's pattern strokes. It takes them from the renderer's display list (`cadcraft_render::build_entities`, with fills and text off), the same way the Dimension/Insert/MLeader branch already does. This gives the same clipped, island-aware strokes that the screen, SVG and plot draw. Dot patterns are included because their points come from the same list. SOLID, gradient and `solid` hatches do not change, because their interior is already a hit.

Point pick, the desktop idle click (same `pick_with`), and crossing and fence selection all use `hit_polylines`, so a stroke counts as a hit on each of these paths. Window selection (entirely inside) uses bounds, so it does not change.

Tests (`hatch_pattern_pick_tests`), from the issue's restoration check:
- ANSI31 square 0..10: `[5,5]` on the diagonal picks the hatch. The boundary `[5,0]` still picks it, and `[15,5]` outside does not.
- The same hatch with a 4..6 island: `[1,1]` on a visible stroke picks it, and `[5,5]` in the empty island stays empty.

The first assertion and the `[1,1]` assertion fail without the fix.

title: Include multileader text in its bounds so zoom, window selection and viewports keep the whole text (#488)
author: MarekSpodBiedry
body:
Fixes #488.

`entity_bounds` for an `MLeader` added only the leader points, the landing and the text insertion point. The text itself was left out, so for the issue's fixture (`mleader` from (0,0) to (25,0) with text "N", height 5) the bounds stopped at x 25.45 while the glyph reaches x 28.78. Everything that uses these bounds got it wrong: Zoom Extents and Zoom Object clipped the N, a non-crossing window that held the leader but not the N still selected the multileader, and a layout viewport showing only the N's right stroke skipped the entity and plotted nothing.

The MText arm's approximate box (attachment point, width or estimated width, line count, rotation) is moved unchanged into a small `mtext_box` helper, and the MLeader arm now adds that box for its text. The renderer draws multileader text through the same `mtext` path as a standalone MTEXT, so the same box applies. Blank text still adds nothing, like a blank standalone MTEXT (the existing `blank` check). Block-content multileaders are unchanged.

Test: `multileader_text_is_inside_its_bounds` builds the issue's multileader and checks the bounds reach past the N's right stroke and cover its height, and that a blank-text multileader does not grow. On main the bounds end at x 25.45 and the test fails.

title: AREA: refuse an open elliptical arc instead of measuring the whole ellipse (#487)
author: MarekSpodBiedry
body:
Fixes #487.

AREA's Object option measured any ELLIPSE entity from its major axis and ratio alone, ignoring the stored start/end span, so a quarter ellipse or a shorter elliptical arc reported the full ellipse's area and perimeter.

`object_area` now checks the span with `cadcraft_geom::Ellipse::is_full` (the same geometry type the other ellipse code paths build) and returns `object has no area` for an open elliptical arc. This matches what AREA already does for a circular ARC, as the issue suggests. A full ellipse is measured as before.

Both entry paths go through `object_area`, so both are covered:
- JSON `area {"handle": ...}` now fails with ``invalid parameters for `area`: object has no area``.
- Interactive `AREA` > Object prints "The selected object has no area." instead of the full-ellipse numbers.

The AREA row in `docs/geometry-parity.md` now says that an open elliptical arc has no area.

Test: `area_of_an_open_elliptical_arc_is_refused_and_a_full_ellipse_is_measured` in `crates/engine/tests/inquiry_keywords.rs` covers the quarter and 45° arcs through JSON, the full ellipse (area 8π), and interactive Object selection of the quarter arc. It fails on main.

title: fix(gpu): handle uncaptured wgpu errors and avoid unstable GL backend on Windows (fixes #602)
author: mahmagha
body:
Fixes #602

## Problem

When opening CADCraft on Windows and loading drawings, the application could panic fatally with:
```
ERROR [main] wgpu::backend::wgpu_core: Handling wgpu errors as fatal by default
thread 'main' panicked at wgpu-30.0.1\src\backend\wgpu_core.rs:3981:18:
wgpu error: Validation Error

Caused by:
  In Surface::configure
    Failed to wait for GPU to come idle before reconfiguring the Surface
```

Two compounding causes:
1. `cadcraft_ui_egui::gpu::install` did not register an uncaptured error handler on the `wgpu::Device`. By default, `wgpu` treats uncaptured errors (including surface timeout / device recovery errors) as fatal, causing the application to panic and losing unsaved user work.
2. PR #31 defaulted Windows to DirectX 12 to avoid AMD's `atio6axx.dll` crash, but still allowed `WGPU_BACKEND` to force `Backends::GL`. On Windows with Intel graphics (such as Intel UHD Graphics 620), the OpenGL ES/GL backend (`wgpu-hal::gles`) frequently times out during `Surface::configure` upon loading drawings or resizing windows (`GpuWaitTimeout`).

## Solution

1. In `crates/ui-egui/src/gpu.rs`: Register `rs.device.on_uncaptured_error` in `install()` to log `wgpu` errors rather than letting `wgpu` abort/panic the application.
2. In `apps/cadcraft/src/graphics.rs`: On Windows, filter out `Backends::GL`. If `backend_override` specifies only `GL` (e.g. `WGPU_BACKEND=gl` left in user environment), log a warning and fall back to `Backends::DX12`. If multiple backends were specified, strip `GL` so that DirectX 12 or Vulkan are used instead.
3. Added test `windows_gl_override_falls_back_to_dx12` in `apps/cadcraft/src/graphics.rs`.

title: ci: refactor workflows to use storytold/craft-common-actions
author: dylanmtaylor
body:
### Summary
Refactors repetitive CI/CD workflows across CADCraft to call centralized reusable workflows and composite actions hosted in the organization repository [`storytold/craft-common-actions`](https://github.com/storytold/craft-common-actions).

### Design Decisions
- **Hosted in Organization Repository**: Workflows live under `storytold/craft-common-actions` (no personal fork/repository).
- **Intentionally Tracks `@main` (Not SHA Pinned)**: Callers deliberately track `@main` with an inline explanation comment so that org-wide CI improvements, security fixes, and build optimizations propagate across all 13+ craftapps automatically without requiring individual PR churn in every repository.
- **Explicit Secrets**: Only the exact required signing secrets are passed explicitly (`secrets: inherit` is avoided).
- **Node 24 Runtimes**: All composite and third-party actions inside `storytold/craft-common-actions` are updated to Node 24 (and pinned internally to immutable commit SHAs), eliminating Node 20 deprecation warnings.
- **Strict Verification**: Build utilities like `nfpm`, `actionlint`, and `trunk` are verified against SHA256 checksums.
- Preserves 100% of existing packaging, release matrix, and linting semantics for CADCraft.

title: Windows: use FXC by default for DirectX 12 startup
author: PedroGuille
body:

Explicit `WGPU_BACKEND` and `WGPU_DX12_COMPILER` overrides remain supported.

title: docs: use present tense in the ArtCraft brand verb list
author: lunar-me
body:
# Summary

This PR fixes a grammar issue in `docs/brand/LICENSE-brand.txt` (line 25).

# Problem

The verb list is in the present tense ("sponsors, endorses, certifies or supports") but opens with the past tense "made", so the clause is ungrammatical and reads as if it describes something the team once did rather than what the marks must never suggest. The line above already uses the present tense: "the ArtCraft team makes it".

The problematic text:

```markdown
They must never suggest that the ArtCraft Team made, sponsors, endorses, certifies or supports
```

# Fix

Replaced with:

```markdown
They must never suggest that the ArtCraft Team makes, sponsors, endorses, certifies or supports
```

- [ ] Breaking change

title: Tool Sets: the gear on a category header opens that category's options
author: switch87
body:
Fixes #606.

## What was wrong

The gear was painted onto the category header with no interact rect of its own, so it was decoration on a row whose only target was the collapse toggle — clicking exactly where a gear promises settings collapsed the category instead.

## What it does now

The gear gets a target of its own (`ui.interact`, a 13 px square inside the 22 px header row, so the header still collapses everywhere else) and opens a per-category options menu, in the shape the Layers palette already uses for its own dropdown:

- one checkbox per tool of the category, so a user can take a tool out of the palette and put it back;
- **Show All** puts every tool of that category back at once.

The choice lives in `UiState::hidden_tools` (command ids, next to `collapsed_groups`), so it survives a restart and can be read and set from automation like the rest of the UI state. A hidden tool leaves the palette only — the command itself stays available from the command line, the menus, scripts and MCP.

The gear is described to assistive technology as "<category> options" and carries a hover text; the three new strings are in the Ukrainian catalog ("Show All" already existed and is reused).

## Tests

`crates/ui-egui/tests/toolsets_gear.rs` (egui_kittest, three tests):

- the gear opens the options and does not collapse the category, while clicking the header itself still collapses and expands it, and the gear's target is smaller than the header row;
- ticking a checkbox in the menu records the command id in the UI state;
- a hidden tool leaves the palette, the rest of the category stays, and **Show All** brings it back.

```text
cargo test -p cadcraft-ui-egui                                    green, all targets
cargo clippy -p cadcraft-ui-egui --all-targets -- -D warnings     clean
cargo fmt --check -p cadcraft-ui-egui                             clean
cargo xtask layers    16 crates, no layering violations
```
